title: Generic authenticated browser QA for read-only application journeys
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Generic authenticated browser QA for read-only application journeys

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `authenticated read-only browser QA` → 0 relevant hits.
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 recent target-file changes or matching open/merged PRs in the prework discovery window; searched all-state browser QA/read-only browser issues. #31992 addressed driver readiness, not authenticated journey verification; #30472 fixed package resolution.
- [x] File refs verified: all eight paths below exist on local `main`; lines cited below were read from that checkout.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — security boundary is specified below, but composing reusable selectors, session hooks, and safe failure behavior requires implementation judgment.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped — issue-only worker handoff avoids anchoring a security-sensitive API to a speculative design.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-25
- **Created by:** ai-interactive, at the user's request for a reusable aidevops capability.
- **Conversation context:** A normal application change needed a one-off authenticated, read-only browser journey to verify the rendered page, responsive controls, and media-dialog selection. Existing generic smoke/screenshot checks cannot express that journey without a project-specific runner.

## What

Add an **opt-in, reusable authenticated browser journey** to aidevops QA. A caller supplies a named environment, an exact allowed application origin, a credential source resolved through existing secret-safe mechanisms, a bounded login/logout lifecycle, and a declarative sequence of read-only navigation/interaction/assertion steps. Support project-defined selectors and assertions rather than a hard-coded site, award ID, login page, or video count. Return small, redacted pass/fail evidence at desktop and mobile widths. Keep existing unauthenticated milestone smoke, screenshots, accessibility, and links commands unchanged by default.

## Why

Checking HTTP status, page titles, or unauthenticated screenshots does not prove that a logged-in user can see a particular page or that a control opens the intended content. Recreating one-off Playwright runners per project increases maintenance and risks credential leakage, unintended writes, and mismatched environments.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`.

**Tier rationale:** The permitted trust boundary, no-write default, and acceptance tests are explicit; implementation still needs bounded decisions about a declarative journey schema and how to reuse the existing runner. Do not weaken the boundary to make unusual sign-in flows pass.

## Implementation

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh:1-42` — extend the existing CLI without changing old commands' behavior.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh` and `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-tests.sh` — reuse viewport/runtime/diagnostics machinery; extract focused new functions/modules rather than growing large existing functions.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh` — cover happy and fail-closed paths using local fake pages/fixtures, without production credentials.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/browser/browser-qa.md:19-48` — document optional journey input, limitations, and a generic example without a real hostname or credential.
- `EDIT: .agents/workflows/ui-verification.md:36-51` — show when to prefer a repository's existing E2E runner versus the new generic journey.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/workflows/milestone-validation.md:101-105` and `.agents/workflows/ui-verification.md:36-51` call existing browser QA; `.agents/tools/browser/browser-qa.md:19-48` documents it. Existing CLI consumers must remain compatible.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh` orchestrates Playwright; its core/tests sub-libraries create transient scripts/reports. New journey must reject app writes at the network boundary (not only `/api/`), except *explicit exact-origin sign-in/sign-out allowlisted endpoints and methods*; any other requested write needs a separate, authorized workflow rather than a silent broad switch.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh` is the focused existing helper suite; `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` covers modified shell/docs. Add the smallest local fixtures inside that suite for origin, method, cleanup, and diagnostics.
- **Schemas/config:** No existing generic journey schema was found in `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh` or its documentation; define a versioned, validated, bounded opt-in input and document examples using placeholders. Avoid arbitrary project code execution from untrusted YAML/JSON.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** Aidevops copies `.agents/scripts/` into the user's installed framework via its normal setup/deploy process. Do not edit the installed copy. Report files are transient and redacted; do not commit or upload cookies, tokens, storage state, raw body dumps, unfiltered traces, or authenticated screenshots.
- **Migrations/backfills:** None; additive opt-in CLI with the existing subcommands remaining the default, verified against `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh:4-12`.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** The new `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-journey.mjs` must always sign out after successful login and close the isolated context/browser on success, failure, or timeout. If cleanup cannot be confirmed, fail visibly without printing sensitive state. Revert the additive subcommand/config to return to old behavior.

### Implementation Steps

1. Verify existing CLI/runtime and select the smallest additive journey input/runner shape; use `.agents/scripts/playwright-runtime.mjs` for package resolution, and `.agents/scripts/site-context-helper.sh` for readiness when a hostname has an inventory entry. An inventory entry establishes context, **not** authentication or write authority.
2. Validate the named environment and exact origin before any navigation; reject a mismatched baseURL, off-origin redirects, unexpected third-party requests carrying credentials, and non-allowlisted state-changing requests. Admit only explicit sign-in/sign-out endpoint+method exceptions for the authentication lifecycle; do not log credential values or URLs with query tokens. Keep separate app writes blocked for the entire run.
3. Run isolated, short-lived browser contexts. Support bounded declarative navigation, button clicks, visibility/count/text/attribute assertions and horizontal-overflow checks with project-owned selectors, desktop/mobile viewports and finite timeouts; expose a safe extension point for repo-owned E2E checks if the declarative subset is insufficient rather than embedding executable arbitrary JS in config.
4. Ensure redacted diagnostics give step, allowed-origin route pattern, viewport, assertion status, console/pageerror count and blocked-write count. Default to no screenshots, traces, recordings, or storage-state exports for authenticated runs. If a screenshot is explicitly authorized in a separate safe path, apply the existing viewport and max-dimension rules in `.agents/reference/screenshot-limits.md` and protect private content.
5. Verify positive and negative cases through the existing helper test suite, then exercise one disposable local site/journey. Document the preference for existing repo E2E runners when they already cover the authenticated path. Make a WIP checkpoint after focused verification, before any broader gate.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Each run owns its browser context and finite temporary files; parallel environments must never share cookies or storage state. No application transaction or durable app write is in scope.
- **Migration/rollback:** Additive opt-in only; removing it restores old commands. No data migration, account setup, or browser-profile rewrite.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Existing `smoke|run|screenshot|links|a11y` behavior and positional options continue to work. Unknown journey schema versions must fail before authentication, rather than guessing.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Repeat read-only assertions only; authentication and sign-out follow the provider's explicit flow. Do not auto-repeat unknown writes or ambiguous login failures.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Denied navigation/write, timeout, auth challenge or sign-out failure stops that run, closes its context and emits only sanitized facts. Preserve original acceptance criteria for a safer retry, never downgrade to a personal browser session or bypass MFA.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** Existing helper suite proves CLI compatibility, a disposable login→assert→logout path, wrong-origin rejection, blocked app POST outside `/api/`, optional-prompt/timeout cleanup, cross-run isolation, and no credential-bearing artifacts. Changed-file lint covers edited scripts/docs. Local smoke of the new CLI against a disposable target proves production entry path, not just generated script text.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Only if implementation touches shared browser transport or common secret-injection infrastructure; otherwise no full-repository gate.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Run focused helper tests and a disposable local authenticated journey.
- [ ] Commit a WIP checkpoint before any broad gates if the implementation touches four or more files.
- [ ] Broaden only for evidenced shared-runtime changes.

### Safety-Stop Recovery

- **Original objective:** Generic authenticated read-only browser QA for arbitrary developer workflows.
- **Preserved directions:** Adapt to targets and changing UI; no site-specific hard-coding or secret-bearing artifacts.
- **Trigger and evidence:** not triggered; on safety or resource stop, record exact gate and non-sensitive evidence.
- **Completed and verified:** none yet; issue is an implementation handoff.
- **Remaining acceptance criteria:** all below.
- **Unsafe route not to repeat:** any route that bypasses auth or permits unrestricted writes to pass verification.
- **Next safe route:** smaller isolated site fixture, focused wrapper tests, and stop on absent credentials/authority.
- **Resume condition:** origin, credential source, and scoped sign-in/out authority are verified.
- **Owner and status:** worker after dispatch; not-triggered.

### Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** No site-specific target names/IDs, production credentials, write-allow switch, personal browser profiles, public screenshots of authenticated content, or new app deployment.

**AI brief owner:** interactive aidevops session; implementation worker owns the issue after dispatch.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-tests.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-qa.md`
- `.agents/workflows/ui-verification.md`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-journey.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-journey-config.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-journey-guard.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-journey-steps.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-journey.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An opt-in journey verifies a named exact-origin authenticated page with project-supplied selectors at desktop and mobile, returning a compact per-step pass/fail report and ensuring logout/context closure; existing unauthenticated CLI behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] Clicking a project-defined read-only control can assert an intended modal title, selected media URL, or other visible state; no target hostname, fixture identifier, video count, or login copy is baked into aidevops code.
- [ ] Wrong-origin navigation, non-allowlisted POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE (including non-`/api/` paths), unapproved auth redirect, missing credential, unknown schema version, and timeout fail closed without an app write or secret-bearing artifact.
- [ ] Authentication exceptions are exact-origin, exact-path and method scoped; no stored cookies, raw credentials, HTML dumps, default trace/recording, or authenticated screenshot appears in report files or logs, even on failure.
- [ ] Tests cover two different disposable journey definitions/environments, proving reuse and isolation; docs direct projects with suitable existing E2E to keep using those tests.

## Context & Decisions

- The current helper runs public/unauthenticated checks and writes its screenshots/reports beneath the agent workspace. Its documentation and caller paths were read locally; the separate Playwright-driver readiness issue #31992 has already shipped and does not solve authenticated journeys.
- Implementation should prefer a bounded general primitive, not a new always-on login gate or a single project's custom test transplanted into aidevops.

title: Evaluate Stagehand v4 as a bounded augmentation or replacement for legacy Playwriter
body:
## Description

Aidevops already documents Stagehand as the natural-language and self-healing browser option, but the integration and benchmarks are oriented around the v3 architecture. Stagehand v4 is now the npm `latest` line (`4.1.0`) and materially changes the integration surface: its engine runs inside the browser, clients communicate over typed bidirectional JSON-RPC, TypeScript/Python/Go SDKs share one protocol, AI primitives are separated from deterministic page controls, and metrics/diagnostics are built in.

At the same time, aidevops policy marks Playwriter as legacy explicit-only compatibility, while the OpenCode MCP activation registry exposes Playwright and Playwriter but no bounded Stagehand route. This creates a gap between the documented tool-selection policy and the runtime capabilities available to agents.

Evaluate Stagehand v4 as an augmentation to Playwright and, where its authenticated-browser and consent model is sufficient, a replacement for legacy Playwriter. This should be a version-aware architecture decision rather than a blanket tool substitution.

## Expected Behavior

Aidevops should have an evidence-backed browser automation policy and runtime path that:

- Keeps standalone Playwright as the fast, deterministic default for isolated automation.
- Selects Stagehand v4 for unknown/changing page structures, typed extraction, replayable adaptive actions, and workflows that benefit from model-assisted browser understanding.
- Uses Playwriter only for explicit legacy compatibility until Stagehand v4 proves equivalent authenticated existing-tab access with the required consent and profile boundaries.
- Makes Stagehand available through a bounded, discoverable execution path in OpenCode without globally loading unnecessary tools or schemas.
- Documents version support, cost, latency, reliability, security boundaries, and migration requirements.

## Current Evidence

- `.agents/tools/browser/stagehand.md:26-42` documents the existing setup, v3-style environment/configuration, primitives, and old performance figures.
- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-automation.md:30-43` routes unknown structure and self-healing work to Stagehand.
- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-automation.md:74-94` contains benchmarks dated 2026-01-24 and a Stagehand feature comparison that predates v4.
- `.agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md:26-41` defines Playwriter as legacy explicit-only compatibility and recommends Stagehand for natural-language/self-healing selectors.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs:201-208,356-365` registers bounded activation for Playwriter and Playwright; no Stagehand activation is registered.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/agent-mcp-tools.mjs:20-21` exposes Playwright and Playwriter tool patterns only.
- `npm view @browserbasehq/stagehand version dist-tags --json` reports `4.1.0` as `latest`, `3.7.3` as `v3-latest`, and a `4.2.0-alpha` line.
- Upstream Stagehand PR browserbase/stagehand#2671 describes v4 as a protocol-first monorepo with TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs over a shared core.

## Proposed Approach

1. Review Stagehand v4's local-browser, browser-extension, Browserbase, SDK, and runtime ownership models against aidevops' browser trust boundaries.
2. Build a capability matrix for:
   - isolated deterministic automation with Playwright;
   - adaptive/unknown-page automation with Stagehand v4;
   - explicitly approved existing authenticated tabs currently served by Playwriter.
3. Verify whether Stagehand v4 can satisfy selected-tab consent, existing cookies/session access, extension/profile isolation, cleanup, and headless-worker requirements. Do not claim Playwriter replacement until these are proven.
4. Decide the lowest-context runtime integration: bounded activation agent, helper-driven SDK invocation, CLI route, or another architecture consistent with lazy MCP/tool loading.

title: Require explicit target-repository validation for cross-repo child tasks
body:
## Description

Add a deterministic target-repository contract for cross-repository child-task creation. A planning session can currently compose work for one registered project while `claim-task-id.sh` or `issue-sync-helper.sh` creates the task in the current coordination repository when the caller supplies the wrong `--repo-path`, `--project-root`, or `--repo` value.

This occurred in a live interactive workflow: a portfolio repository owned the parent tracker, while four implementation children belonged to another registered repository. The briefs described the external site and its write surface, but issue creation accepted the coordination repository without a mismatch warning or block. The children then required recreation with repository-local task IDs, planning records, labels, and dependencies.

The primary cause was agent routing error; this enhancement is a defence-in-depth guardrail rather than a claim that the helpers selected the wrong repository autonomously.

## Expected Behavior

Brief schema v2 should support a machine-readable target repository, for example:

```markdown
- **Target repository:** `owner/repository`
- **Parent:** `other-owner/coordination-repository#123`
```

When target metadata is present, issue and task-ID creation should compare it with:

- the slug resolved from `--repo-path` or `--project-root`;
- an explicit `--repo` argument; and
- the repository selected for task-ID allocation.

A mismatch should fail before advancing a counter, writing `TODO.md`, or creating an issue. Same-repository tasks without target metadata should retain current behavior. Cross-repository parent references must remain valid and must not force children into the parent's repository.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Work in a registered coordination repository containing a parent issue.
2. Compose a child brief whose files and implementation belong to a second registered repository.
3. Invoke `claim-task-id.sh` or `issue-sync-helper.sh` with the coordination repository as the target.
4. Observe that the task ID, TODO entry, and issue can be created there without a target-repository mismatch gate.

## Proposed Implementation Contract

- Add canonical target-repository metadata to brief schema v2 and cross-repository task documentation.
- Validate the declared target against the resolved Git remote before any counter or GitHub write.
- Fail closed only when explicit metadata conflicts; do not infer repository ownership from prose, URLs, or filenames.
- Preserve the existing explicit `--repo-path` and `--repo` interfaces for correctly routed tasks.
- Include the target slug in dry-run and publication receipts for auditability.
- Add tests covering correct same-repo creation, correct cross-repo child creation, explicit mismatch rejection, absent metadata compatibility, and parent references in a different repository.

## Candidate Files

- `.agents/scripts/brief-readiness-helper.sh` — validate canonical target metadata
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` and its extracted issue/counter helpers — compare allocation target before mutation
- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` and relationship helpers — compare issue transport target before creation
- `.agents/reference/task-lifecycle.md` — document the cross-repository contract
- Existing claim-task, issue-sync, and brief-readiness test suites — add mismatch and compatibility coverage

## Verification

Run the focused claim-task, issue-sync, brief-readiness, and cross-repository relationship tests. Add an integration test proving that a child can reference a parent in another repository while its task ID, TODO entry, and issue are created only in the declared target repository.

## Environment

- **aidevops version:** 3.34.30
- **Latest version:** 3.34.30
- **Install method:** Homebrew
- **AI assistant:** OpenCode
- **OS:** macOS 26.6.2
- **Shell:** bash 5.3.20
- **gh CLI:** 2.101.0

## Additional Context

The target repository was already registered with aidevops, so this was not caused by missing repository discovery data. The safe workaround was to allocate fresh repository-local task IDs, create the child issues in the correct repository, link them to the coordination parent, close the misplaced issues, and repair both planning ledgers.

title: OpenCode: plain-text @playwriter can connect MCP without routing to scoped agent
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `OpenCode agent routing @playwriter session routed to seo MCP tools scoped dedicated agent` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 recent target-file commits / 1 related merged PR (#31344) / 0 matching open PRs — prior fix verified and current edge case still reproduced
- [x] File refs verified: 5 refs checked, all present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — bounded routing guard and documentation change inside the existing scoped-permission boundary
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — issue-only handoff is sufficient and the exact implementation choice needs worker validation

## Description

In OpenCode, a user can submit a prompt beginning with the literal text `@playwriter` from a non-Playwriter parent session and reasonably believe the documented Playwriter route was selected. When OpenCode stores that token as an ordinary text part rather than a structured `agent` part, aidevops still allows the parent agent to connect the Playwriter MCP. The connection succeeds, but the parent cannot receive `playwriter_*` tools or launch the dedicated Playwriter agent, so the requested browser operation stops after a misleading partial activation.

The local configuration is coherent and the scoped Playwriter profile works when OpenCode creates a structured agent mention. This is therefore a routing/guardrail gap rather than a broken Playwriter installation.

## Why

The current partial activation wastes a user-approved browser operation and can mislead both the user and parent agent into retrying through contexts that cannot receive the scoped tools. A truthful fail-closed route is especially important for authenticated or transactional browser work.

## Expected Behavior

The Playwriter route should fail closed before MCP activation when the current context is not the dedicated Playwriter agent, with actionable guidance that the user must select `@playwriter` from OpenCode autocomplete so the prompt contains a structured agent mention. Alternatively, a supported parent route should delegate directly to the registered Playwriter profile without widening `playwriter_*` permissions.

Documentation should distinguish a structured OpenCode agent mention from literal prompt text.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```text
@playwriter

Use my existing authenticated browser tab for a bounded browser transaction.
```

Submit the text from an existing SEO parent session without a structured agent-mention part.

**Actual output**:

```text
Connected MCP playwriter. Lifecycle readiness does not grant its tools to the current agent; continue in the dedicated playwriter agent, where its tool permissions are scoped.
```

The parent then attempted a general subagent, which reported that Playwriter browser tools were unavailable. No browser action occurred.

OpenCode database evidence for the failing user message:

```text
session.agent = SEO
message.data.agent = SEO
part.data.type = text
part.data.name = null
```

Control evidence from an earlier successful invocation in the same parent session:

```text
part.data.type = agent
part.data.name = playwriter
part.data.source.value = @playwriter
child session.agent = playwriter
```

**Expected output**:

Either create the dedicated Playwriter child session, or refuse activation before connecting and explain how to create a structured `@playwriter` mention.

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: OpenCode user-message handling followed by the generated Playwriter activation profile in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-agent-profiles.mjs:111-153`.
- **Call chain**: plain-text user part remains in the SEO parent; the parent calls `aidevops_mcp`; `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-activation-tool.mjs:261-285` connects the MCP and reports that tools remain scoped to the dedicated agent.
- **Integrated verification**: live OpenCode session evidence above; focused unit coverage currently verifies scoped profile creation and the post-connect message, but not the plain-text mention path.

**Causal code**:

```text
`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-activation-tool.mjs:283-285` was introduced by merge commit 5c702adebe65f7e8516dd806af74561b1b5575e0 for #31278.
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start or continue a non-Playwriter OpenCode parent session, such as SEO.
2. Enter or paste literal `@playwriter` text without selecting the Playwriter autocomplete item, followed by a browser task.
3. Observe that OpenCode stores only a text part and keeps the parent agent as SEO.
4. Let the parent call `aidevops_mcp` for Playwriter.
5. Observe a successful MCP connection but no `playwriter_*` tools and no supported route into the dedicated Playwriter agent.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually connected the registry-approved Playwriter MCP from the SEO parent; this exposed the scoping warning but could not complete the task.
- Tried a general subagent; it had no Playwriter browser-tool permission.
- Inspected OpenCode session records to distinguish a plain text part from a structured `agent` part.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-activation-tool.mjs:261-285` — fail closed or return actionable route guidance when activation occurs outside the dedicated agent.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-agent-profiles.mjs:111-153` — preserve scoped activation profiles and expose any agent identity needed by the selected guard design.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs` — cover plain-text non-agent invocation and structured-agent success.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md:26-32,66-94` — distinguish autocomplete-selected agent mentions from literal text.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/context/mcp-discovery.md:126-164` — keep on-demand MCP discovery guidance consistent.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tools.mjs:234` creates `aidevops_mcp`; `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-agent-profiles.mjs:165-185` registers dedicated activation agents; `.agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md` and `.agents/tools/context/mcp-discovery.md` tell users and agents how to invoke them.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-activation-tool.mjs:245-285` mutates MCP lifecycle state through connect/disconnect; `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-agent-profiles.mjs:137-153` mutates runtime agent tool and permission profiles.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs:35-96,511-526` verifies scoped profile registration and the current post-connect diagnostic; live OpenCode session records provide the missing text-part versus agent-part reproducer.
- **Schemas/config:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs:200-215` declares Playwriter's `activationAgent`, `toolPattern`, and disabled global scope; generated `opencode.json` keeps `playwriter_*` false globally.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/` is deployed into the active aidevops runtime bundle by setup; generated user config is an output and must not be hand-edited for this fix.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the reproduced state is runtime message-part classification and MCP profile behavior, with no persisted aidevops data format change.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-activation-tool.mjs:256-259` owns disconnect cleanup; rollback is reverting the guard/guidance change while retaining the existing #31278 scoped-agent behavior.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add a fail-closed guard or supported delegation path for MCP activation requests made outside each MCP's dedicated activation agent.
2. Make the diagnostic explicitly identify the active agent and explain that literal `@playwriter` text is not a structured agent mention.
3. Update `.agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md` and relevant OpenCode invocation guidance to require selecting the autocomplete item.
4. Add a regression test covering plain-text `@playwriter` in a non-Playwriter parent, while preserving the existing scoped-agent success path.
5. Consider the same bounded behavior for other on-demand MCP activation agents rather than implementing a Playwriter-only exception.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** MCP lifecycle state may be shared across sessions; a refused wrong-agent call must not disconnect or alter an MCP already used by a valid scoped agent.
- **Migration/rollback:** no migration is needed; reverting the change must restore the current diagnostic without weakening global tool denial.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** preserve existing OpenCode runtimes that do not expose current-agent identity by returning truthful guidance rather than assuming delegation succeeded.
- **Idempotency/retry:** repeated wrong-agent activation attempts must remain side-effect free; repeated valid connect/disconnect calls retain existing bounded lifecycle behavior.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** existing one-reset connection recovery remains unchanged; if agent identity cannot be verified, fail closed before browser work and explain the structured mention route.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the focused Node test covers profile registration, lifecycle messaging, wrong-agent behavior, retries, and tool scoping; changed-file lint covers plugin and Markdown edits. An interactive OpenCode check proves the text-part versus structured-agent route.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required unless implementation changes shared agent routing beyond on-demand MCP profiles.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-activation-tool.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-agent-profiles.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs`
- `.agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md`
- `.agents/tools/context/mcp-discovery.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A plain-text `@playwriter` request from a non-Playwriter agent cannot appear ready for browser work after MCP connection.
- [ ] The user receives actionable guidance to select the structured Playwriter agent mention or use a supported delegated route.
- [ ] A genuine structured `@playwriter` mention still creates a Playwriter child with `aidevops_mcp` and `playwriter_*` permissions.
- [ ] Playwriter tools remain disabled globally and unavailable to unrelated agents.
- [ ] A wrong-agent or plain-text invocation must not connect Playwriter, widen tool permissions, or alter a valid scoped agent's lifecycle state.
- [ ] Focused plugin tests cover both the plain-text failure path and structured-agent success path.
- [ ] Browser invocation documentation explains the OpenCode autocomplete requirement.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.34.31
- **Latest version**: 3.34.31
- **Install method**: Homebrew
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: macOS 26.6.2
- **Shell**: bash 5.3.20
- **gh CLI**: 2.101.0

## Additional Context

Issue #31278 fixed the earlier defect where Playwriter connected but tools were unavailable by routing Playwriter through a scoped agent. The current behavior is a different edge case: the scoped route is healthy, but literal mention text can leave the task in the wrong parent while still allowing lifecycle activation.

## Problem

Required Qlty Regression Gate fails on unrelated PRs because Qlty action/install v2.3.0 resolves moving latest CLI 0.645.0 while validators and workflow QLTY_VERSION remain pinned to 0.643.0. PR #32383 has a terminal failed Qlty Smell Regression job with this exact version mismatch; Qlty Smell Threshold also fails for the same reason. title: bug: issue workers still miss image references after #32019
body: ## Description An OpenCode issue-work session in aidevops 3.34.33 could read the issue text but could not view the PNG referenced by its GitHub `user-attachments` `` tag. The attachment request returned HTTP 404 (`text/plain`). The agent nevertheless made an image-dependent design proposal and uploaded an isolated preview without having seen the reference. The user had to attach the same image directly to the conversation and request a revision. Related: #32019 was closed by #32037, which hardened target selection and attachment **classification in the review path**. This report captures a later, distinct **issue-execution handoff** failure: when the image is unavailable to the agent, it should not proceed with image-dependent work as though the reference had been reviewed. Whether the attachment is genuinely unavailable from GitHub, blocked by session authentication, or omitted from prompt transport remains unconfirmed. This report is not a claim that #32037 caused the 404. ## Expected Behavior When an issue requires a visual reference, the issue-processing session should either receive a usable image through an authorized attachment path or explicitly mark the visual dependency blocked and request a direct upload before implementing it. A failed fetch must not silently degrade into a speculative visual implementation. Preserve the issue's repository and object identity; do not leak private image contents to public reports. ## Reproducer **Symptom command** (the private attachment URL is withheld from this public report; command shape and arguments other than the URL match the observing session): ```bash curl -sSL --max-time 15 --output /dev/null --write-out 'status=%{http_code} type=%{content_type}\n' "$ATTACHMENT_URL" ``` **Actual output** on 2026-09-25, after the merge closing #32019: ```text status=404 type=text/plain; charset=utf-8 ``` The issue body was available through `gh issue view` and contained an `` pointing to the attachment. The image was not visible to the agent through that link; the direct user-uploaded PNG was readable and resolved the visual ambiguity. The first preview visibly diverged from the intended reference. The observing session then rebuilt the preview using the directly supplied image. **Expected output**: a usable image attachment in the issue handoff, or a clear access-blocked status before visual design work proceeds. **Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation. The response only establishes a 404 in this session, not whether the cause is a GitHub object/access state, issue ingestion, or the runtime's attachment handling. **Owning-path proof**: not established. #32037 changed `.agents/scripts/review-evidence-helper.sh` and `.agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md` for review flows, but the issue-execution attachment ingress and any linked prompt-transport code must be identified by the investigator; do not assume review code owns this incident. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Start an OpenCode aidevops issue-execution session on an issue whose required visual mockup is an inline GitHub `user-attachments` image. 2. title: Feature: add a repository-only pre-commit hook repair command
body:
### Problem

Repairing a missing repository pre-commit quality hook currently requires the broad `install-hooks-helper.sh install` command. That command also manages pre-push and user-level settings/hooks. There is no public command for repairing only the missing pre-commit dispatcher while preserving those unrelated settings.

This is particularly useful for linked worktrees, whose hook belongs to the common Git directory rather than the worktree's `.git` file.

### Proposed Solution

Add an opt-in `install-pre-commit` command to `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh`, leaving the default full-install behavior unchanged:

- Install only a missing pre-commit dispatcher in the current repository's common Git hooks directory.
- Leave existing managed hooks unchanged; refuse to replace custom hooks, symlinks, or a configured `core.hooksPath`.
- Require the repository-local or deployed validator that the dispatcher will actually execute, with both validator preflight and a runtime check before installation.
- Refuse force/unknown options and avoid overwriting a concurrently created hook.
- Preserve pre-push and user-level settings/hooks byte-for-byte.

Reuse the existing dispatcher rather than adding another hook implementation. Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-install-hooks-validator-preflight.sh` with isolated-home, disposable-repository cases for ordinary and linked worktrees, refusal paths, idempotence, and unchanged unrelated files.

A local implementation is ready for a linked PR. The focused suite currently passes 26 tests, and changed-file lint, ShellCheck, Bash syntax checks, and `git diff --check` pass. Verification commands:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-install-hooks-validator-preflight.sh
bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

### Alternatives Considered

- Rerunning full installation: unnecessarily broad for a single missing repository hook.
- Manually writing `.git/hooks/pre-commit`: duplicates framework logic and lacks a supported preflighted entrypoint.

### Third-party Tool Integration

None. No dependencies, integrations, default configuration changes, or global installation are proposed.

### aidevops Version

3.34.33 (source base `8f160c091ffec5989923b63e993ac78134761a94`), tested on macOS.

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

title: Affinity execute_script per-call approval is not enforced under the default opencode --auto launcher
body:
## Observed

In the #32406 acceptance run (fresh OpenCode process on v3.36.0), the `affinity` agent called `affinity-studio_execute_script` and it ran immediately. No approval prompt appeared, so the operator could not deny the call. The script passed its document-path guard and ran inside Affinity. It only stopped because of an unrelated import bug, before it made any change. The file hashes were unchanged afterwards.

## Root cause

- `.agents/scripts/runtime-launcher.py:22` starts interactive OpenCode with `--auto`. The observed process was `opencode --auto --agent Build+`.
- OpenCode describes `--auto` as: "auto-approve permissions that are not explicitly denied (dangerous!)".
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/on-demand-mcp-tool-policy.mjs:16` enforced the "per-call approval" for `approvalRequiredTools` only as an OpenCode `ask` rule. Under `--auto`, that rule is approved without a prompt, so the documented approval step did not apply in launcher sessions.
- `tests/test-affinity-mcp-registry.mjs` checked that the config says `ask`, not what happens at run time.

## Decision (operator)

Remove the approval friction and let the Affinity agent do everything the user asks. Affinity's own **Settings > Model Context Protocol** toggles (Desktop files, network, saved scripts, hints, Canva AI) are the capability authority.

## Change

- `mcp-registry.mjs`: Affinity loses its `allowedTools` / `approvalRequiredTools` entries, so the `affinity` agent gets the full `affinity-studio_*` toolset with plain allow. The connection is still off by default, is connected only by the `affinity` agent, and stays invisible to other agents. The activation guidance is updated to match.
- `tools/design/affinity.md` and `configs/capability-registry.json`: now describe the in-app toggles as the permission authority and drop the claim of per-call approval. Also recorded: `AddChildNodesCommandBuilder` lives in `/commands.js`.
- Tests: `test-affinity-mcp-registry.mjs` and `test-creative-profiles.mjs` now assert a wildcard allow with no `ask` for the affinity agent, while other agents still get no Affinity tools.

## Verification

`node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-affinity-mcp-registry.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-creative-profiles.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs` → 35/35 pass. `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` → exit 0.

Ref #32406 (acceptance continues there; that issue stays open).

title: Flaky PEM scrub performance-budget test under full-suite load
body:
## What

Make the PEM performance-budget test in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-credential-scrub.mjs:197-205` robust under full-suite load, without weakening its ReDoS protection.

## Why

- It failed during `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` validators (`npm run test` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`) with "PEM scan averaged 8.621ms per 10KB" against a 5ms budget.
- It passed in isolation straight afterwards: 228ms total for 100 runs, about 2.3ms per run.
- The same flake occurred during the #32427 work.
- The budget is a wall-clock average, so it is sensitive to CPU contention from parallel test files. A catastrophic-backtracking regression would be orders of magnitude slower, not 1.7x.

## Reproducer

1. `cd .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops && npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run test`. It fails intermittently at `test-credential-scrub.mjs:204` with `PEM scan averaged 8.621ms per 10KB` (observed 2026-09-27 on macOS, alongside other load).
2. `node --test tests/test-credential-scrub.mjs` passes (25/25; the PEM test took 228ms for 100 runs).

## How

- EDIT `test-credential-scrub.mjs:197-205`, and apply the same pattern to the named-field budget test at about lines 170-181. Pick one of:
  1. Use the **minimum** of several timed batches (for example 5 batches of 20 runs) instead of one average. The minimum filters out contention noise.
  2. Compare against a linear-scaling reference: time 10KB and 40KB inputs and assert the ratio stays below about 8, which catches super-linear backtracking regardless of machine speed.
- Keep an absolute ceiling generous enough to catch real regressions, for example 50ms per 10KB.

## Acceptance

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-credential-scrub.mjs` passes.
- `npm run test` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops` passes 5 consecutive times.
- Temporarily swapping in a known backtracking regex such as `/(-+)+X/` still fails the test (a local check only, not committed).

On docs-only PR #32440, the non-required `Qlty Smell Threshold` job failed twice on the same synthetic merge commit/tree (5814a32f / 7fa4593c): 78 normalized smells against threshold 77, after reporting divergent scan identities and a third consensus attempt. The PR changed only `.agents/tools/browser/browser-benchmark.md`; its required changed-file Qlty Regression Gate passed. A nearby successful `main` job (run 36279710807, commit 5de05f40) reported 74 against 77. Do not assume the Markdown change introduced four source-code smells, and do not increase the ratchet to hide an actual regression.

## Reproducer

Inspect PR #32440 Code Quality Analysis run 36279867137 and rerun its failed jobs: the original threshold job 108509532066 and the rerun 108512321776 both report the same 78/77 failure for scan tree 7fa4593c. Compare `main` run 36279710807 job 108509092068, which reports 74/77. The synthetic merge commit 5814a32f has parent 5de05f40, and the GitHub commit-file list contains only `.agents/tools/browser/browser-benchmark.md`. The threshold job reports divergent scan identities before selecting 78; investigate why the same code files appear to score differently.

## Implementation scope

- Compare the exact normalized SARIF identities from `main` and the docs-only PR synthetic merge under the same pinned Qlty 0.643.0 and isolated-clone settings. Determine whether scans vary on identical code, the merge tree contains unexpected scanned files, or the counting helper changes the inputs.
- Inspect `.agents/scripts/qlty-smell-threshold-helper.sh` and `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`; fix the evidenced cause at the narrowest layer. Preserve real repository-wide regressions as failures.
- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-qlty-smell-threshold-helper.sh` to cover the identified case. Do not adjust `.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf` to absorb nondeterministic debt.

## Verification

- Reproduce the 74-vs-78 result or prove the cause with matching input tree/SARIF identity evidence, then run the focused threshold helper tests and ShellCheck for changed shell scripts.
- Confirm a docs-only PR and its base produce the same normalized code-smell identities under pinned inputs, while a genuinely added smell still fails the threshold. Check the real `Qlty Smell Threshold` job and required Qlty Regression Gate on a PR.

Independent follow-up to #32440; the Stagehand documentation PR was merged through its green required gates and is not a source-code smell fix.

title: fix(opencode-plugin): Anthropic OAuth cache stability (cch collision, lost cache marker) and first-prompt context reduction for OpenCode 1 and 2
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `opencode v2 system transform anthropic oauth provider-auth release full-loop` → 0 hits — no prior lesson; a new cch-collision lesson was stored this session
- [x] Discovery pass: 2 commits (`bb8da3537` GH#32415 Opus OAuth repair, `42cdfdfe2` GH#32072) / 0 merged PRs / 0 open PRs touch target files in last 48h
- [x] File refs verified: 14 refs checked, all present at HEAD `6c71f6f02`
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — trust/compliance-sensitive Anthropic OAuth wire shape across two runtime majors
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — interactive session implements directly

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-27
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (with maintainer)
- **Conversation context:** First-turn context grew from ~17.7K to ~30K tokens; investigation also found an Anthropic OAuth cache-buster and a lost cache marker. Maintainer requested full-loop through release and deploy, with OpenCode 1 (1.18.x) and OpenCode 2 (2.0.x) compatibility and a logged rollback method.

## What

Ship one PR (or a tight pair) that:

- **A1 — cch placeholder collision (cache-buster):** `finalizeBillingHeaderHash` in `provider-auth-body.mjs` substitutes the body hash with a first-match `String.replace`. `serializeWithKeyOrder` emits `messages` before `system`, so once the billing placeholder text appears anywhere in conversation history (tool result, doc read, compaction summary) the history copy receives the per-request hash (bytes change every request → prompt-cache miss) and the real billing header ships unsigned. Fix: substitute only at the header position (per-request sentinel → hash body with placeholder at that position → replace sentinel).
- **A2 — lost `cache_control`:** `redistributeSystemToMessages` drops `cache_control` from redistributed system blocks (probe: 3 markers in, 2 out). Carry the marker onto the joined redistributed block, keeping ≤4 breakpoints.
- **A3 — attributable redistribution log line:** add kept count, short sha of overflow text, and session to the `provider-auth: redistributed N system blocks` log line.
- **B1 — TTSR system transform works on OpenCode 1:** `ttsrSystemTransform` reassigns `output.system`, which OC1 discards. Mutate in place; drop the Anthropic identity unshift (avoids a new kept system block → untested wire shape); keep greeting OFF (matches effective behaviour today; AGENTS.md fallback greets); keep Quality Rules; move OpenAI intent tracing to a tool schema property instead of a system block.
- **B2 — names-only Codex wrapper skill catalogue** (~8.7K chars saved beyond current compaction), handling the OC2 skill-list format fail-open.
- **B3 — setup migration removes stale `~/.config/opencode/tool/osgrep.ts`** (guarded: only when it is the osgrep tool).
- **B4 — dedupe native Read reminder of `.agents/AGENTS.md`** when byte-identical to loaded guidance, only if a deterministic, cache-stable hook exists in both runtimes; otherwise document and defer.

## Why

- Measured: sessions where the placeholder entered history dropped from 91.6% to 8.1% Anthropic cache hit rate (76 of 87 calls zero cache read); clean sessions stay ~91.7%.
- Lost cache marker prevents cross-session reuse of the identical ~75K-char redistributed block.
- First-prompt context ~30K tokens vs ~17.7K earlier; target ~22K without losing guidance, skills or invocation paths.

## Reproducer

1. Build an Anthropic request body whose `messages` contain a tool_result with the billing placeholder text (the `cch=` field followed by five zero digits and `;`), plus the billing header system block.
2. Run `transformRequestBody` twice on identical input.
3. Observed: the tool_result copy receives a different hash on each call (probe: `ecefd`, then `35820`) while the header keeps the placeholder unsigned. Expected: tool_result bytes identical across calls; header signed.
4. Redistribution probe: input with 3 `cache_control` markers leaves `redistributeSystemToMessages` with 2.

Session evidence: after the placeholder entered history, 87 calls hit 8.1% cache (76 zero-read) versus 91.6% before in the same session.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** Anthropic OAuth compliance wire shape (billing header, redistribution, tag renames, tool-name normalisation, `agent__intent`, adaptive thinking, cch signing) must stay intact on two runtime majors; regressions affect the shared OAuth pool.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth-body.mjs` — A1 header-position substitution (`finalizeBillingHeaderHash`), A2 marker carry (`redistributeSystemToMessages`), A3 log line
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth-cch.mjs` — A1 helper if needed (`buildBillingHeader`, `computeBodyHash`)
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/ttsr.mjs` — B1 in-place system mutation (`ttsrSystemTransform`)
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tool-definition.mjs` — B1 OpenAI `agent__intent` schema property
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/context-catalogue.mjs` — B2
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh` — B3 (`cleanup_osgrep`)
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/context-efficiency.md` — loading contract updates
- `EDIT/NEW: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/*.mjs` — regression tests for A1, A2, B1, B2

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** OC1 `index.mjs` (`experimental.chat.system.transform`, `tool.definition`, request fetch wrapper); OC2 `v2.mjs` context hook and `v2-provider-auth.mjs` routing to `transformRequestBody` / `transformOpenAIRequestBody`
- **Writers/mutation paths:** request-body transforms only; no persisted state
- **Existing verification/tests:** `node --test tests/*.mjs` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/`; CI `.github/workflows/plugin-import-check.yml`
- **Schemas/config:** none
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed bundle under `~/.aidevops/agents` (symlink to active runtime bundle) via release + `aidevops update`
- **Migrations/backfills:** B3 setup migration only
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** see Rollback below

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** per-request pure transforms; sentinel must be unique per request
- **Migration/rollback:** runtime-bundle rollback covers both runtimes (single symlinked bundle)
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** OC1 1.18.x and OC2 2.0.x both exercised by E2E probe
- **Idempotency/retry:** retried requests re-sign from a fresh sentinel; history bytes must stay identical across requests
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if signing fails, preserve today's behaviour (header with placeholder) rather than dropping the header

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
cd .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops && node --test tests/*.mjs
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
# E2E probe: TTSR hook -> transformRequestBody / transformOpenAIRequestBody on OC1 and OC2 paths
```

## Rollback (if the Anthropic OAuth pool breaks in OpenCode 1 or 2)

Pre-deploy known-good bundle (recorded 2026-09-27 before this change): `3.36.2-6c71f6f025eb-1790468387-89804.hmO5BP`. Revalidate with `aidevops runtime-bundle status` before deploy; auto-update may advance it.

Immediate (covers both runtimes — both load the plugin via `~/.aidevops/agents`, a symlink to the active bundle):

```bash
aidevops runtime-bundle rollback --bundle-id 3.36.2-6c71f6f025eb-1790468387-89804.hmO5BP --reason "GH#<this issue> anthropic oauth regression"
aidevops auto-update disable
# then fully quit and restart both: opencode (OC1) and opencode2 (OC2)
```

Rollback leaves process leases and the Pulse pin unchanged.

Durable: hotfix worktree (`worktree-helper.sh add hotfix/vX --base vY`), `git revert -m 1 <merge sha>`, patch release, then `aidevops auto-update enable` (check with `aidevops auto-update check`).

Diagnostics: `~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-plugin.log` (redistribution lines), `~/.aidevops/runtimes/opencode-v2/data/opencode/log/opencode.log`, `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-diagnose.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A billing placeholder string present in a tool_result stays byte-identical across two consecutive transformed requests, the real header is signed, and its hash verifies
- [ ] Redistributed system text keeps a `cache_control` marker and the request carries ≤4 breakpoints
- [ ] Anthropic wire `system` array is unchanged versus current behaviour (billing header only, plus the exact official prompt when present) — no new kept system block
- [ ] TTSR system-transform output reaches the wire on OC1 (in-place mutation) and OC2
- [ ] OpenAI tool schemas carry `agent__intent`
- [ ] First-prompt context measurably reduced; every skill name, guidance pointer and invocation path stays reachable
- [ ] `node --test tests/*.mjs` passes; changed-file lint clean
- [ ] Released and deployed; maintainer told when to test OC1 and OC2

## Context & Decisions

- Frontmatter stripping dropped: frontmatter is consumed by `agent_config.py` (`permission.task`) and `config-agent-profiles.mjs`.
- Greeting stays OFF in the plugin: an Anthropic one-shot greeting would change the joined redistributed block on turn 2 and force a full cache rewrite.
- Out of scope follow-up: stable OpenAI first-turn cache key.

title: Release exact-tag deploy never finalises on busy main; converged runtime ends as superseded
body:
## What

A published release whose exact-tag deployment is deferred for "protected-main convergence" should be finalised with a terminal deployment receipt as soon as the active runtime verifiably contains the release tag. It should not keep deferring while `origin/main` moves, and it should not be marked `superseded` with no deploy receipt.

## Why

This is the fifth report in this area, after #31533, #32044, #32103 and #32125. Each earlier fix made one recovery step resumable, but on a busy `main` the lane still never finishes:

- The v3.36.2 release (source PR #32434, protected-main provenance PR #32439, merge `aefeca852631`) published successfully to GitHub Release, npm and Homebrew. The publish and postflight runs both succeeded.
- Five `aidevops release reconcile 32434` runs over about 30 minutes all logged the same messages and exited in `phase=exact-tag-deployment` with `terminal_receipt=null`:
  - `[ERROR] Post-release deployment gate verified protected integration aefeca852631, but active runtime 4e045c0fd5ed is stale; defer for protected-main convergence`
  - `[ERROR] Post-release deployment gate could not verify the active runtime before deployment`
  - `[INFO] Post-publication deployment deferred for protected-main runtime convergence`
- The active runtime was a sibling squash merge (PR #32432), and `main` advanced again before every retry (for example `0cece506d`).
- The scheduled auto-update then moved the runtime to `3.36.2-6c71f6f025eb`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor v3.36.2 6c71f6f025eb` succeeds, so deployment had converged.
- The lane never recorded that. `aidevops release status 32434` now reports `RELEASE_RECEIPT=superseded` / `STALE_RELEASE_TAG=v3.36.2` / `LATEST_RELEASE_TAG=v3.36.3`, because another session released v3.36.3 (source PR #32436) in the meantime.
- Operator impact:
  - Two red `[ERROR]` lines appear for an expected, non-failing deferral.
  - The release child reported "Release complete" while the receipt was null.
  - A human has to keep re-running reconcile with no bounded end.
  - The outcome ("superseded") hides the fact that v3.36.2 was successfully deployed.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: `aidevops release reconcile 32434`, then later `aidevops release status 32434`, run from a linked aidevops worktree.

**Actual output**:

```text
RELEASE_LANE={"active":true,"source_pr":32434,"phase":"exact-tag-deployment","tag":"v3.36.2",...,"terminal_receipt":null}
RELEASE_REMOTE_STATE=published
[ERROR] Post-release deployment gate verified protected integration aefeca852631, but active runtime 4e045c0fd5ed is stale; defer for protected-main convergence
[ERROR] Post-release deployment gate could not verify the active runtime before deployment
[INFO] Post-publication deployment deferred for protected-main runtime convergence
```

After auto-update swapped the runtime to `3.36.2-6c71f6f025eb` (a descendant of `v3.36.2`), the output was:

```text
RELEASE_RECEIPT=superseded
STALE_RELEASE_TAG=v3.36.2
LATEST_RELEASE_TAG=v3.36.3
release:superseded already recorded for PR #32434
```

**Expected:** a terminal exact-tag deployment receipt for v3.36.2 once the active runtime contains the tag.

**Steps:**

1. Merge release PR A and an unrelated PR B close together on protected `main`, so that the active runtime bundle is built from B and is neither an ancestor nor a descendant of A's release commit.
2. Publish the release. `aidevops release reconcile <A>` defers with exit 76 as quoted above.
3. Let at least one more unrelated PR merge to `main`, then re-run `aidevops release reconcile <A>`. It defers again; repeat indefinitely.
4. Let `aidevops-auto-update` swap the runtime to a bundle that descends from the release tag. `aidevops release reconcile <A>` still does not record a deployment receipt. If a newer release is published first, the lane ends as `superseded` with no deployment evidence.

Observed on 2026-09-27, macOS, v3.36.2.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh:836-947` (the active-runtime gate that returns 76), the `stale_runtime` branch at about line 936, and `run_post_publication_gates` at about line 1046:
  - When the active runtime SHA **descends from the release tag commit** (`merge-base --is-ancestor <tag-commit> <active_sha>`), and the existing bundle-convergence verification passes, treat deployment as converged and finalise the receipt. Protected-main tip stability should not be required in that case; an active runtime that already contains the tag is sufficient exact-tag evidence.
  - Keep the current strict checks, including the `#aidevops:trust-boundary` provenance, for sibling and unrelated runtimes.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`, supersession path at about lines 1215-1260 and 1440-1470: before recording `superseded` for a lane stuck in `exact-tag-deployment` or `reconcile-required`, check whether the active runtime descends from the stale tag. If it does, record the deployment receipt as well, for example `deployed_then_superseded`, so the evidence is kept.
- Deferral UX:
  - Log the expected deferral at INFO or WARN, not `print_error`.
  - Print one next action and the condition it is waiting for, for example "waiting for the runtime to include <tag>; auto-update or `aidevops update` converges it".
- Convergence trigger: after the runtime bundle swap in the auto-update or setup path, reconcile any active lane in `exact-tag-deployment` whose tag is now an ancestor of the new bundle. Alternatively, document that `aidevops update` followed by `aidevops release reconcile <PR>` is the finalising step. Pick whichever is lower-risk and state why.
- `.agents/workflows/release.md`, standard-tier handoff: a child must not report "Release complete" while `terminal_receipt=null`. It should report the state as "published; deployment deferred".
- Reuse the existing fixtures in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh`, around lines 726-926 (the stale-active and protected-integration cases), for regression coverage of the descendant-runtime finalisation and deployed-then-superseded paths.

## Acceptance

- Scenario: deferred lane, then the runtime moves to a bundle descending from the tag, then `aidevops release reconcile <PR>`. The lane gets a terminal deployment receipt, exits 0 and prints no `[ERROR]` lines.
- Scenario: a stale lane is superseded after the runtime already contains its tag. The receipt records both the deployment evidence and the supersession.
- Sibling or unrelated runtimes that do not contain the tag still defer (exit 76). Provenance and trust-boundary checks are unchanged.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh` and the existing release and reconcile tests pass. ShellCheck is clean on changed scripts.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: Add a reusable cost-capped NanoGPT Stagehand v4 public-page probe
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Reusable cost-capped NanoGPT Stagehand v4 public-page probe

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `Stagehand NanoGPT bounded reusable probe` → no relevant lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: Stagehand route added in PR #32394; evidence in merged PRs #32400, #32404, #32440; no open PR targeting the route found.
- [x] File refs verified: four tracked files and the cited line ranges were inspected.
- [x] Tier: thinking — model-billing and credential-use safety require a fail-closed bound, not a guessed cost limit.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — local one-off script had private absolute paths and was deleted; it is not a safe source artifact.

## What and why

Provide an **explicit, opt-in, repeatable** public-page Stagehand v4.1.0 extraction probe using a configured NanoGPT model without exposing its API key. An interactive run currently requires an ad hoc temporary script; the three successful corrected runs on `https://example.com` (PR #32440) took median 12,978 ms and reported about $0.004 each, while the deterministic locator took median 8 ms. Initial callback attempts uncovered the SDK's `json_schema`/`structuredContent` response contract, fenced-JSON handling, and a two-call extraction flow. Preserve these lessons in a safe reusable capability rather than a user's private absolute-path script.

Related to #32376, but this leaf is **not** the authenticated-tab/profile-isolation comparison. Do not attach to or inspect any existing signed-in browser tab. Do not use the OpenCode free tier as an embedded callback: PR #32404 records its HTTP 403 restriction. Do not spend against a provider credential in CI or worker execution without separate trusted test authority; the historical $2 interactive test cap does not grant recurring or headless spending.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `bash .agents/scripts/stagehand-v4-helper.sh help`

**Actual output:** `Usage: .agents/scripts/stagehand-v4-helper.sh {install|setup|status|run-example}` followed by `Opt-in isolated Stagehand v4.1.0; run-example requires OPENAI_API_KEY and STAGEHAND_MODEL.` There is no reviewed NanoGPT command.

`.agents/scripts/stagehand-v4-helper.sh:63-79` has only the reviewed `run-example` path requiring `OPENAI_API_KEY` and an `openai/` model; `.agents/tools/browser/stagehand-v4-example.mjs.txt:7-25` uses that single provider. `.agents/tools/browser/browser-benchmark.md:89-132` documents the NanoGPT callback experiment but does not supply a reusable reviewed runner. The 2026-09-27 probe needed a temporary script, a bounded process, three-or-fewer callback requests, fenced-JSON normalization, and accounting for two model calls per successful extraction.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/stagehand-v4-helper.sh:11-16,63-96` — add a separate explicit NanoGPT probe command or justify a small dedicated helper. Keep `run-example` unchanged and prevent provider fallback.
- `NEW: .agents/tools/browser/stagehand-v4-nanogpt-probe.mjs.txt` (or another reviewed repo-owned source, exact basename worker may select) — fixed public target, SDK callback, time/request/input bounds, redacted output, cleanup. Do not copy the private temporary script or hard-code user paths.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-stagehand-v4-route.sh:14-42` — focused offline negative and positive cases; use existing test fixture pattern.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/browser/browser-benchmark.md:89-132` — describe exact opt-in invocation, scope, reported cost semantics, and historical vs reproducible results.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** CLI dispatch in `.agents/scripts/stagehand-v4-helper.sh`; docs/examples in `.agents/tools/browser/`; avoid changing legacy Playwright/Playwriter routes.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/stagehand-v4-helper.sh` creates only the reviewed isolated Stagehand v4 example; never write browser profiles or credential files. New probe output is stdout only unless an explicitly selected non-secret output path is designed.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stagehand-v4-route.sh` supplies installed-version fixtures and missing-key/modified-example refusal; add mocked callback/cost cases without paid API calls.
- **Schemas/config:** installed Stagehand 4.1.0 `ClientLLM` response requires `json_schema` plus parsed `structuredContent`; use provider/model metadata as available, and refuse when a trustworthy maximum cost cannot be bounded. No persistent default provider config change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** the existing helper copies a reviewed example to a separate local project without overwriting a user edit; do not modify the deployed `~/.aidevops/agents/` mirror directly.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because this adds a new opt-in command to `.agents/scripts/stagehand-v4-helper.sh` and leaves the existing installed route unchanged; no state migration.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/scripts/stagehand-v4-helper.sh` must close the local browser and SDK session/server on success, failure, timeout, or fuse; removing the opt-in command restores previous behavior.

### Implementation Steps

1. Check installed Stagehand/OpenCode SDK versions and local exported interfaces before coding; derive the callback `generate` request/response contract from installed types rather than guessing. Choose a provider-auth path that uses OpenCode's configured NanoGPT account without reading `auth.json` or printing credentials.
2. Make the probe fail closed before inference unless it has an **explicit per-invocation USD cap**, model ID, fixed public target, conservative request/input/output bounds, and evidence-backed worst-case pricing. Account for retries and provider overhead; post-call cost reporting alone is not a hard cap. If hard bounding cannot be proven, keep the live path disabled and still deliver the safe offline harness with a clear blocker. Preserve Playwright as deterministic-default and the existing `run-example` behavior.
3. Provide structured success/failure receipts (navigation, deterministic locator, AI extraction, callback count, reported tokens/cost, elapsed time, and unknown/unreceipted spend separately). Handle fenced JSON only at the format boundary; do not present corrected-run 3/3 as an unconditional success rate. No raw prompt/page content, key, or profile detail in logs.
4. Exercise the fixed public-page path only with fresh trusted billing authority; automated verification uses mocked SDK/provider responses. Commit and push a WIP before broad gates if the work grows; proceed through the narrowest relevant lint and PR checks.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** single-run request and spend counters must not race or leak across runs; reject parallel callbacks if not safely accounted.
- **Migration/rollback:** opt-in only; removing it must leave the original OpenAI example and Stagehand v3 users unchanged.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** pin/verify v4.1.0 and SDK response shape; fail closed if versions change and invalidate pricing/format assumptions.
- **Idempotency/retry:** reruns require fresh explicit authority/budget; retries count against the same per-run ceiling. No silent provider or model fallback.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** close owned processes and record any unknown cost; an incomplete receipt is not a successful benchmark. Keep the objective open if a cap or auth fuse prevents live use, then seek an approved bounded transport rather than relaxing the fuse.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- **Surface mapping:** helper/example invocation and failure boundaries map to `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stagehand-v4-route.sh`; docs map to the changed-file Markdown check; live inference requires separate trusted authorization.

bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-stagehand-v4-route.sh

shellcheck .agents/scripts/stagehand-v4-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-stagehand-v4-route.sh

bash .agents/scripts/stagehand-v4-helper.sh help

Run `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` for edited code and documentation.
- An operator-approved local public-page run only after checking current pricing/cap; report actual provider usage and whether cap was enforceable. This is not a CI acceptance dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Positive: opt-in reviewed probe extracts `Example Domain` from a fresh isolated `https://example.com` browser using a configured NanoGPT provider and an enforceable per-run cap; reports deterministic/model timings, request count and provider cost.
- [ ] Negative regression: missing key/cap, unsupported version, provider 403, over-budget projection, malformed JSON, extra request, and timeout each fail closed with browser/server cleanup and no paid fallback or profile access; offline fixtures cover the no-cap, two-call success, and over-limit cases.
- [ ] Existing `run-example` and Playwright-default paths remain unchanged; documentation distinguishes this probe from a full v3/v4 benchmark and from the untested authenticated-tab lane.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/stagehand-v4-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tools/browser/stagehand-v4-nanogpt-probe.mjs.txt`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stagehand-v4-route.sh`
- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-benchmark.md`

title: Canonical checkouts go silently stale: no convergence owner, SSH remotes fail under launchd, dead scheduler jobs unreported
body:
## What

Clean canonical checkouts should converge to their merged default branch automatically, and scheduled sync failures should be visible. Today three linked gaps leave canonicals silently stale:

1. **No convergence owner.** After a merge, `full-loop-helper-merge.sh` prints `CANONICAL_SYNC_PENDING=true` (about lines 1591-1615), but nothing consumes it. `repo-sync-helper.sh check` is deliberately report-only: lines 516-535 only log `STALE …; human checkout left unchanged`. The last run that pulled anything was on 2026-07-10. Since then, every run has logged `0 pulled`.
2. **GitHub SSH remotes fail under launchd.** `run_git_with_auth_fallback` (`repo-sync-helper.sh:433-461`) retries only GitHub **HTTPS** remotes via the `gh` credential helper. SSH remotes (`git@github.com:owner/repo.git`) fail in the launchd context with `ssh_askpass: exec(/usr/X11R6/bin/ssh-askpass): No such file or directory` / `Permission denied (publickey)`. That makes 8-10 repos fail on nearly every run for weeks, including `marcusquinn/aidevops.sh`.
3. **Stale scheduler entries go unnoticed.** A launchd job labelled `sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` runs `~/.aidevops/agents/custom/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh check`, and that script no longer exists. The job has `LastExitStatus = 32512` (exit 127), and its log repeats "No such file or directory". No health surface reports it.

## Why

- Observed 2026-09-27: the `aidevops.sh` canonical checkout (clean, on `main`, SSH remote) was **94 commits behind** `origin/main` after this session's merges. The `aidevops` canonical (HTTPS remote) was current.
- Agents are told canonicals are read-only service mirrors that audited paths keep converged (`.agents/AGENTS.md` "Git workflow"; `reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md`). In practice, no path converges a clean, behind-only canonical, so humans and agents read stale code there.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: `tail -n 40 ~/.aidevops/logs/repo-sync.log` and `git -C <canonical-of-an-ssh-remote-repo> status -sb --untracked-files=no`

**Actual output**:

```text
[2026-09-27 01:54:06] [INFO] CHECK aidevops.sh: reading origin/main...
ssh_askpass: exec(/usr/X11R6/bin/ssh-askpass): No such file or directory
git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey).
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
[2026-09-27 01:54:08] [ERROR] FAIL aidevops.sh: git ls-remote failed
...
[2026-09-27 01:57:36] [INFO] Sync complete: 0 pulled, 94 skipped, 8 failed
```

```text
## main...origin/main [behind 94]
```

Also: `launchctl list sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` reports `"LastExitStatus" = 32512` with `ProgramArguments` pointing to a missing `custom/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh`.

**Expected:** a clean, default-branch, strictly-behind canonical is fast-forwarded (or at least surfaced as actionable). SSH GitHub remotes are readable under launchd through the existing `gh` fallback. Missing-program aidevops jobs are flagged.

## How

- **Part A, SSH fallback (smallest, do first).** EDIT `.agents/scripts/repo-sync-helper.sh:433-461`.
  - When the remote is a GitHub SSH URL and the stderr is an auth failure, retry the same read-only operation against the equivalent `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git` URL, using the existing `run_git_with_gh_credential` path. Pass the URL explicitly; do not rewrite the configured remote.
  - Run SSH attempts with `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes"` so launchd never tries `ssh-askpass`.
  - Follow the existing `is_github_https_remote` / `is_git_auth_failure` helpers. Add cases to `.agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-sync-helper-gh-auth.sh`.
- **Part B, guarded convergence for clean behind-only canonicals.** In `repo-sync-helper.sh`, after the `STALE` detection (about line 534), add a convergence step. It is limited to checkouts that are:
  - on the default branch
  - clean, using the existing `is_working_tree_clean`
  - strictly behind: `merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD <upstream_sha>` after a fetch of only that ref
  - registered in `repos.json`, and not opted out

  For those, run `git merge --ff-only`. Never touch diverged, dirty, detached or non-default-branch checkouts; keep today's `STALE`/`SKIP` logs for them. Keep it behind an explicit config or flag if maintainers prefer. State the chosen default and why in the PR, and reconcile it with `reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md`. Optionally, let `full-loop-helper-merge.sh`'s `CANONICAL_SYNC_PENDING` path call the same function for the merged repo. Add cases to `.agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-sync-helper-status.sh`.
- **Part C, visibility.**
  - Have the health/status surface (`repo-aidevops-health-helper.sh`, or `aidevops status`) report:
    - repos whose repo-sync result was `FAIL` for more than N consecutive runs
    - canonicals that were `STALE` for more than 24h
    - `sh.aidevops.*` launchd jobs (and systemd equivalents via `setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh`) whose program or first script argument is missing
  - Report only, with an explicit removal command; do not auto-unload user jobs.
- If Parts A-C are too large for one PR, deliver A and C first and file B as a linked follow-up with this evidence.

## Files Scope

Authorized implementation map for the existing A-C outcome (no hard exclusion in the original brief):
- `.agents/scripts/repo-sync-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-sync-helper-gh-auth.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/fixtures/repo-sync-fake-git.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-sync-helper-status.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/repo-aidevops-health-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-aidevops-health.sh`
- `.agents/reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md`

Integration evidence: `repo-sync-helper.sh` owns the check result and convergence,
`repo-aidevops-health-helper.sh` is the named health surface, and the three
existing test scripts and the Git fixture cover their behavior (the stricter clean-tree guard now uses git status). Verify with those scripts and
ShellCheck on changed shell scripts. This scope does not authorize modifying
user jobs or bypassing canonical safeguards.

## Acceptance

- Under launchd (or `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`), `repo-sync-helper.sh check` reads a GitHub SSH-remote repo successfully when `gh auth status` is valid, with no `ssh-askpass` error.
- A clean, default-branch canonical that is strictly behind is fast-forwarded (or clearly marked as convergence-eligible if gated off). Dirty, diverged or non-default-branch canonicals are untouched, and tests prove it.
- The health/status output lists the missing-program `sh.aidevops.*` job and the persistently failing repos.
- The existing repo-sync tests pass, and ShellCheck is clean on changed scripts.
