title: Add mirror-sync routine for registered private upstream mirrors (mirror_upstream in repos.json)
body:
## What

Add a framework routine that keeps registered **private mirrors** of third-party upstream repositories current. It uses the `mirror_upstream` / `mirror_upstream_url` fields that `repos.json` entries already carry. Upstream changes are merged into a dated sync branch and pushed to the mirror only when the merge is clean and non-destructive. Conflicts are reported, never forced.

## Why

- Users keep private mirrors of licensed or third-party template repos to build on. The framework already recognises these entries: `privacy-guard-helper.sh:196-220`, `contributor-insight-helper.sh:60-66` and `session-miner-actuation-helper.sh:214` treat `mirror_upstream` as a privacy marker. Nothing syncs them.
- Observed 2026-09-27: a user-local routine that did this (`~/.aidevops/agents/custom/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh`, launchd label `sh.aidevops.mirror-sync`) had disappeared around 2026-04-24. Since then:
  - The launchd job has failed on every run with exit 127 (`LastExitStatus = 32512`).
  - The mirrors were synced by hand only occasionally, with a merge of `upstream/main` into `sync/upstream-YYYYMMDD` and then `main`.
  - One mirror is now 13+ upstream commits behind.
- The legacy script also misread boolean `"mirror_upstream": true` (a privacy-only marker on some entries) as an upstream slug, logging `upstream=true`.

## How

- NEW `.agents/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh` with `check | sync | status [--repo <slug>]`. Model it on `.agents/scripts/repo-sync-helper.sh` (config discovery, logging, `run_git_with_auth_fallback`, state file).
- **Selection:** only `repos.json` entries where `mirror_upstream` is a **string** `owner/repo`. Boolean or empty values are privacy markers: skip them with an INFO line. The upstream URL is `mirror_upstream_url` if set, otherwise `https://github.com/<mirror_upstream>.git`. The mirror is the entry's `slug` (its `origin`).
- **Never mutate the canonical checkout.** Canonicals are read-only service mirrors (see `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Git workflow"). Work in a helper-owned temporary clone or linked worktree under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`, and remove it afterwards.
- **Algorithm, per mirror and upstream default branch:**
  1. Fetch `upstream/<branch>` and `origin/<branch>`.
  2. If upstream is already an ancestor of origin, record `OK up-to-date`.
  3. If origin is an ancestor of upstream (a pure mirror), fast-forward push the upstream tip to `origin/<branch>`.
  4. Otherwise (the mirror has local commits), create `sync/upstream-YYYYMMDD` from `origin/<branch>` and merge upstream with `--no-ff`.
     - If the merge is clean, push the sync branch, then push it to `origin/<branch>` only as a fast-forward of the current origin tip.
     - On conflict, abort the merge. Push nothing to `<branch>`, and record `CONFLICT` with the conflicting paths. Optionally open an issue or PR on the **mirror** repo, never upstream, using the aidevops GitHub wrappers.
  5. Never `--force`, never push to the upstream remote, and never push tags unless explicitly configured.
- **Auth:** reuse the GitHub SSH-to-HTTPS `gh` credential fallback and `BatchMode=yes` from #32453 Part A. If #32453 hasn't landed, implement the shared helper once and let both scripts use it.
- **Scheduling:** register a new core routine in `.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh`.
  - Follow `r906` / `describe_r906` (about lines 24 and 423-453): daily, with launchd and systemd via `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh`.
  - Install it only when at least one entry has a string `mirror_upstream`.
  - **Reuse the label `sh.aidevops.mirror-sync`** so installing the routine replaces a stale user job with that label. Only replace it if the existing job's program or script path is missing, or its plist was framework-generated; otherwise leave it and report the collision.
- **Docs:** add a short section to `reference/routines.md`, or a new `reference/repo-mirrors.md` linked from it. Cover the `repos.json` fields, what the routine will and won't push, conflict handling, and how to opt out (`"mirror_sync": false`).
- **Privacy:** mirror slugs are private by definition. Logs and any GitHub writes must stay on the mirror repo or in local logs, never in public issues or TODOs (see `reference/pre-push-guards.md`).
- **Tests:** add a NEW `.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh` using local bare repos as origin and upstream. Cases:
  - up-to-date no-op
  - pure-mirror fast-forward
  - diverged mirror with a clean merge (sync branch plus ff-push of `main`)
  - conflict: no push to `main`, and a `CONFLICT` state
  - boolean `mirror_upstream` skipped
  - upstream auth failure reported as `FAIL` without a prompt
  - the canonical checkout is untouched

## Acceptance

- `mirror-sync-helper.sh check` lists each string-`mirror_upstream` mirror with `OK`, `BEHIND n`, `DIVERGED` or `FAIL`, and makes no remote writes.
- `mirror-sync-helper.sh sync`:
  - brings a clean mirror to include the upstream tip, using only fast-forward pushes to the mirror's default branch
  - on conflict, leaves the mirror's default branch unchanged and records `CONFLICT`
  - never force-pushes and never writes to upstream
- `setup.sh --non-interactive` installs the routine only when mirrors are configured, and replaces a missing-program `sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` job.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh` passes. The existing routine and scheduler tests pass (`test-launchd-install-if-changed.sh`, `test-systemd-unit-generation.sh`). ShellCheck is clean.

title: Approval snapshots go stale when supervisor dashboards that link a PR refresh
body:
## Problem

External PR approvals signed with `sudo aidevops approve pr N` become `STALE_APPROVAL` within minutes whenever the PR is listed on a supervisor Queue Health Dashboard issue. `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate` then reports `missing cryptographic development authority` and asks for a re-sign, which goes stale again on the next dashboard refresh.

Observed on PR #32402 (head `d1449dcbdb`): approval comment signed at `2026-09-27T01:12:11Z`; minutes later `approval-helper.sh verify pr 32402 marcusquinn/aidevops --expect-head d1449dcb… --require-authority` → `APPROVAL_REASON: stale-or-unproven-continuity` / `STALE_APPROVAL`. The only timeline mutations after signing were the approval flow's own lock/unlabel, and no PR comment changed.

## Reproducer

1. Pick an open external PR that appears in a supervisor dashboard's "Open PRs" table (timeline shows `cross-referenced` events from `[Supervisor:*]` issues).
2. `sudo aidevops approve pr <N> <owner/repo>`; immediately `approval-helper.sh verify pr <N> <owner/repo> --expect-head <sha> --require-authority` → `VERIFIED`.
3. Wait for the next dashboard refresh (a few minutes) and re-run the same verify → `APPROVAL_REASON: stale-or-unproven-continuity` / `STALE_APPROVAL`.
4. Rebuild the snapshot with `approval_snapshot_v2_build pr <N> <owner/repo> <approval-comment-id> <issued_at> stable current` (from `approval-snapshot-v2.sh`): the only fields that differ over time are `linked_references[].source.title/body` of the dashboard issues.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh` → `_approval_snapshot_v2_linked_references_json` (source object, around the `source: (if (.source.issue // null) == null ...` block) binds each cross-referencing source's `title`, `body`, and `state` into the signed digest. Supervisor dashboard issues (e.g. #23855, #23404, #23126 — authored by write-access supervisors, marker `<!-- aidevops:dashboard-freshness -->`) mention every open PR in their "Open PRs" table and rewrite their title/body every pulse. Every dashboard refresh therefore changes the PR snapshot digest.

GH#29009 already removed linked-source `updated_at` for the same class of reason; source title/body/state have the same mutability problem for auto-updated sources. PR approvals have no continuity fallback (`_approval_classify_digest_mismatch` only replays lifecycle continuity for issues).

## Proposed fix

In `_approval_snapshot_v2_linked_references_json`, keep binding source identity (`kind`, `repository`, `number`, `id`, `node_id`, `author`) and the reference event itself, but stop binding mutable `title`/`body`/`state` for linked sources — or, narrower, omit them only for sources whose author is maintainer-equivalent (the content cannot be attacker-controlled) or whose body carries the dashboard freshness marker **and** a trusted author. Mark the change `#aidevops:trust-boundary`. Keep the current profile as a verified-legacy profile so already-signed approvals still verify when their full digest matches (same pattern as the GH#29009 `legacy` profile in `approval_snapshot_v2_build`).

Reference pattern: the GH#29009 `source_timestamp_profile` handling in the same function; `_approval_classify_digest_mismatch` in `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh`.

## Verification

- Existing approval tests: `rg -l "approval-snapshot-v2|approval-helper" .agents/scripts/tests` and run the matching suites.
- Add a focused case: a PR snapshot with a cross-referencing trusted dashboard source whose title/body change after `issued_at` must still verify; an untrusted source edit must still produce `STALE_APPROVAL` if bodies remain bound for untrusted authors.
- Runtime: sign an approval on an open external PR that appears on a dashboard, wait for the next dashboard refresh, and confirm `approval-helper.sh verify pr N <repo> --expect-head <sha> --require-authority` still returns `VERIFIED`.

Files: `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh`, `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh` (only if a legacy/continuity classification is needed), related tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`.

title: t18483: Restart OpenCode V2 background service after agents redeploy
body:
## What

After an aidevops agents redeploy swaps the runtime bundle, the long-running OpenCode V2 (`opencode2`) background service keeps running. Directories it opens for the first time afterwards do not load the aidevops plugin: `opencode.log` has no `loading plugin` line for those locations. Without the plugin, the provider-auth OAuth hooks are missing, so Anthropic requests fail with `AI.Error.Authentication: API key is invalid`.

Directories the service opened before the swap keep working, and `opencode2 run --standalone` works. `opencode2 service restart` fixes it.

## Why

Updates are mostly run by AI sessions, so a warning alone goes unseen. While V2 is an isolated preview runtime, setup should restart the service after a deploy. Revisit this (for example, defer the restart until the service is idle) when `opencode2` becomes the default.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh`: add `_restart_opencode_v2_service_after_deploy` and call it at the end of `deploy_aidevops_agents`.
  - Reads the pid from `${AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_STATE_HOME:-~/.aidevops/runtimes/opencode-v2/state}/opencode/service.json` without reading other fields.
  - Restarts only when that pid is alive and is not an ancestor of setup, so it never kills the service hosting the running session; in that case it warns.
  - Resolves the binary via `~/.aidevops/.opencode-v2-bin-resolved` and falls back to `~/.local/bin/opencode2`.
  - Runs the restart with a 60s timeout. Set `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_OPENCODE_V2_SERVICE_RESTART=1` to opt out.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh`: covers the restart, opt-out, ancestor and dead-pid cases.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh`
- `shellcheck -x` on both files
- Live check: the function restarted the real service (the pid changed). An Anthropic request from a newly opened directory then succeeded; before the restart it failed with "API key is invalid".

title: bug(approval): terminal-blocker CLAIM_RELEASED comment invalidates signed issue approval
body:
## Problem

A framework-generated terminal-blocker `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment invalidates an existing signed issue approval. As a result, the approved issue cannot be redispatched or started interactively until a maintainer signs it again.

Observed on #32362: approval comment `5836571216` verified before the second worker attempt. The worker then posted a trusted-owner `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked ...` ops comment that included the `<!-- aidevops:terminal-blocker-observation revision=... blocker=... -->` fragment and a `Terminal blocker:` / `Projected state:` / `Next action:` / `Raw evidence remains...` block. After that, `approval-helper.sh verify issue 32362 marcusquinn/aidevops` returned `STALE_APPROVAL` (`APPROVAL_REASON: stale-or-unproven-continuity`). `interactive-start-helper.sh --issue 32362` also failed its maintainer gate pre-check (`approval=STALE_APPROVAL`).

Diagnosis (source walk): `approval_snapshot_v2_build` keeps comment `5839090019` in the snapshot comment set because `canonical_dispatch_audit` in `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh:100-109` accepts only a single-line `CLAIM_RELEASED ...` body between `ops:start` and `ops:end`. Timeline continuity replay (`approval-helper-continuity.sh`) passes: every label and assignee mutation came from an authorized actor. The digest mismatch is caused only by this comment.

## Expected behavior

A canonical terminal-blocker release comment written by `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` (`terminal_blocker_observation_fragment` + `_terminal_blocker_recovery`, lines 290-331) and posted by a trusted association after signing should not count toward the approval snapshot. Arbitrary prose, extra lines, or copied markers must still be bound to the approval.

## Worker Guidance

- **Files to modify:** `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh` (`canonical_dispatch_audit`, or a sibling `canonical_terminal_blocker_release` definition used in the same exclusion select).
- **Reference pattern:** `canonical_no_work_escalation_skip` in the same file. It is an exact full-envelope regex with a bounded field grammar and the `aidevops_worker_footer` suffix. Mirror the exact writer text: the enumerated `reason` / `owner` values and fixed `Next action:` sentences from `_terminal_blocker_recovery`, plus `revision` / `blocker` hex fields.
- **Trust boundary:** keep the trusted-association, post-cutoff, unedited (`updated_at == created_at`) constraints. Mark the change with `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.
- **Verification:** extend the existing approval snapshot tests (`rg -l "canonical_dispatch_audit|CLAIM_RELEASED" .agents/scripts/tests`). Use a synthetic terminal-blocker release that must be excluded, plus a variant with one extra prose line that must remain bound. Then `approval-helper.sh verify issue 32362 marcusquinn/aidevops` should return `VERIFIED` without re-signing.

Related: #32362 (blocked by this defect).

title: Anthropic latest-generation tier fallbacks and OpenAI-vs-Anthropic provider-family model A/B
body:
## Goal

The Anthropic OAuth account is available again (pool status: 1 account, token endpoint OK). This issue has two parts:

1. Bring the Anthropic same-tier fallbacks up to the latest generation.
2. Let the existing issue-level model A/B compare **OpenAI vs Anthropic as provider families** on background workers, including the workers' OpenCode subagent delegations.

## Evidence

- `opencode models anthropic --verbose` lists `claude-haiku-4-5` (latest Haiku), `claude-sonnet-5` and `claude-opus-5-5`. Sonnet 5 and Opus 5.5 advertise adaptive `low|medium|high|xhigh|max` effort variants. Haiku 4.5 only has budget variants (`high|max`).
- Live headless smoke tests (2026-09-27) passed for `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5@low` and `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5@medium`, including a read-tool call on Haiku and Sonnet 5.
- The shipped routing table still points at `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-6`.

title: Interactive subagent delegation OpenAI-vs-Anthropic A/B with parent-acceptance reporting
body:
## Goal

Extend the OpenAI-vs-Anthropic model A/B (#32468) to **interactive** OpenCode subagent delegations. These are children launched from a human-driven primary session. Headless workers are out of scope because they already inherit the per-issue arm route.

## Why

The #32468 issue-level trial covers background workers and their subagents. The per-issue `AIDEVOPS_MODEL_ROUTING_TABLE` is passed to the worker, and the plugin's tier router (`loadModelRouting` in `index.mjs`) reads it. Interactive sessions have no issue arm, so their children always follow the shipped routing table. Interactive children also carry the richest outcome signal: parent acceptance receipts (`aidevops_objective_receipt` → `subagent.acceptance` runtime events, with `accepted_unchanged` / `accepted_repaired` / `rejected`).

## Proposed design (worker should verify before implementing)

- **Assignment unit.** Assign per child session, not per parent. Use a stable hash of `experiment.id + seed + child sessionID` into one of the two provider-family arms (same arm schema as `model-ab-helper.mjs` `tiers` arms).
- **Opt-in config.** Use a user-owned opt-in config (for example a `subagent_ab` block or a separate private JSON path read by the plugin). It is off by default and bounded by `starts_at`/`ends_at` with the same 168-hour cap. Reuse `validateExperiment` where possible.
- **Router hook point.** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-effort-handlers.mjs` `routeTierMessage` → `applyConnectedRoutingModel`. When a trial is active and the route is not pinned, select from the arm-merged routing (arm model first, shipped same-tier fallbacks after), then record the arm on the policy.
- **Excluded children.** Skip pinned agents, domain/creative/browser routes and `specialist-advisor`. They have their own routing contracts.
- **Telemetry.** Add `ab_experiment`/`ab_arm` to the `onRoutingDecision` payload (`subagent-effort-params.mjs`) so runtime events carry the arm.
- **Report.** Add a `model-ab-helper.mjs report-subagents` view. It joins routing decisions to `subagent.acceptance` events by child session and reports, per arm: delegations, accepted_unchanged, accepted_repaired, rejected, interventions, tokens/cost. It must never infer acceptance from child completion.
- **Same-model clamp.** Keep the rule that children cannot exceed their parent's effort. It only applies when the model is the same, so cross-provider children are unaffected.

## Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-effort-handlers.mjs`, `subagent-effort.mjs`, `subagent-effort-params.mjs`, `index.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/model-ab-helper.mjs`, `model-ab-report.mjs` (reuse the arm schema and validation from #32468)
- Tests: extend `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs`
- Docs: `.agents/workflows/optimize-tiers.md` (A/B section)

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-ab-helper.mjs`
- With the trial off, routing is byte-identical to today (existing tests pass unchanged).
- With a trial on, a non-pinned `general` child is routed to its arm's tier model, and the routing decision carries the arm.

Depends on #32468.

title: full-loop merge gate: name the failing readiness condition (draft) and stop printing 'no approval required' after verified authority
body:
## Problem

The `full-loop-helper.sh merge` / `pre-merge-gate` diagnostics are misleading in two places.

1. Draft PR readiness failure lists every condition instead of the failed one. Interactive `commit-and-pr` intentionally creates drafts; the gate should name `isDraft` and provide `gh pr ready N --repo <slug>`.
2. A verified external/fork authority approval is reported as `no approval required`. The trust-boundary diagnostic must distinguish no targets from verified targets.

## Reproducer

1. Create an interactive draft PR with `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr`.
2. Run `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <owner/repo> --squash`; the output must name the draft condition.
3. Run `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate <PR>` for an external/fork PR with a verified `sudo aidevops approve pr` signature; output must name verified targets.

## Evidence

- PR #32460 had only `isDraft: true` failing and succeeded after `gh pr ready 32460`.
- PR #32402 had verified approval comment 5852036108 but emitted the incorrect success text before merging at `e01527b`.

## Proposed fix

- Evaluate readiness conditions separately and retain fail-closed behavior.
- Mark the authority diagnostic `#aidevops:trust-boundary`, reporting either no external authority targets or verified targets.
- Apply equivalent user-facing diagnostics in the merge helper.

## Verification

- Run matching existing tests for `pre-merge-gate`, `_full_loop_verify_pr_readiness`, and `external authority`.
- Exercise a draft gate and verified external-authority gate.
- Run ShellCheck and `linters-local.sh --changed`.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh`

title: approval-helper: warn when a pinned older runtime bundle verifies approvals signed by a newer version (false STALE_APPROVAL)
body:
## Problem

Long-running interactive sessions keep calling framework helpers from the runtime bundle that was active when the session started. This is intentional: each process holds an immutable bundle lease (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`, `RUNTIME_BUNDLE_LEASE`). But the **approval verification and merge-authority decisions** made from such a session then use outdated verification logic, and the output gives no hint of this.

Observed 2026-09-27, after merging and deploying #32460 (GH#32455, new approval snapshot profile):
- `readlink ~/.aidevops/agents` → `runtime-bundles/3.37.1-19865e0439dc-…` (contains the fix).
- `which -a approval-helper.sh` in the same session → `runtime-bundles/3.36.3-146ded09ad96-…/agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` (no fix).
- `approval-helper.sh verify pr 32402 … --require-authority` (PATH, 3.36.3) → `STALE_APPROVAL`.
- `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh verify pr 32402 …` (active bundle) → `APPROVAL_REASON: exact-snapshot` / `VERIFIED`.

The maintainer signature had been produced by the newer signer (v3.37.1). The older verifier cannot reproduce the new snapshot profile, so it reported a false stale result. This fails closed, so it is safe. But it invites a pointless re-sign loop (a human `sudo` action) and cost a debugging round.

## Reproducer

1. Start an OpenCode session (the PATH resolves helpers from the current runtime bundle `A`).
2. Merge a change to the approval snapshot format and deploy it (`setup.sh --non-interactive`), so `~/.aidevops/agents` points at bundle `B`.
3. Sign an approval with the new signer: `sudo aidevops approve pr <N> <owner/repo>`.
4. **Symptom command**: in the original session, `approval-helper.sh verify pr <N> <owner/repo> --expect-head <sha> --require-authority`. **Actual output**: `STALE_APPROVAL`, while `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh verify …` → `VERIFIED`. No output mentions the bundle mismatch.

## Proposed fix

Emit a clear diagnostic when the verifier is older than the active bundle, without changing lease semantics:
- In `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` (verify path, where `STALE_APPROVAL`/`API_ERROR` are printed), and in the merge authority gate (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`, the external authority preflight): if the helper's own bundle directory differs from `readlink ~/.aidevops/agents` (resolve both; only when the script runs from a `runtime-bundles/` path), print to stderr:
  `APPROVAL_NOTE: verifier bundle <old> is older than active bundle <new>; re-run with ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh before re-signing`.
- Optional: the signed approval footer already records the signer version (`vX.Y.Z automated scan`). If the verifier's version is lower than the signer's, add the same note even without a bundle comparison.
- Never change the verdict based on this check. It is advisory only; mark it `#aidevops:trust-boundary`, with a comment that it cannot grant authority.

## Verification

- Add a focused case to `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh` (or a small sibling test), only if a fixture for bundle paths is cheap: run the helper from a fake `runtime-bundles/<old>/agents/scripts` copy with `HOME` pointing at a fake active symlink to `<new>`. Assert that the note appears on stderr and that stdout/exit code are unchanged.
- Runtime: in a session started before a deploy, run PATH `approval-helper.sh verify …` and confirm that the note names both bundles.
- ShellCheck and `linters-local.sh --changed` clean.

Files: `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`; reference for bundle-path detection: `RUNTIME_BUNDLE_LEASE` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`.

title: t18484: Add forge image-embed helper for PR/issue screenshots without web upload
body:
**Task ID:** `t18484` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-09-27
**Tags:** `feature` `framework` `interactive` `auto-dispatch`

## Outcome

Add forge image-embed helper for PR/issue screenshots without web upload

## Done when

- [ ] `publish` against a public repo prints one Markdown embed per image, each URL returns `200` with an `image/*` content type, and the asset branch contains the images.
- [ ] `publish` refuses (non-zero exit, nothing on stdout) when the target branch is the repo default branch or an open PR head branch, when a file is not an allowed image type, and for private repos without `--allow-private`.
- [ ] `github-cli.md` documents the method, the privacy check and the cleanup command; `gitlab-cli.md` documents the native uploads API.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean and `linters-local.sh --changed` passes.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `.agents/scripts/screenshot-import-helper.sh` — header, `source shared-constants.sh`, `cmd_*` functions, `cmd_help`, `main` with `case` dispatch. Copy this structure.
- **Load only if:** `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` — ShellCheck or complexity gate failures.
- **Why:** keeps the new helper consistent with framework shell conventions (explicit `return 0/1`, `local var="$1"`, Bash 3.2 compatible).
- **Stop when:** helper structure, API sequence below and verification commands are clear.

### Worker Quick-Start

```bash
# Verified API sequence (worked on 2026-09-27 against a public fork):
base64 -i image.png -o image.b64                         # macOS; use `base64 -w0 image.png` on GNU into a temp file
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/git/blobs -F encoding=base64 -F content=@image.b64 --jq .sha
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/git/trees -f "tree[][path]=image.png" -f "tree[][mode]=100644" \
  -f "tree[][type]=blob" -f "tree[][sha]=BLOB_SHA" --jq .sha   # repeat the 4 tree[] fields per file
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/git/commits -f "message=..." -f tree=TREE_SHA --jq .sha   # parentless on first publish
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/git/refs -f ref=refs/heads/BRANCH -f sha=COMMIT_SHA
# Embed URL (verified 200 image/png after redirect):
https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/raw/COMMIT_SHA/image.png
```

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/forge-image-embed-helper.sh` — model on `.agents/scripts/screenshot-import-helper.sh` structure.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/git/github-cli.md:103-110` — add a `### Screenshots and Images` subsection after "Pre-Submission Checklist" (before `## See Also`).
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/git/gitlab-cli.md` — add a short "Images in issues/MRs" note: GitLab has a native uploads API (`glab api projects/:id/uploads -F file=@path` returns a `markdown` field), so the helper is not needed there.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** new helper; no existing callers (`rg "forge-image-embed" .agents` is empty). Readers are agents following `github-cli.md`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the helper writes only to the remote repo given by `--repo`, on the branch given by `--branch` (default `aidevops-assets`), plus temp base64 files under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}` removed on exit.
- **Tests/fixtures:** N/A because no existing tests cover forge image publishing (searched `.agents/scripts/tests/` for screenshot/image helpers); verification is ShellCheck through `linters-local.sh --changed` plus the live publish below. No new test harness is requested.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A — no config keys added (`rg` of `.agents/configs` shows no image/asset settings).
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` automatically; no index to update (`screenshot-import-helper.sh` is referenced only from docs, not from a registry).
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because this is a new-file-only capability with no existing stored state to migrate.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** remote asset branches can be deleted with `gh api -X DELETE repos/OWNER/REPO/git/refs/heads/BRANCH`; document this. Deleting the branch eventually breaks embeds, so the doc must say to keep it while the PR/issue matters.

### Implementation Steps

1. Create the helper with commands `publish`, `help`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn
# forge-image-embed-helper.sh — publish images to an asset-only branch and print Markdown embeds
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=shared-constants.sh
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/shared-constants.sh"

# publish --repo OWNER/REPO [--branch NAME] [--message MSG] FILE [FILE...]
# stdout: one line per file: ![<basename>](https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/raw/<sha>/<basename>)
cmd_publish() { ...; return 0; }
```

   Required behaviour of `publish`:
   - Validate `--repo` as `owner/name`; require `gh` authenticated.
   - Refuse if the repo is private unless `--allow-private` is passed (private raw URLs do not render for people without access); read `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO --jq .private`.
   - Refuse if `--branch` is the head branch of any open PR on that repo (`gh pr list --repo OWNER/REPO --head BRANCH --state open`) or equals the default branch — assets must never enter a reviewed branch.
   - Per file: must exist, MIME type image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif or image/webp (`file --mime-type -b`), size ≤ 10 MB; reject duplicate basenames.
   - Create blobs, then a tree. If the branch exists: use its tip commit as `parents[]` and its tree as `base_tree`, then `PATCH refs/heads/BRANCH` with `force=false`. If not: parentless commit, then `POST refs`.
   - After publishing, check each embed URL with `curl -sIL -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}'` and fail if it is not `200 image/*`.
   - Print embeds on stdout; logs on stderr via shared `log_*`.
2. `help` text lists usage, the privacy warning, and the cleanup command.
3. Add to `github-cli.md` a subsection (≤ 15 lines): GitHub has no attachment API; before publishing, view each image and confirm no secrets, private repo names or local private paths are visible (cross-link `reference/pre-push-guards.md`); run the helper against the fork you push from (for upstream PRs) or the repo itself; paste the embeds into `--body-file` content; keep the asset branch while the thread matters; never commit screenshots into the PR branch; resize large captures first (`reference/screenshot-limits.md`).
4. Add the GitLab uploads note to `gitlab-cli.md`.
5. Run ShellCheck and exercise the helper once against a test repo you own (see Verification).

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** two publishes to the same branch race on the ref update; `force=false` makes the loser fail with 422 — report it and tell the user to rerun. No local git state is touched.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; rollback is deleting the helper and the doc lines. Remote asset branches are independent.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** new file only; older deployments simply lack the helper.
- **Idempotency/retry:** rerunning creates a new commit with identical blobs (GitHub deduplicates blob storage); earlier pinned URLs keep working because commits stay reachable on the branch.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** blobs/trees/commits created before a failed ref update are unreferenced and garbage-collected by GitHub; nothing is printed on failure, so no half-valid embeds are pasted. Temp base64 files are removed by a `trap` on exit.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/forge-image-embed-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
.agents/scripts/forge-image-embed-helper.sh help
# Live check against a throwaway public repo you own (not the aidevops repo):
.agents/scripts/forge-image-embed-helper.sh publish --repo <your-login>/<scratch-repo> --branch aidevops-assets-test <any-small.png>
# Negative checks:
.agents/scripts/forge-image-embed-helper.sh publish --repo <your-login>/<scratch-repo> --branch <scratch-repo-default-branch> x.png   # must refuse
.agents/scripts/forge-image-embed-helper.sh publish --repo <your-login>/<scratch-repo> README.md   # must refuse (not an image)
```

- **Surface mapping:** ShellCheck/linters prove shell conventions; the live publish proves the API sequence and URL verification; negative checks prove the default-branch/PR-branch guard and MIME validation.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — new standalone helper plus two docs.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not add image upload to `gh-write-helper.sh` or signature/PR wrappers in this task; do not add browser automation.

**AI brief owner:** maintainer interactive session that filed this task.

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/forge-image-embed-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tools/git/github-cli.md`
- `.agents/tools/git/gitlab-cli.md`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18484-brief.md`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `screenshot embed PR fork asset branch` → 1 hit — the lesson stored in this session (orphan asset branch + commit-pinned raw URL, verified on an upstream PR)
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh --keywords "image attachment PR comment screenshot embed forge"` → 1 recent commit on target docs (138608aa7, unrelated recovery hardening) / 0 merged related PRs / 0 open related PRs; `rg "git/blobs|user-attachments|upload.*screenshot" .agents` finds no existing guidance
- [x] File refs verified: 5 refs checked, all present at HEAD (`.agents/tools/git/github-cli.md` 115 lines, `.agents/tools/git/gitlab-cli.md` 76 lines, `.agents/scripts/screenshot-import-helper.sh` 273 lines, `.agents/reference/screenshot-limits.md`, `.agents/reference/gh-command-discipline.md`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — new helper within a decided design; worker still writes shell logic and error handling

## Origin

- **Session:** opencode:unknown-2026-09-27
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (requested by maintainer)
- **Conversation context:** Adding screenshots to an upstream draft PR needed images in the PR body, but GitHub has no REST/GraphQL API for comment/body attachments (web drag-and-drop only). The working method was: create blobs, a tree, a parentless commit and a ref on a separate asset-only branch of the contributor's fork via `gh api`, then embed commit-pinned `https://github.com/<fork>/raw/<sha>/<file>` URLs. The maintainer asked for this to become reusable framework knowledge for any git-platform post or comment.

## What

1. A new helper, `.agents/scripts/forge-image-embed-helper.sh`, that publishes one or more local images to an asset-only branch of a GitHub repository through the Git Data API, then prints ready-to-paste Markdown image embeds pinned to the commit SHA.
2. Short guidance in `.agents/tools/git/github-cli.md` (and a GitLab note in `.agents/tools/git/gitlab-cli.md`) telling agents when and how to use it, including the privacy check before publishing.

Agents that need screenshots in an issue, PR body, or comment on any GitHub repo (own or upstream) can then run one command instead of inventing the API sequence, and never need browser upload.

## Why

- GitHub exposes no API for issue/PR attachments; agents otherwise either skip screenshots (upstream CONTRIBUTING files often require them for UI changes, e.g. anomalyco/opencode "UI Changes") or ask the human to drag and drop.
- Committing screenshots into the PR branch pollutes upstream diffs; an asset-only branch keeps them out of review.
- The manual sequence is easy to get wrong in restricted shells (OpenCode Bash blocks redirects and command substitution, so base64 content must go through files and `gh api -F content=@file`).

## Tier

### Tier checklist (verify before assigning)

- [ ] **Exact execution contract supplied?** Skeleton and API sequence given; the worker writes the function bodies.
- [x] **Targets and reference pattern verified?**
- [x] **No semantic or design decision remains?**
- [x] **Bounded, reversible, low-consequence impact?**
- [x] **No stateful coordination to invent?**
- [x] **Focused verification and rollback are explicit?**
- [x] **No dispatch-path risk override?** None of the target files are in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`.

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Decided design with a verified API sequence and a reference helper structure; the worker still implements argument parsing, validation and error handling in new shell code.

## PR Conventions

Leaf task: the PR uses `Resolves` with this task's issue number.

## Context & Decisions

- Chosen: Git Data API on an asset-only branch, commit-pinned URLs. Ruled out: committing images into the PR branch (pollutes upstream diffs); gists (binary files need git push, not `gh gist create`); browser drag-and-drop automation (needs authenticated browser, fragile); third-party image hosts (privacy, link rot).
- `raw/<sha>/` URLs are used instead of branch URLs so later pushes to the asset branch cannot change what an existing comment shows.
- GitLab and Gitea have native attachment APIs; only GitHub needs the workaround.
- Prior art: this session's use on an upstream opencode PR (both embeds verified 200 image/png).

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/screenshot-import-helper.sh` — structure to copy.
- `.agents/tools/git/github-cli.md:103` — insertion point after Pre-Submission Checklist.

title: deploy-agents-on-merge: succeed fast when the active runtime bundle already contains the merged SHA instead of waiting out the setup lock
body:
## Problem

`deploy-agents-on-merge.sh` blocks for up to `AIDEVOPS_SETUP_WAIT_TIMEOUT_S` (900s default, `setup.sh` around line 1144) when another `setup.sh --stage ai-session` or `--non-interactive` run holds the setup lock. It does this even when that concurrent deploy already contains, or will install, the merged commit. It then reports a failure, so a deploy that actually succeeded looks like it failed.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: `deploy-agents-on-merge.sh` (full-loop postflight) run as a 900s bounded operation right after merging #32460.

**Actual output**: the operation was terminated at the 900s budget (exit 143) while `setup.sh` waited for the lock: `Another setup.sh --non-interactive is running (pid …). Waiting up to 900s (AIDEVOPS_SETUP_WAIT_TIMEOUT_S)`. Meanwhile the active bundle already contained the merged commit.

**Expected:** return 0 quickly with `already deployed by active bundle 3.37.0-5c7320079798…`.

Steps:

1. With pulse/auto-update active, merge a framework PR and immediately run `deploy-agents-on-merge.sh` (as the full-loop postflight does).
2. While a concurrent `setup.sh` holds the lock, the deploy waits. Observed 2026-09-27 after merging #32460 (`5c73200`): holder pids 44180, 441 and 15943; the bounded operation was killed at 900s (exit 143).
3. In the same window, `~/.aidevops/agents` was re-pointed 3.36.4 → `3.37.0-5c7320079798…` → `3.37.1-19865e0…`. The merged commit was deployed by the concurrent run, and `cmp` of the changed files against the repo matched. Evidence: `~/.aidevops/logs/setup-stage-timings.log`.

## Proposed fix

In `.agents/scripts/deploy-agents-on-merge.sh`, the transactional stage function (the `setup.sh --stage ai-session` call around lines 386-397) and the `--non-interactive` path (around line 715):
- **Before invoking setup:** resolve the active bundle from `readlink ~/.aidevops/agents`. Bundle directories embed the short source SHA, e.g. `3.37.0-5c7320079798-…`. If `git merge-base --is-ancestor <merged-sha> <bundle-sha>` succeeds, log `already deployed by active bundle <name>` and return 0.
- **When the lock is held** (exit 75, or a detected holder before calling): poll the active bundle for up to a bounded interval (for example 120s, configurable), and succeed as soon as a bundle containing the merged SHA becomes active. Otherwise exit 75 with holder pid/command and a clear retry instruction, instead of waiting out the whole 900s ceiling.
- Never skip deployment when the ancestry check cannot be evaluated; fall back to the current behaviour.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-noninteractive-lock.sh`, plus any `rg -l "deploy-agents-on-merge" .agents/scripts/tests` matches.
- Add a case only if an existing fixture can fake the `~/.aidevops/agents` symlink cheaply: an active bundle that already contains the SHA should return 0 without calling setup.
- Runtime: run `deploy-agents-on-merge.sh` right after a concurrent `aidevops update` that includes the merge. It should return quickly with `already deployed`.
- ShellCheck and `linters-local.sh --changed` clean.

Files: `.agents/scripts/deploy-agents-on-merge.sh`; reference: setup lock wait in `setup.sh` (`AIDEVOPS_SETUP_WAIT_TIMEOUT_S`).

title: full-loop merge: canonical sync report says canonical_path_unavailable for PRs without a local worktree
body:
## Problem

After a successful `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, the canonical sync report says `CANONICAL_SYNC_PENDING=true reason=canonical_path_unavailable` whenever the merged PR has no local worktree, for example an external/fork PR merged from a maintainer session. The canonical checkout exists; the helper just never looks it up in that case. The message also gives no next command, so the operator has to find `canonical-recovery-helper.sh` manually.

Root cause: in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`, the merge flow (around lines 1978-1986) resolves `_canonical_dir` only inside the `if [[ -n "$_cleanup_target" ]]` branch, via `_merge_current_canonical_dir_for_cleanup "$_cleanup_worktree"`. When `_merge_fresh_worktree_cleanup_target` returns nothing, `_canonical_dir` stays empty, and `_merge_report_canonical_sync_state` (around line 1611) prints `canonical_path_unavailable`.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: from a maintainer interactive session, merge an external/fork PR that has no local worktree: `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <owner/repo> --squash`

**Actual output**:

```
LIFECYCLE_STATE=MERGED merge_sha=e01527b0e…
CANONICAL_SYNC_PENDING=true reason=canonical_path_unavailable
```

**Expected:** the canonical checkout path is named and reported as either `CANONICAL_SYNCED` or pending with the exact next command.

Observed on PR #32402 (merge `e01527b`). The registered canonical checkout existed and was later synced manually with `canonical-recovery-helper.sh sync-mirror`.

## Proposed fix

- Resolve the canonical directory independently of the cleanup target. Use the first `git worktree list --porcelain` entry from the current repository, or the registered `repos.json` path for the slug. Drop the `!= current_root` restriction when the session is already running in the canonical checkout, since it only matters for cleanup.
- When the sync is pending, print the exact guarded next command documented in `workflows/full-loop.md` §4.7 and `workflows/git-workflow.md`: `canonical-recovery-helper.sh fast-forward-current …` when the checkout is clean and not diverged, otherwise the `sync-mirror` form. Do not run it automatically unless §4.7 already authorizes that for this repo class, and keep all preservation guards.
- Keep `reason=` values for the genuinely unavailable cases.

## Verification

- `rg -l "CANONICAL_SYNC_PENDING|_merge_report_canonical_sync_state" .agents/scripts/tests` and run the matches; extend one with a no-cleanup-target case if a fixture already exists.
- Runtime: merge a PR that has no local worktree; the output should name the canonical path and either `CANONICAL_SYNCED` or the exact next command.
- ShellCheck and `linters-local.sh --changed` clean.

Files: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`.

title: fix(opencode): typed launch in Tabby split tab reattaches to live session via recovery marker cwd
body:
## What

Running `aidevops opencode` (or plain `opencode`) in a Tabby tab that was opened/split from a live aidevops OpenCode tab reattaches to the **already-open** session instead of starting a new one. Two TUIs then drive the same session concurrently.

## Reproducer

1. Open a Tabby profile tab running `aidevops opencode --tabby-shell` in a project; send one message so the session is created.
2. Split or open a new tab from that tab (cwd becomes `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-tabby-recovery/<ses_id>/`).
3. Type `aidevops opencode`.

**Symptom command**: `aidevops opencode` (typed in the split tab)

**Actual output**: the TUI opens the existing `<ses_id>` conversation (already open in the first tab) instead of an empty new session. The marker `recovery.json` in the cwd names that session; the launcher prepends `--session <ses_id>`.

**Expected**: a new session in the recorded project directory.

## Why

Observed in an interactive Tabby session (OpenCode V1 1.18.32, aidevops v3.37.2):

1. While a session runs with `AIDEVOPS_TABBY_SESSION_RECOVERY=1`, `createSessionRecoveryMarkerHandler` writes the marker and emits OSC 1337 `CurrentDir` pointing at the marker directory `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-tabby-recovery/<ses_id>/` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-marker.mjs:247-248`, escape built at `:73`).
2. Tabby uses that CurrentDir as the cwd for any new tab/split from that tab.
3. Typed `aidevops opencode` inside Tabby is auto-promoted to `--tabby-shell` mode (`.agents/scripts/opencode-launcher-helper.sh:260-273`, a self-heal for pre-`--tabby-shell` recovery tokens).
4. `resolve_tabby_recovery` reads `recovery.json` from the cwd and prepends `--session <ses_id>` (`opencode-launcher-helper.sh:1461-1471`). `resolveSessionRecoveryMarker` (`session-recovery-marker.mjs:200-222`) validates marker/DB integrity but never checks whether the session is currently open in another process.
5. Plain `opencode` typed in such a tab runs with the marker directory as its project directory (footer shows the recovery path).

Risk: two front ends writing to one session can interleave/corrupt history; users also lose the "new session" they asked for.

## How

1. **Liveness guard** — in `session-recovery-marker.mjs` `writeSessionRecoveryMarker`, record the owning OpenCode process PID (and a start-time or boot token to resist PID reuse) in the marker (bump `schema_version` or add an optional field accepted by schema 1). In `resolveSessionRecoveryMarker`, if the recorded owner is alive, return a distinct result (e.g. exit status 3 from the CLI `resolve`) meaning "session live — start new session in `marker.directory`".
2. **Launcher handling** — in `opencode-launcher-helper.sh` around lines 1461-1476, on the "live" result set `launch_dir` to the marker's recorded directory and `data_dir` to its data dir but do **not** add `--session`. Genuine Tabby-restart recovery (owner dead) keeps current behaviour.
3. **Cwd hygiene** — when the launcher (tabby-shell or not) is invoked from inside a recovery marker directory, always launch from the recorded project directory rather than the marker directory, and for the post-exit login shell `cd` there too (see tabby-shell exec path ~`opencode-launcher-helper.sh:300-356`).
4. Keep existing symlink/permission/trust checks unchanged.

## Acceptance

- From a live aidevops OpenCode tab in Tabby, split/new tab then `aidevops opencode` → a **new** session in the original project directory; the original session is untouched.
- Quit Tabby entirely with a session open, relaunch Tabby → profile tab still resumes the saved session (owner dead).
- Plain `opencode` in a tab whose cwd is a recovery marker dir no longer uses the marker dir as project (either launcher shim redirects, or document as out of scope if the unmanaged `opencode` path cannot be intercepted).
- Existing tests for the marker/launcher pass: `rg -l "session-recovery-marker|tabby" .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests .agents/scripts/tests` to locate them; `shellcheck .agents/scripts/opencode-launcher-helper.sh` clean.

## Verification

- `node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-marker.mjs resolve --cwd <marker-dir> --work-dir ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work` returns the "live" status while the session's TUI runs, and the resume tuple after it exits.
- `aidevops opencode --dry-run` from a marker dir shows no `--session` while the owner is alive.

## Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-marker.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-launcher-helper.sh`
- Related tests (paths to be located with the `rg` above; not verified here).

title: Agent-workspace tmp has no retention routine; system-cleanup.sh targets obsolete paths and is unscheduled
body:
## Problem

The framework tells agents to put temporary artifacts under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}` (`.agents/AGENTS.md`, "Tool and file discipline"), but no routine prunes that directory. Session scratch directories (issue bodies, snapshots, PR drafts) build up indefinitely. Agents also cannot delete them: the command policy blocks `rm -rf` under home. So sessions end up telling the user to delete them by hand, which contradicts the rule that cleanup is routine-owned.

The only retention code is `.agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh`, and it targets obsolete paths:
- `TMP_DIR="$HOME/.agents/tmp"`, not the agent-workspace tmp directory
- `LOG_DIR="$HOME/.agents/logs"`, `AGENT_DIR="$HOME/.agents"`, `PROJECT_DIR="$HOME/git/aidevops"` (lowercase `git`)
- Nothing schedules or calls it: `rg -l "system-cleanup.sh" .agents setup.sh` matches only the script itself.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: `rg -n "TMP_DIR=|PROJECT_DIR=" .agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh`, then `rg -l "system-cleanup.sh" .agents setup.sh`

**Actual output**: `TMP_DIR="$HOME/.agents/tmp"` and `PROJECT_DIR="$HOME/git/aidevops"`; the only reference is the script itself. Meanwhile an interactive session's `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/<session-scratch>/` directory is never removed, and the agent cannot remove it (`rm -rf` is blocked by command policy).

**Expected**: a scheduled routine prunes stale agent-workspace tmp entries, so sessions can report temp cleanup as automatic.

## Proposed fix

- Point retention at `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`. Prune top-level entries older than a configurable retention period (default 7 days, by mtime). Skip `session-checkpoints/` and anything newer than the retention period. Skip entries referenced by a live session lease or lock if such a registry exists. Use the existing trash-backed deletion helper if one exists instead of raw `rm -rf`.
- Either fix `system-cleanup.sh` (paths from `shared-constants.sh`, drop the stale `PROJECT_DIR`) and schedule it, or fold the tmp pruning into the existing pulse cleanup (`.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`). Prefer whichever already runs on a schedule. Scheduled job naming: launchd `sh.aidevops.<name>`.
- Dry-run by default when invoked manually. Log deletions to `~/.aidevops/logs/`.

## Verification

- Run `shellcheck` and `linters-local.sh --changed`.
- Runtime: create an old scratch directory (`touch -t` to more than 8 days ago) and a fresh one under the tmp root. Run the routine in dry-run mode, then for real. Only the old directory is removed, and `session-checkpoints/` is untouched.
- Run the existing `rg -l "pulse-cleanup|system-cleanup" .agents/scripts/tests` matches.

Files: `.agents/scripts/system-cleanup.sh` and/or `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`, and scheduling in `setup.sh` / routines only if a new job is needed.

title: Document the working invocation for hyphenated Python tests (python3 -m unittest fails with Empty module name)
body:
## Problem

Most Python tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` have hyphenated file names (for example `test-source-access-helper.py`), so they cannot be imported as modules. The usual invocations fail, and there is no documented canonical way to run one test or a filtered subset:
- `python3 -m unittest -k <pattern> .agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py` → `ValueError: Empty module name`
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s .agents/scripts/tests` does not collect hyphenated files (the default pattern is `test*.py` and needs importable names)
- `python3 -m pytest …` → `No module named pytest` (not a framework dependency)

The working form is running the file directly: `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py -k <pattern>`. Agents only find this after one or two failed attempts. Observed while verifying #32460.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: `python3 -m unittest -k trusted .agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py`

**Actual output**: `ValueError: Empty module name`

**Expected**: either the documented command works, or the documentation points to a working command (`python3 <file> [-k pattern]`).

## Proposed fix

Documentation first, lowest cost:
- Add a short "Running Python tests" note in the place agents look when they verify changes. Candidates: `.agents/reference/ci-gate-policy.md` (verification guidance) and a one-line header comment convention in the Python test files. Say to run a hyphenated test file directly (`python3 .agents/scripts/tests/<file>.py [-v] [-k pattern]`), and that pytest is not a dependency.
- Check that each hyphenated test file ends with `unittest.main()` so the direct form works: `rg --files-without-match "unittest.main" .agents/scripts/tests --glob "test-*.py"` (note: `rg -L` follows symlinks, it does not list non-matching files). On 2026-09-27 this listed four files, named in Files Scope below. Add a `__main__` guard only where the file is a unittest module; leave files that are intentionally run another way unchanged and say so in the PR.
- Optional, only if cheap: a tiny runner (for example in `.agents/scripts/tests/`) that loads hyphenated files by path via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` and accepts `-k`. Do not add a new test framework dependency.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/reference/ci-gate-policy.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-operator-subagents.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-config-boundary.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-project-config-restore.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-session-miner-steerage-quality.py`

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py -k trusted` passes.
- The `rg --files-without-match` check above lists no hyphenated unittest files missing `unittest.main()`, or the remaining ones are explained in the PR.

title: Completion guidance: routine-owned cleanup gets one no-action line, never a user task
body:
## Problem

Interactive sessions keep telling the user to clean up things a routine already owns: deferred worktrees and session scratch directories. The guidance says routine-owned cleanup should be silent (`.agents/reference/session.md` Session Lifecycle, and `workflows/full-loop.md` "User-facing completion"). But in practice:
- the agent attempted `worktree-helper.sh remove` on a merged, cleanup-deferred worktree, and when the guarded removal refused, told the user to handle it or run `worktree-helper.sh clean`;
- when the command policy blocked `rm -rf` on a session scratch directory, the agent turned that into a "left for you" item.

The maintainer's preferred behaviour: cleanup happens through routines once sessions close. At most, a completion message should say so in one line that makes clear no action is needed. It should never present routine cleanup as a user task.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: complete an interactive `/full-loop` merge whose cleanup is deferred (`LIFECYCLE_STATE=CLEANUP_DEFERRED`), in a session that also wrote scratch files under the agent-workspace tmp directory.

**Actual output**: the completion message included "Left for you (optional): … worktree … `worktree-helper.sh clean` … delete `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/<scratch>/` when convenient".

**Expected**: either nothing about cleanup, or one line such as `Cleanup: the worktree is removed automatically by a routine after this session closes; no action needed.`

## Change

- `.agents/AGENTS.md` (Completion messages): routine-owned cleanup gets one no-action line unless user action is required or work is at risk (+15 bytes; the file stays under the 24000-byte ratchet).
- `.agents/reference/session.md` (Session Lifecycle): do not attempt deferred cleanup; guarded-removal refusals and command-policy deletion blocks are not user tasks; give the no-action example line; user action only for failures that require it or put unpublished work at risk.
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` (User-facing completion): the same no-action line replaces "silent".
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh`: literals updated, plus new assertions for the no-action line and the blocked-deletion case.

Related: #32485 adds the missing retention routine for agent-workspace tmp, so scratch-directory cleanup is also routine-owned in practice.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh` → PASS
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` → exit 0; markdownlint 0 issues; `wc -c .agents/AGENTS.md` → 23948 (limit 24000)

title: Route session compaction to a cheaper model/effort and measure continuation quality
body:
## What

Route OpenCode session compaction (summary generation) to a cheaper model/effort than the primary session, and measure whether sessions still continue cleanly afterwards.

## Why

A 14-day local observability sample (`~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/llm-requests.db`, 2026-09-27 review under #32484) shows:

- compaction is ~3% of estimated spend;
- each compaction request cost $0.30–2.30 (API-equivalent) with ~0% cache hits, because it re-sends the whole context uncached;
- compaction currently runs on the primary model and effort (GPT-6 Sol medium for the daily driver).

Summarisation is a bounded, extraction-style task, which is the `simple` tier's contract. The risk is poorer checkpoints, and therefore worse continuations, so this needs outcome measurement, not only a config change.

## How

1. Confirm how OpenCode selects the compaction model. The likely surface is the built-in `compaction` agent in OpenCode config (`agent.compaction.model` / `variant`); verify with Context7 OpenCode docs or the installed OpenCode version before assuming. The exact config key is **not yet known**.
2. If supported, register a default in the plugin config hook, following the `registerAgents`/`applyDailyDriverDefaults` pattern in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-agent-profiles.mjs` and `config-hook.mjs`:
   - resolve the model from the routing table's `simple` tier via `routingProfile(routing, "simple")` in `model-routing.mjs`; never hardcode a model ID;
   - preserve any explicit user `agent.compaction` model/variant pin.
3. Check that the cheaper model's context window can accept the compaction input. The plugin caps GPT-6 at a 240K compaction target (`model-limits.mjs`, `context-budget-policy.mjs`). If the simple-tier model cannot take the full pre-compaction context, fall back to the parent model.
4. Measure: compare compaction cost (`llm_requests` rows where the mode is compaction) and continuation quality (first post-compaction turn succeeds without re-reading already-summarised files, and no user correction follows) before and after, over at least one week of normal use. Record the result in `.agents/reference/model-effort-evaluation.md`.

## Files

- EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-hook.mjs` and/or `config-agent-profiles.mjs`: compaction agent default.
- REFERENCE `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-routing.mjs`, `model-limits.mjs`, `compaction.mjs`, `compaction-lifecycle.mjs`.
- EDIT `.agents/tools/context/model-routing.md`: document the compaction route.

## Acceptance

- The compaction model comes from the routing table, and user pins are preserved.
- A context-size guard falls back to the parent model when the cheaper model cannot fit the input.
- Existing plugin tests pass (`node --test` with explicit files: `test-compaction-*.mjs`, `test-model-limits.mjs`, `test-model-routing.mjs`).
- A dated evaluation note records the cost delta and continuation quality evidence, or that the feature is unsupported by the host.

title: Enforce parent acceptance receipts for subagent results via a hook (1.6% coverage today)
body:
## What

Make parent acceptance of subagent results observable by default: prompt for, or infer safely, an `aidevops_objective_receipt` decision after each completed child Task, instead of relying on the model to call the tool voluntarily.

## Why

The tiering and effort review under #32484 (2026-09-27) found that only **8 of 504** recorded interactive subagent dispatches (1.6%) had a parent acceptance/repair receipt. Without receipts, routing feedback cannot tell a verified child contribution from host completion. That blocks evidence-based decisions on whether cheaper child routes (Luna / Sol low) are good enough. See `.agents/reference/model-effort-evaluation.md` for the coverage limits this causes.

Deterministic prompt rules should migrate to hooks (`.agents/AGENTS.md` "Quality and diagnostics"; `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf`).

## How

1. Read `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/objective-receipt-tool.mjs` (tool contract: never infers acceptance from host completion) and its registration in `index.mjs:429` / `v2.mjs:303`.
2. Read the Task tool after-hook path in `subagent-effort-escalation.mjs` (`host_outcome` recording) to find where a child completion is known together with its `callID`/child session ID.
3. Implement the lowest-friction enforcement that keeps the tool's "explicit decision only" contract:
   - Preferred: after a completed child Task, append a short synthetic reminder to the tool output. It should name the `contribution_id`/`run_id` values the parent needs so a receipt call is a copy, not a lookup.
   - Do **not** auto-record `accepted_*`. Recording `unknown` when a session ends without a decision is acceptable if it is clearly labelled as inferred absence.
4. Keep the reminder short (token cost on every child return) and skip it for pinned or advisory-only children if that is already distinguishable.
5. Add an entry to `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf` marking this rule as migrated.

## Files

- EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-effort-escalation.mjs` (or a new small module it calls, to avoid Qlty complexity regressions).
- REFERENCE `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/objective-receipt-tool.mjs`, `observability.mjs` (`recordObjectiveDecision`).
- EDIT `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf`.

## Acceptance

- Each completed child Task output carries a receipt reminder with the identifiers needed.
- No acceptance is inferred from host completion.
- The existing plugin tests pass (`node --test` with explicit files: `test-subagent-effort.mjs`, `test-observability-routing-join.mjs`, `test-routing-feedback.mjs`).
- A local qlty smell check (`qlty smells --no-snippets <changed files>`) shows no new findings.
- After one week, the receipt coverage ratio (`runtime_events` receipts ÷ interactive child dispatches in `llm-requests.db`) is reported on this issue or in `model-effort-evaluation.md`.

title: Evaluate a primary-session compaction target below 240K for interactive cost
body:
## What

Evaluate whether a primary-session compaction target below the current 240K tokens lowers interactive cost without hurting task continuity, and change the default only if the evidence supports it.

## Why

The 2026-09-27 cost review under #32484 (14-day local observability, API-equivalent estimates) found:

- primary sessions are ~90% of estimated spend;
- each primary request re-reads 140K–255K cached tokens;
- reasoning is under 1% of tokens, so effort barely changes per-request cost.

Context size, not model effort, therefore drives main-session cost. Every turn pays for the whole cached context, so a lower compaction target reduces the per-turn cost of long sessions. The trade-offs are more frequent compactions (each ~$0.30–2.30 with ~0% cache hits) and possible loss of working detail.

## How

1. Read the current targets and their overrides:
   - `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-limits.mjs` (`GPT6_COMPACTION_TARGET`, `ASTRA_COMPACTION_BUDGET_TARGET` = 240000);
   - `context-budget-policy.mjs` (`target: 240000`, 500K for newer Anthropic models);
   - `context-budget.mjs` / `context-budget-gpt6.mjs`, including user-selectable targets and the opt-out.
2. Using `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/llm-requests.db` (`llm_requests`), model the cost of historical primary sessions at candidate targets (for example 160K and 200K):
   - per-turn cached-input cost (assume linear context growth between compactions);
   - plus the extra compaction count × the observed median compaction cost.
   - This is a replay estimate from existing telemetry; do not build new benchmark infrastructure.
3. If a lower target is materially cheaper (> 10% of primary spend), propose it as an opt-in selection first, via the existing user-selectable target mechanism. Record continuity evidence (post-compaction re-reads, user corrections) before changing the shipped default.
4. Coordinate with the sibling issue that routes compaction to a cheaper model, which changes the compaction cost term.

## Files

- REFERENCE/EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-limits.mjs`, `context-budget-policy.mjs`, `context-budget-gpt6.mjs`.
- EDIT `.agents/reference/model-effort-evaluation.md`: dated analysis and decision.
- EDIT `.agents/tools/context/model-routing.md` only if the default changes.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/reference/model-effort-evaluation.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-limits.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/context-budget-policy.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/context-budget-gpt6.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/context-budget.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/tools/context/model-routing.md`

The plugin files and `model-routing.md` change only when the evidence supports a new opt-in or default; an analysis-only outcome edits `model-effort-evaluation.md` alone.

## Acceptance

- A dated analysis in `model-effort-evaluation.md` gives cost estimates per candidate target, including the added compaction cost, and states its assumptions.
- The default changes only with that evidence. Otherwise it is an opt-in selection, or the issue closes with the rationale.
- Existing tests pass (`node --test` with explicit files: `test-gpt56-context-config.mjs`, `test-model-limits.mjs`, `test-context-budget.mjs`, `test-v2-context-budget.mjs`).

title: OpenCode V2 parity: load framework AGENTS.md, sanitize service restart env, leave Tabby recovery dirs
body:
## Problem

After the GH#32444 release (v3.37.1/v3.37.2), a user test showed OpenCode V2 (`opencode2`) does not load everything OpenCode 1 loads, and one V2 session skipped the aidevops greeting.

Evidence gathered from the V2 session database, the V2 server log and the shared plugin log:

1. **V2 never loads the framework user guide.** OpenCode 1 loads `~/.aidevops/agents/AGENTS.md` (~24 KB, the Framework Rules) through `instructions` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. The isolated V2 config (`~/.aidevops/runtimes/opencode-v2/config/opencode/opencode.json`) only has `plugins`, and there is no `AGENTS.md` in the V2 config dir. V2 sessions therefore run without the framework rules (git safety, completion discipline, security rules). V2 does watch and load `<V2 config>/opencode/AGENTS.md`: a probe with a symlinked canary `AGENTS.md` in a copied config home produced a `core/instructions` entry and the canary reply.
2. **The V2 background service inherits the environment of whatever process restarted it.** `_restart_opencode_v2_service_after_deploy` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh`) runs `opencode2 service restart`, and the shim passes the full caller environment through. The live service after the last deploy carries an unrelated OpenCode 1 session's `OPENCODE_PID`, `AIDEVOPS_OPERATION_ID`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` pinned to a days-old 3.34.33 runtime bundle. If a deploy runs from a headless context, `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS`/`AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS`/`OPENCODE_HEADLESS` leak in too, and `isHeadless()` then suppresses the greeting (and changes other interactive behaviour) for every V2 session until the next restart. The affected session's request had 5 redistributed system blocks versus 6 for otherwise identical sessions; the ~1.6K-char difference matches the greeting block. The previous service process is gone, so its exact environment cannot be confirmed.
3. **`opencode2` starts inside Tabby recovery marker directories.** OpenCode 1 reports `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-tabby-recovery/<session>/` to Tabby as the tab's current directory (OSC 1337). Tabs opened from that tab start their shell there, and `opencode2` then creates a session in the marker directory. That session misses the project `AGENTS.md` and runs tools in the wrong directory. The OpenCode 1 launcher resolves markers (`resolve_tabby_recovery` in `.agents/scripts/opencode-launcher-helper.sh`); the V2 shim does not.
4. **Greeting skips are not observable.** `ttsrSystemTransform` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/ttsr.mjs`) silently omits the greeting when disabled or when `shouldInjectGreeting` returns false, so the cause of a missing greeting cannot be read from logs.

## Proposed fix

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh` (or the V2 setup path in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`): ensure `<V2 config>/opencode/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `~/.aidevops/agents/AGENTS.md`. Never replace a user-authored regular file.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh` `_setup_write_opencode_v2_shim`:
  - for service lifecycle commands (`service …`, `serve --service`), drop session-scoped and headless variables before exec;
  - when started inside a validated recovery marker directory, `cd` to the marker's recorded project directory (never resume the OpenCode 1 session in V2);
  - bump a shim version marker so existing shims are regenerated.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh` `_restart_opencode_v2_service_after_deploy`: restart with the same sanitized environment.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/ttsr.mjs`: log one line per session when the greeting is skipped, with the reason (`disabled`/`headless-or-child`).
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`: update the greeting-source comment (the V2 config `AGENTS.md` is the framework guide, not a greeting fallback, so the plugin greeting stays the default).

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh` covers the symlink, the regular-file guard, the shim version marker, service environment sanitization, and recovery-directory redirection.
- Relevant plugin tests for the greeting-skip log.
- Live check after deploy:
  - a fresh `opencode2` session's `instruction_state` includes `core/instructions` containing the framework guide;
  - `opencode2 service restart` from a shell with `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1` yields a service without that variable (`ps -E`);
  - `opencode2` launched from a marker directory opens in the project directory;
  - the greeting still appears exactly once.

Ref #32444

title: fix(opencode): context7 on-demand MCP activation and V2 terminal title version suffix
body:
## What

Two gaps found while verifying OpenCode V1 1.18.32 / V2 2.0.3 with aidevops v3.37.2:

1. **Context7 cannot be connected on demand.** `context7` is registered disabled (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs`, remote `https://mcp.context7.com/mcp`) but has no `activationAgent`, so `aidevops_mcp` rejects it and no Context7 tools are reachable in V1 or V2 sessions. Build+ lists `context7` as its library-docs path.
2. **V2 terminal title lacks `· AIDevOps <version>`.** V1 stores the suffix in the session title (`session-title-suffix.mjs`). V2 titles come from `v2-plugin/tui.mjs`, which renders status dots but no version suffix.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: in an `opencode2` (or `opencode`) session, ask "start the context7 MCP"; observe the Tabby tab title in `opencode2`.

**Actual output**: agent reports `aidevops_mcp` only accepts playwriter, posthog, playwright, quickfile, mobile-mcp, blender-lab, affinity-studio, freecad, ableton, davinci-resolve, backblaze-b2; sidebar lists `context7 Disabled`. V2 tab title is `🟢 Greeting` while V1 shows `Greeting · AIDevOps 3.37.2`.

## How

- `mcp-registry.mjs`: give `context7` `activationAgent: "context7"`, `agentSource: ["tools","context","context7.md"]`, `modelTier: "simple"`, untrusted-content and CLI-fallback guidance. It stays disconnected at startup and tools stay scoped to the `context7` agent, matching the PostHog pattern.
- `v2-plugin/tui.mjs`: append the suffix (via `withAidevopsTitleSuffix`) to the terminal title only (V2 session titles double as tab labels), reading `~/.aidevops/agents/VERSION` at most once per minute.

## Acceptance

- `@context7` can `aidevops_mcp connect context7` and use `context7_*` tools; other agents do not get them.
- V2 terminal title shows `<dot> <title> · AIDevOps <version>`.

## Verification

`node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-context7-mcp-registry.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-tui-title.mjs`

title: bug(release): exact-tag deployment gate rejects active bundle when main advanced before publication merge
body:
## Problem

The post-release exact-tag deployment gate rejects a valid active runtime bundle when `main` moved forward while a release was in progress. Publication succeeds, but the release lane stays in `exact-tag-deployment` with no terminal receipt, and the local agents stay on the previous VERSION label.

## Reproducer

Observed on v3.37.3, source PR #32474. Release tag `dbfed4421` (base `7d6e75664`). Before publication merged, another session deployed the runtime bundle from `main` commit `b91c0a895` (GH#32488), which changed `.agents/AGENTS.md`. Publication PR #32497 merged as `8179fe777`, with parents `8c70b3879` (main, which descends from `b91c0a895`) and `c89b5ad98` (release side).

**Symptom command**:

```
aidevops release reconcile 32474
```

**Actual output**:

```
Post-release squash recovery rejected active source b91c0a895dff: changed path is not identical in release: .agents/AGENTS.md
Post-release deployment gate rejected active source b91c0a895dff: it is neither ancestry-related nor a lane-authorized squash-integrated source
PARTIAL RELEASE SUCCESS: GitHub release v3.37.3 remains published; post-publication gates failed
```

The gate recognises the protected integration merge and takes the `stale_runtime=1` path (exit 76 plus a recorded `stale_runtime_recovery`). The next deployment from a descendant then converges the lane, and #32474's release receipt moves to `release:published`.

Impact note: until #32512 (merged in #32513), this left the public lane in `exact-tag-deployment` and blocked `aidevops update` and auto-update for every git install.

## Root cause

In `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh:747-757`, `_verify_protected_release_integration` accepts only a protected-main merge whose two parents are exactly `active_sha` and `release_sha`. When `main` advances past the active source before the publication merge, the integration merge's first parent is a descendant of `active_sha`, not `active_sha` itself. The check then falls through to `_verify_squash_integrated_active_source` (lines 761-793), which rightly rejects the post-base path changes.

## Expected

If both `active_sha` and `release_sha` are ancestors of protected `origin/main`, and a protected merge exists whose first-parent history contains `active_sha` and whose other parent contains `release_sha`, treat the active source as release-integrated. That is the `stale_runtime=1` path, which redeploys from the integrated tree. Unrelated or unmerged active sources must still be rejected.

## Worker Guidance

- **Files:** `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh` (`_verify_protected_release_integration`). Tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh`, which already covers these error messages.
- **Pattern:** keep the `#aidevops:trust-boundary` semantics. Require protected `origin/main` ancestry for both SHAs. Accept a merge `M` on `--ancestry-path release..main` where `release` is an ancestor of one parent and `active` is an ancestor of the other.
- **Verification:**
  - Add a regression fixture: active commit on main, then main advances, then a publication merge of the release branch. The gate must pass.
  - Keep a negative fixture where the active source is not on protected main. It must still be rejected.
  - Then `aidevops release reconcile 32474` should converge the lane for v3.37.3.
