title: Worker metrics readers count future-dated (year 2100) fixture rows as live successes
body:
## What

Worker outcome readers must ignore metric rows timestamped in the future. Existing future-dated rows should also be quarantined, not counted.

## Why

The first two lines of the production `~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` are test-fixture rows with `"ts":4102444800` (2100-01-01). They have no `session_key`, `issue_number` or `repo_slug`, and `result=success`. Every rolling window (`worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 1h|24h|7d`, pulse capacity and success-rate readers) includes them, so each window reports 2 successes that never happened. Retention by age also keeps them forever. The same sentinel value is used intentionally in test fixtures, for example `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-activity-helper.sh:145` (`T_FUTURE_SENTINEL`). At some point a test run wrote to the real metrics path instead of its fixture override.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**

```bash
rg -n '"ts":4102444800' ~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl
```

**Actual output**

```text
1:{"ts":4102444800,"role":"worker","model":"openai/gpt-5.4","result":"success","activity":true,"duration_ms":45000,"exit_code":0}
2:{"ts":4102444800,"role":"worker","model":"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6","result":"success","activity":true,"duration_ms":240000,"exit_code":0}
```

## How

- Reader guard: in the window filters of `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh` and the pulse capacity/diagnose readers that consume this ledger, exclude rows where `ts > now + 300`. Report them as a count of `future_dated_ignored`.
- Producer: find which test writes to the default ledger path without the metrics-path override, and make it use a temporary path. Where it can't be found, record the search you did. Candidates are tests that emit `openai/gpt-5.4` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` success rows without a session key.
- Do not hand-edit the live ledger. The reader guard makes the existing rows harmless.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-issue.sh` (actual issue metrics reader: exclude future attempts; verify issue diagnosis)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-terminal-health.py` (actual capacity metrics reader: bound time before success/failure counting; verify existing worker health tests)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-activity-helper.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Rows with `ts` more than 5 minutes in the future do not count in any rolling window or success rate, and the summary reports how many were ignored.
- Current-time and past rows are counted exactly as before. The existing `T_FUTURE_SENTINEL` fixture behaviour stays deliberate and tested.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-activity-helper.sh`
- `worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 1h` on the live ledger no longer includes the two 2100-dated successes.

title: Mesh remote workers: transport-neutral OpenCode workers over Nostr VPN/NetBird, nvpn setup helper
body:
## Goal

Make OpenCode remote workers over a private mesh (Nostr VPN, self-hosted NetBird, plain SSH/WireGuard) a first-class, transport-neutral aidevops path. Prefer decentralised or self-hosted coordination and peer-to-peer traffic over third-party coordination servers.

## Evidence (from #23846 live validation)

- `remote-dispatch-helper.sh` supports only `--transport ssh|tailscale` and auto-classifies any `100.x.x.x` address as Tailscale. NetBird also assigns addresses in `100.64.0.0/10` (the validated peer was `100.75.13.55`), so a NetBird peer is mislabelled. With the `tailscale` CLI installed, dispatch would use `tailscale ssh` against a non-Tailscale peer.
- Nostr VPN enrollment, aliases (MagicDNS) and the NetBird port fix took many manual steps: `nvpn` has no alias command, and alias changes needed hand edits on each device.
- nvpn 4.1.16 defaults include third-party bootstrap peers (`fips1.iris.to`, `fips2.iris.to`) and public Nostr relay discovery. This isn't documented, and neither is a direct-only mode.
- `netbird.md` and `remote-dispatch.md` don't cover the validated SSH-forward OpenCode pattern or the NetBird/nvpn coexistence.

## Files

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/nostr-vpn-helper.sh`: add `setup-admin`, `join`, `approve`, `set-alias`, `dns-check`, `direct-only`.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/remote-dispatch-helper.sh`: add `netbird|nvpn|wireguard` transports (plain SSH); treat `100.x.x.x` as Tailscale only when `tailscale status` lists it.
- NEW `.agents/reference/mesh-remote-workers.md`: transport comparison and the worker/OpenCode pattern.
- EDIT `.agents/services/networking/{netbird,nostr-vpn}.md`, `.agents/tools/containers/remote-dispatch.md`, `.agents/reference/domain-index.md`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on changed scripts, and the existing plus new focused tests.
- Live: `direct-only` between two Macs keeps `mesh_ready: true` with no non-roster FIPS peers. `remote-dispatch-helper.sh add … --transport netbird` then `check` succeeds.
- `linters-local.sh --changed`.

Ref #23846

title: chore: remove Closte hosting integration (supersedes GH#30503 legacy-only decision)
body:
## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `Closte removal legacy hosting wp-helper` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 2 commits in the last 48h touch target files (`61f09b057` added an unrelated migration to `migrations.sh`; `9474bdf26` regenerated `subagent-index.toon`); 0 open PRs mention Closte; no open Closte issue
- [x] File refs verified: 33 files matched by `git grep -i -l closte origin/main` at `05ff8d3d1` (2026-09-27); line numbers below are from that commit
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. The removal decision, compatibility policy and orphan cleanup pattern are decided below; the worker still edits about 30 files and adjusts shared helpers and tests
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped, because the work is a mechanical sweep and a seed adds no signal

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-27
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (maintainer-approved)
- **Conversation context:** While refreshing the aidevops.sh landing page, the maintainer confirmed that Closte should be removed from aidevops entirely. The website already dropped it (marcusquinn/aidevops.sh PR 173: "Retired integrations are removed, not badged (Closte, September 2026)").

## What

Remove the Closte hosting integration from the framework. Delete the helper, the guide and the config template. Remove Closte from hosting and WordPress helpers, recommendations, provider docs, the URL allowlist, the subagent index and the tests. Existing installs lose their orphaned deployed copies on the next `setup.sh` run. Afterwards `git grep -i closte` finds only historical records (`CHANGELOG.md`, `todo/PLANS.md`) and the one deprecated-path cleanup entry.

## Why

Closte has been legacy-only since t18303 (GH#30503), and the maintainer no longer uses or recommends it. Keeping it costs context tokens (the subagent index, docs and recommendation tables load it), adds allowlist surface and leaves helper branches nobody exercises. `closte-helper.sh` is still a "Placeholder for future implementation" stub.

**This supersedes the GH#30503 instruction** "Do not remove Closte helpers, configuration examples, allowed URLs, or mutation safeguards". The maintainer reversed that decision on 2026-09-27.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The removal and compatibility policy are decided and every target is listed. The worker still edits shared shell helpers (`servers-helper.sh`, `wp-helper.sh`) and existing tests, which needs judgement beyond verbatim replacement. None of the targets are in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`.

## How (Approach)

### Worker Quick-Start

```bash
# Full target list (expect 33 files before, 3 after: CHANGELOG.md, todo/PLANS.md, migrations.sh)
git grep -i -l closte
# Orphan-cleanup precedent: cleanup_deprecated_paths() deprecated_paths list
git grep -n "GH#5155" -- .agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh
# Regenerate the subagent index after deleting the guide (do not hand-edit)
.agents/scripts/subagent-index-helper.sh generate
```

### Files to Modify

**Delete:**
- `.agents/scripts/closte-helper.sh` (stub: "Placeholder for future implementation")
- `.agents/services/hosting/closte.md`
- `configs/closte-config.json.txt`

**Shell helpers and tests:**
- `.agents/scripts/servers-helper.sh:35-36,77,129,203,239`: remove the `closte` case arm, the list and help lines, and `closte` from the `hostinger | hetzner | closte | ...` alternation.
- `.agents/scripts/wp-helper.sh`:
  - `:8` header: drop "Closte".
  - `:195` `check_sshpass` message: "Hostinger/Closte" becomes "password-based SSH".
  - `:326` `hostinger | closte)` becomes `hostinger)`.
  - `:340-346`: remove the `closte_password` default-path `else` branch (only `hostinger_password` remains).
  - `:710` help `Hosting Types`: remove the `closte` line.
  - `*)` "Unknown hosting type" branch: also print the supported types (`localwp, hostinger, hetzner, cloudways, cloudron`) so a leftover `"type": "closte"` site gets actionable guidance.
- `.agents/scripts/coderabbit-pro-analysis.sh:76`: `Hostinger, Hetzner, Closte` becomes `Hostinger, Hetzner`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-init-project-context.sh:185-189`: remove the Closte guide assertions (the file is deleted). Keep the surrounding test's other assertions intact.
- `tests/test-smoke-help.sh:111`: remove `"closte-helper.sh"` from the helper list.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh` `cleanup_deprecated_paths()` (list at about `:146-185`): add `"$agents_dir/scripts/closte-helper.sh"` and `"$agents_dir/services/hosting/closte.md"` under a comment `# GH#<this issue>: Closte integration removed`. rsync only adds and overwrites, so deployed installs keep orphans without this (see the GH#5155 comment at `:169`).

**Config templates and allowlists:**
- `.agents/configs/wordpress-sites.json.txt:87-98,106`: remove the `closte-site` example and the `_hosting_types.closte` entry. Keep the JSON valid.
- `configs/wordpress-sites-config.json.txt:70-82,128`: remove the `closte-site` example and the `WP_CLOSTE_APP_PASSWORD` example line. Keep the JSON valid.
- `.agents/configs/allowed-urls.txt:113,197,304`: remove `app.closte.com`, `closte.com` and `docs.closte.com`.
- `.agents/configs/simplification-state.json:3328`: remove the `.agents/services/hosting/closte.md` key. Keep the JSON valid.
- `.gitignore:24`: remove `closte_*`.
- `.agents/subagent-index.toon:55`: regenerate with `subagent-index-helper.sh generate`, not by hand.

**Docs** (remove the Closte mention or row; reword the surrounding sentence so it still reads naturally):
- `.agents/aidevops/recommendations.md:23,55,65,148,202`:
  - l.23 drops "; Closte is legacy-only".
  - l.55 drops the "Retain Closte guidance…" sentence.
  - l.65 removes the table row.
  - l.148 heading becomes "Password Authentication (Hostinger)".
  - l.202 removes `"closte": 8084` and fixes the trailing comma so the example stays valid JSON.
- `.agents/aidevops.md`
- `.agents/aidevops/{api-integrations,configs,docs,providers,requirements,service-links,services}.md`
- `.agents/content/guidelines.md`

**Leave intact (history):** `CHANGELOG.md` and `todo/PLANS.md`.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:**
  - `servers-helper.sh` dispatches to `closte-helper.sh`; after removal, `closte` is an unknown server.
  - `wp-helper.sh` reads `type` from the user's `wordpress-sites.json`.
  - `tests/test-smoke-help.sh` iterates the helper list.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** None. `closte-helper.sh` is a stub with no mutations.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `tests/test-smoke-help.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-init-project-context.sh`, `wp-helper.sh help`, `servers-helper.sh help`.
- **Schemas/config:** `wordpress-sites.json.txt` and `wordpress-sites-config.json.txt` templates (JSON validity). User copies under the aidevops config dir are not rewritten.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:**
  - `.agents/subagent-index.toon` is regenerated by the helper.
  - Deployed `~/.aidevops/agents/**` copies are removed via `cleanup_deprecated_paths()`.
  - `.wiki/Providers.md` is edited in place.
- **Migrations/backfills:** Only the deprecated-path cleanup. No config rewriting, because user `wordpress-sites.json` files are user-owned.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Revert the PR. Deployed files come back on the next `setup.sh` because the cleanup list only deletes paths that the new release no longer ships.

### Implementation Steps

1. Delete the three files, then apply the edits above file by file.
2. Add the two deprecated paths to `cleanup_deprecated_paths()`.
3. Run `.agents/scripts/subagent-index-helper.sh generate` and confirm the `services/hosting` line no longer lists `closte`.
4. Run `git grep -i -n closte` and confirm only the three expected files match.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** None. These are static docs and helpers; no locks or shared state.
- **Migration/rollback:** Existing `wordpress-sites.json` sites with `"type": "closte"` stop working. They get the improved "Unknown hosting type" error that lists supported types; password-SSH hosts can use `hostinger`-style fields (`ssh_password_env` or `password_file`) and SSH-key hosts can use `hetzner`. User config is deliberately not rewritten. The maintainer's install has no Closte-typed sites.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** An older deployed `servers-helper.sh` may still reference `closte-helper.sh` until setup runs. Setup deploys the new helper and removes the orphan in the same run.
- **Idempotency/retry:** `cleanup_deprecated_paths()` already guards with `[[ -e ]]`, so re-runs are no-ops.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** If setup is interrupted, the orphaned files stay harmless (stub and doc) and the next run removes them.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
git grep -i -l closte                      # expect only CHANGELOG.md, todo/PLANS.md, .agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh
bash tests/test-smoke-help.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-init-project-context.sh
.agents/scripts/wp-helper.sh help | grep -ci closte    # expect 0
.agents/scripts/servers-helper.sh help | grep -ci closte    # expect 0
jq empty .agents/configs/wordpress-sites.json.txt configs/wordpress-sites-config.json.txt .agents/configs/simplification-state.json
.agents/scripts/subagent-index-helper.sh check
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:**
  - `git grep` proves the sweep is complete.
  - The smoke and init tests prove the edited tests still pass.
  - The `help` checks prove the user-facing helpers are clean.
  - `jq` proves the templates are still valid.
  - `subagent-index-helper.sh check` proves the index is in sync.
  - `linters-local.sh --changed` covers ShellCheck and markdown.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required. No shared contracts or release infrastructure change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/closte-helper.sh`
- `.agents/services/hosting/closte.md`
- `configs/closte-config.json.txt`
- `configs/wordpress-sites-config.json.txt`
- `.agents/scripts/servers-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/wp-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/coderabbit-pro-analysis.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-init-project-context.sh`
- `tests/test-smoke-help.sh`
- `.agents/configs/wordpress-sites.json.txt`
- `.agents/configs/allowed-urls.txt`
- `.agents/configs/simplification-state.json`
- `.agents/subagent-index.toon`
- `.gitignore`
- `.wiki/Providers.md`
- `.agents/aidevops.md`
- `.agents/aidevops/*.md`
- `.agents/content/guidelines.md`
- `.agents/tools/deployment/hosting-comparison.md`
- `.agents/tools/wordpress.md`
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/*.md`
- `.agents/workflows/conversation-starter.md`

**Hard boundaries:** Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md` or `todo/PLANS.md`. Do not rewrite user config files. Do not change other hosting providers' behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Only historical records and the cleanup entry mention Closte.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "! git grep -i -l closte | grep -v -x -e CHANGELOG.md -e todo/PLANS.md -e .agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh"
  ```

- [ ] `setup.sh` removes deployed orphans: `cleanup_deprecated_paths()` lists `scripts/closte-helper.sh` and `services/hosting/closte.md`.

  ```yaml

    method: codebase
    pattern: "agents_dir/services/hosting/closte.md"
    path: ".agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Negative: other hosting types are unaffected. `wp-helper.sh` still handles `hostinger`, `hetzner`, `cloudways`, `cloudron` and `localwp`, and `hostinger` keeps its `hostinger_password` default.

  ```yaml

    method: codebase
    pattern: "hostinger_password"
    path: ".agents/scripts/wp-helper.sh"
  ```

- [ ] `tests/test-smoke-help.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-init-project-context.sh` pass. `linters-local.sh --changed` is clean. The three JSON files parse.

## Context & Decisions

- Remove the integration rather than badge or deprecate it: this matches the website policy "Retired integrations are removed, not badged".
- Do not rewrite user configs; improve the unknown-type error instead. User-owned config should not be mutated for a provider with no known active estates.
- Reference removal pattern: GH#31203 (`d60c362dd`, "remove remaining Auggie MCP integrations"). Closte has no MCP or app-config entries, so only the deprecated-path cleanup part applies.

title: fix(planning): clear stale publication:pending when a task issue closes before publication reconciliation
body:
## Problem

`publication:pending` is left permanently on closed issues. On `marcusquinn/aidevops`, **28 closed issues** carry it and **none are open** (`gh issue list --state closed --label publication:pending --limit 500`). The label no longer blocks anything on a closed issue, but it tells anyone scanning labels that the task's planning was never published, which is false. Examples: #32462, #32447, #32438, #32422, #32420, #32415, #31971, #31199.

## Root cause (verified on #32422 / t18480)

Issue timeline and main history:

```
21:13:30Z  labeled publication:pending        (claim-task-id at interactive task creation)
21:57:27Z  98b2438c8 lands on main            (squash of the PR; contains the TODO.md `ref:GH#32422` entry)
21:57:28Z  issue closed                       (PR `Resolves #32422`)
21:58:00Z  labeled status:done / solved:interactive
```

For interactive full-loop tasks, the TODO/brief entry reaches the default branch in the **same squash merge** that closes the issue. The only paths that clear the label ignore closed issues:

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh:242`: `cmd_reconcile` lists only `--state open --label publication:pending`.
- `.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh:153` and `:174`: `_publication_reconcile_one` requires `.state == "OPEN"`.
- `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml:295-305` runs the reconciler on the merge push, but the issue is already closed about 1 s later, so it is skipped.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1266` (`_repair_pending_planning_publications`) calls the same open-only reconciler.

The same stranding happens whenever an issue closes (merged, duplicate, not planned) before reconciliation succeeds, for example when brief readiness fails as in #32542.

## Proposed fix

Add a terminal `CLOSED` transition. On a closed issue, `publication:pending` has no dispatch meaning, because pulse only dispatches open issues.

1. **Close path (primary):** where completion labels are applied (`status:done` + `solved:*`: see `.agents/scripts/solved-attribution-helper.sh` and the `solved:*` handling in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`), remove `publication:pending` in the same edit when the live issue state is `CLOSED`.
2. **Bounded sweep (backfill + safety net):** add a `sweep-closed` subcommand to `planning-publication-reconcile.sh`. It lists `--state closed --label publication:pending` up to a limit (reuse `AIDEVOPS_PUBLICATION_RECONCILE_LIMIT`), re-reads each issue, confirms `state == CLOSED`, and removes only that label via `gh_issue_edit_safe`. Call it from `_repair_pending_planning_publications` in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`, respecting the existing per-repo cap. The first pulse cycles backfill the 28 issues here and any in other managed repos.
3. **Audit:** removing this label must not raise a security-anomaly issue. Check how `gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq` (see `expected_planning_publication_transition`, l.117-134) and the audit helper's `suspicious` classification treat `publication:pending` removal. If it is flagged, add a narrow expected transition: caller is the new function, before-state has the label, after-state lacks it, the issue is closed, and no other label, title or body delta. Mark the check with `#aidevops:trust-boundary`, following `_gh_audit_verify_planning_publication_transition` in `shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh:386`.
4. **Reopen safety:** confirm that a reopened issue whose canonical task is **absent** from the default branch cannot become dispatchable just because the label was removed at close. Check the reopen normalization path and `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`. If it could, only remove the label when the TODO `ref:GH#N` entry exists on the default branch, or restore it on reopen.
5. **Docs:** add the `CLOSED` terminal state to the state model in `.agents/reference/planning-publication-lifecycle.md` (l.65-87). The existing "Do not bulk-label historical work" note (l.243) is about adding labels, not removing them.

Keep new logic in small functions; do not grow `_publication_reconcile_one` (already long).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/solved-attribution-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/planning-publication-lifecycle.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publication-reconcile.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-solved-attribution-helper.sh`

`dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` is in scope only if step 4 shows a reopen path can make the issue dispatchable; otherwise leave it unchanged.

## Acceptance

- Closing an issue that carries `publication:pending` leaves no `publication:pending` once completion labels are applied.
- `planning-publication-reconcile.sh sweep-closed --repo marcusquinn/aidevops` clears all 28 existing instances. A second run makes no mutations.
- Open-issue behaviour is unchanged: the open reconciler still removes the blocker last and only after default-branch validation.
- No new security-anomaly issues are filed for these removals.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publication-reconcile.sh   # add closed-issue sweep + idempotency fixtures
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-solved-attribution-helper.sh        # close-path removal
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh        # open pending issues still blocked
shellcheck .agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh .agents/scripts/solved-attribution-helper.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
gh issue list -R marcusquinn/aidevops --state closed --label publication:pending --json number --jq length   # 0 after sweep
```

title: browser-qa-helper misses the Playwright runtime installed by aidevops setup
body:
## Observed

`browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot` failed with "Playwright Node package is not importable", even though a working Playwright package and matching browser were already on the machine. They came from the setup step `npx -y playwright@latest install` (`setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh:384`).

- Working pair present: `~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/playwright` (1.62.1, root spec `playwright@^1.62.1`) plus `~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1234`.
- With `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE` pointed at that copy, `playwright-runtime.mjs status` reports `packageImportable: true` and `browserBinaryAvailable: true`.
- Without the variable, the resolver fails. As a result, an agent installed a duplicate Playwright copy and downloaded another ~650 MB of Chromium, which had to be cleaned up afterwards.

## Root cause

`scripts/playwright-runtime.mjs`:

- `resolutionAnchors()` looks only next to the script, in the current directory, and in `node_modules/.bin` entries on `PATH`.
- `resolveViaNpx()` runs `npx --no-install --package playwright ...`. npx keys its cache by the exact package spec, so a copy cached as `playwright@latest` / `playwright@^x.y.z` is not reused for the bare `playwright` spec, and `--no-install` then fails.

This follows #30472, which added the resolver.

## Expected

The helper finds the Playwright copy installed by aidevops's own setup, or setup installs Playwright where the resolver looks. It should never tell agents to install a second copy while a usable one exists.

## Suggested fix (smallest)

Pick one:

1. Have setup install the browser-QA Playwright runtime into one stable, framework-owned location that `resolutionAnchors()` includes.
2. Or make `resolveViaNpx()` use the same spec that setup uses (e.g. `playwright@latest`).

Also consider:

- Making the "not importable" error point to `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE` and the supported install path, so agents stop installing ad-hoc copies.
- Using the system Chrome (`channel: "chrome"`) as a fallback, since Playwright MCP already relies on it and Brave is often absent on Linux.

## Verification

On a machine where only the setup-installed npx copy and its browser exist, `browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --url <local> --viewports desktop` succeeds without setting any environment variable.

title: fix: consolidation successors must carry a canonical Files Scope
body:
## What

Consolidation-task workers must write a canonical `### Files Scope` on the consolidated successor issue. They currently omit it or write non-canonical prose, and the pre-claim scope gate (#32579) then holds every successor at `missing_files_scope`.

## Why

The consolidation instructions (`.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh` `_compose_consolidation_worker_instructions`) require the `auto-dispatch` label, but they never ask for a scope. They also use raw `gh issue create`, which bypasses the creation-time `_gh_ci_validate_dispatch_scope` check in `shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`. The pulse therefore creates briefs that its own gate rejects.

## Reproducer

Observed on 2026-09-27 in a private managed webapp repo:

1. A parent issue gained substantive comments and the pulse dispatched a `consolidation-task` child.
2. The consolidation worker filed the successor with `consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch`. Its `## Files Scope` lines put prose after the path, for example `` - `todo/<brief>.md` — source brief. ``, and some lines listed several comma-separated paths.
3. `pre-dispatch-validator-lib-brief-scope.sh:53` accepts only one path per line, so `_dispatch_preclaim_brief_scope` posted `Brief hold: reason=missing_files_scope` and set `status:blocked`.
4. The successor stays blocked until someone rewrites its body by hand.

## Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] The consolidation child instructions list `### Files Scope` with the canonical `- EDIT: path` / `- NEW: path` one-path-per-line format and explain why it matters.
- [ ] Regression: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` passes.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh
```

title: perf(opencode-plugin): reduce first-prompt context further — on-demand rare tools, stable OC1 plugin greeting, retire legacy AGENTS.md templates, pointer-sized agent__intent
body:
## Summary

GH#32444 reduced the first Anthropic request from ~44.7K to ~33.2K tokens. A fresh capture shows further reducible first-prompt context in OpenCode 1 (OC1 1.18.32) and OpenCode 2 (OC2 2.0.3) without losing guidance, skills, or invocation paths. This issue covers four items in one PR:

1. **On-demand dispatch for rarely used plugin tools (OC1).** Seven tool definitions cost 8,386 chars (~2.3K tokens) on every request: `gpt_image_generate` 1,918 (0 calls in 30 days), `ai-research` 1,850, `aidevops_objective_receipt` 1,128 (0 calls), `aidevops_mcp` 1,125, `model-accounts-pool` 1,118, `session-rename_sync_branch` 634, `aidevops` 613. Move the rarely used plugin tools behind one compact dispatcher whose description carries a one-line signature per sub-tool; invalid arguments return the full sub-tool schema so the model can self-correct. Keep frequently used or per-agent gated tools direct where dispatch would hurt usability or gating. Project-local `.opencode/tool` tools are not plugin tools; trim their descriptions instead of wrapping them.
2. **Stable plugin greeting on OC1.** OC1 still ships the runtime-generated fallback greeting AGENTS.md (2,467 chars) and uses the one-shot `createSessionStartGreetingGate`. OC2 already uses `createRootSessionGreetingGate` (identical greeting on every request of a root session, so the cache prefix stays stable). Reuse the root gate on OC1, enable the plugin greeting by default with the detected OpenCode version, and slim the generated fallback to the pinned precedence phrases.
3. **Stop deploying legacy home/Git-root AGENTS.md templates.** `templates/deploy-templates.sh` (`deploy_home_agents`, `deploy_git_agents`) writes outdated 3–4K-char AGENTS.md files that OC2 loads from parent directories (3,048 chars in the OC2 capture) and that point at the contributor guide instead of the user guide. Stop deploying them and add a setup migration that removes only copies whose git blob hash equals a historical template version (user-edited copies are preserved). A live Git-root copy on the maintainer machine matches historical blob `31dcf6bf`.
4. **Pointer-sized `agent__intent` schema.** The injected intent parameter costs 171 chars per tool: 3,762 chars in OC1 (22 tools) and 2,052 chars in OC2 (12 tools). The system prompt already carries the full "Intent Tracing (observability)" instruction, so the per-tool description can become a short pointer.

## Measurements (Haiku probe, first request, tokens ≈ chars/3.6)

| Runtime | Body chars | Tokens | Tool chars |
|---|---|---|---|
| OC1 1.18.32 | 89,283 | ~33.6K | 38,440 (22 tools) |
| OC2 2.0.3 | 76,708 | ~29.4K | 14,199 (12 tools) + Code Mode catalogue ~8.5–9K |

Expected after items 1–4: roughly 4–5K fewer tokens on OC1 and ~1.5K fewer on OC2; exact numbers are recorded in the PR.

## Constraints

- Anthropic OAuth wire shape unchanged: `system` stays [billing header, identity]; framework text stays redistributed into the first user message; tool-name prefixing, `agent__intent`, adaptive thinking, and cch signing preserved.
- Prompt-cache prefix must be deterministic per session (tool list and greeting identical on every request of a root session).
- No guidance, skill, or invocation path is removed; everything remains reachable on demand.
- Per-agent `aidevops_mcp` gating (`config-agent-profiles.mjs`) must keep working.

## Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tools.mjs`, `index.mjs` — tool registration, dispatcher site, greeting gate wiring.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/gpt-image-tool.mjs`, `objective-receipt-tool.mjs`, `oauth-pool-tool.mjs`, `mcp-activation-tool.mjs` — dispatch candidates.
- `.opencode/tool/ai-research.ts`, `.opencode/tool/session-rename.ts` — project-local tool descriptions.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/ttsr.mjs`, `root-session-greeting-gate.mjs`, `greeting.mjs`, `oauth-pool-token-endpoint.mjs` — greeting gate and version source (reference pattern: `v2.mjs` root gate wiring).
- `.agents/scripts/generate-runtime-config-agents.sh` (`_generate_greeting_agents_md`) — fallback greeting file.
- `.agents/reference/context-efficiency.md` — greeting policy documentation.
- `templates/deploy-templates.sh`, `templates/home/`, `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh`, `setup.sh` — item 3.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth-body.mjs` (`INTENT_PARAM_SCHEMA`) — item 4.

## Reproducer

Setup: install a capture plugin that records the outgoing Anthropic request body (OC1: an `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` plugin wrapping `fetch`; OC2: a plugin using the `http.request` session hook), then measure total chars, per-tool definition chars, and per-tool `agent__intent` chars.

**Symptom command**:

```
opencode run --agent "Build+" -m anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 "Context probe: reply with exactly OK and nothing else."
```

**Actual output** (per-tool size report from the OC1 capture, abridged):

```
body chars 89283 (~33.6K tokens); tools 22, tool chars 38440
agent__intent per tool: 171 chars (22 tools = 3762 chars)
gpt_image_generate          1918
ai-research                 1850
aidevops_objective_receipt  1128
aidevops_mcp                1125
model-accounts-pool         1118
session-rename_sync_branch   634
aidevops                     613
fallback greeting AGENTS.md 2467 (OC1 only)
OC2: body chars 76708 (~29.4K tokens); tools 12, tool chars 14199; legacy Git-root AGENTS.md 3048
```

**Expected**: rarely used tools, duplicate greeting text, legacy templates, and repeated intent descriptions do not occupy the first prompt; all remain reachable on demand.

## Verification

- Plugin tests: `node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/<affected>.mjs` (provider-auth, TTSR/greeting, V2 adapter with isolated HOME), plus a focused dispatcher test.
- Shell: ShellCheck for changed scripts; `.agents/scripts/tests/test-greeting-precedence.sh`; `tests/test-batch-quality-hardening.sh`.

## Follow-ups (separate issues)

Trimming the built-in Bash/Task descriptions via `tool.definition`, deduplicating the framework AGENTS.md against Build+, and OC2 gaps found during capture are tracked separately.

title: worktree-cleanup: PR-state and age policy for unregistered third-party worktrees (follow-up to #32536)
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to GH#32536 (PR #32559). Unregistered central worktrees are now evaluated, but only through the merged-branch path. Most of them are contribution PRs to third-party repos, where "merged into our default branch" is never true. So worktrees for closed or rejected upstream PRs, abandoned review/demo branches, and worktrees whose canonical repo was deleted still stay forever.

Observed on one host (27 unregistered worktrees):

| Class | Count | Examples (public repos) |
|---|---|---|
| Upstream PR open | 8 | Eugeny/tabby #11309/#11310, block/buzz #5353/#5436/#5440, awesome-opencode #431 |
| Upstream PR closed/merged | 11 | crosspoint-reader #3379-#3381, turbostarter/extro #4/#6/#7, afragen/git-updater #1156/#1158/#1159 |
| No PR, >30 days idle | 7 | review/demo/evidence branches (openai/codex, tambo-ai/tambo, crosspoint-reader) |
| Canonical repo missing | 1 | gitdir target deleted; git state unreadable |

Three open-PR worktrees had a local commit not on any known remote ref, and one had uncommitted edits. Those are exactly the cases that must be reported, not deleted.

## Policy (agreed with maintainer)

For each central worktree whose canonical repo is not in `repos.json`:

1. **Nothing live**: no live registry owner, no process cwd inside, no forensics/security markers. Otherwise skip.
2. **Upstream PR open** (search `upstream` remote first, then `origin`, by head branch): keep regardless of age. If it has unpushed commits or uncommitted changes, emit a `thirdparty-open-pr-unsent-work` report row (throttled to once per day per worktree).
3. **Upstream PR closed or merged**: if it has unique work (unpushed commits, dirty, or untracked files), make a verified compact archive via `worktree-archive-helper.sh` first, then remove. No age wait.
4. **No PR found**: age = newest of HEAD reflog, index mtime and last commit date, **not** directory mtime (bulk moves reset directory mtimes). At 30+ days (`WORKTREE_UNREGISTERED_MAX_AGE_DAYS`, default 30), archive any unique work, then remove.
5. **Canonical repo missing** (orphaned gitdir): bounded file-level archive, then move the directory to recoverable trash. Never permanent delete.
6. **Removal**: when the canonical exists, use `git worktree remove` from the canonical so metadata is pruned. Otherwise use recoverable trash, same as the `central-fixtures` pass.
7. **Rollout**: first release defaults to report-only (`WORKTREE_UNREGISTERED_APPLY=0`) and logs one row per decision plus a summary (`thirdparty eligible=N candidate_bytes=N removed=N archived=N kept_open_pr=N`). Flip the default to apply after one clean report cycle.

title: session-recovery-marker: owner liveness always false on macOS (/proc-only start token)
body:
## What

`processStartToken()` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-marker.mjs:28-37` reads `/proc/<pid>/stat`. `/proc` does not exist on macOS, so the function always returns `null` there. As a result, `resolveSessionRecoveryMarker()` (`:229-232`) always reports `ownerLive: false` on macOS.

## Impact

- **Product:** the live-owner guard added by #32507 (GH#32482, "avoid resuming live Tabby sessions from split tabs") never fires on macOS, the primary Tabby platform. A split tab can resume a session whose owner is still running.
- **Tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-session-recovery-marker.mjs:44-50` expects `ownerLive: true` and fails on every macOS host, including unmodified `main` @ `ca3fbd9c4`. Linux CI passes. The local `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` project validator (`npm run test` in `.agents/scripts`) therefore blocks every macOS PR push until `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PROJECT_VALIDATORS=1` is set. Observed while shipping GH#32589.

## How

- Add a portable fallback in `processStartToken(pid)`. Keep `/proc` first on Linux. On other platforms, use `spawnSync("ps", ["-o", "lstart=", "-p", String(pid)], { encoding: "utf8" })` and return the trimmed value when non-empty. `lstart` is stable for a PID's lifetime, so it works as a start token the same way `/proc` field 22 does.
- The writer (`:130-131`) and reader (`:231-232`) already share `processStartToken`, so no schema change is needed. Tokens written by old macOS markers were `null` and therefore already invalid.
- Reference pattern for liveness: `session-stall-recovery-ledger.mjs:10-13` (`process.kill(pid, 0)`). A start token is still required to guard against PID reuse.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-marker.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-session-recovery-marker.mjs`

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-recovery-marker.mjs` passes on macOS and Linux.
- On macOS, `node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-marker.mjs resolve --cwd <marker dir> --work-dir <work dir>` exits `3` while the owner is live.

title: fix(dispatch): brief hold re-comments on every label flap; catch unscoped auto-dispatch briefs at creation
body:
## What

Stop the missing-Files-Scope brief hold from re-commenting every time another path clears `status:blocked`, and catch unscoped auto-dispatch briefs before they are published.

## Why

PR #32579 (GH#32531) added a pre-claim hold for auto-dispatch briefs without a canonical Files Scope. Within hours, 7 open issues were held (#32588, #32526, #32496, #32487, #28377, #28839, #32594). Other pulse paths on three runner accounts moved each issue back to `status:available`, and each re-block posted another identical "Brief hold" comment. #28377 got 7 identical comments in about an hour (timeline 16:03Z to 17:20Z). This broke GH#32531's acceptance criterion: "not reprocessed every pulse cycle until the body changes".

The root authoring gap: 5 of the 7 were interactive briefs listing files under `## Files`, `### Files to Modify` or in prose. The creation-time wrapper check (`_gh_ci_validate_dispatch_scope`) accepts bodies with no file section. `claim-task-id.sh` withholds `auto-dispatch` while publication is pending (GH#30325), so the check never sees the intent.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/28377/timeline?per_page=100" \
  --jq '.[] | select(.event=="labeled" or .event=="unlabeled" or .event=="commented") | "\(.created_at) \(.event) \(.actor.login // .user.login) \(.label.name // "")"'
```

**Actual output** (excerpt, 2026-09-27):

```text
16:22:41Z labeled status:blocked      16:22:46Z commented (Brief hold)
16:24:18Z labeled status:available
16:30:06Z labeled status:blocked      16:30:22Z commented (Brief hold)
16:32:17Z labeled status:available
16:32:56Z labeled status:blocked      16:33:07Z commented (Brief hold)
...                                    17:20:03Z commented (Brief hold)
```

**Expected**: one hold comment for an unchanged body.

## How

1. `_dispatch_preclaim_brief_scope` stamps the hold comment with `<!-- aidevops:brief-hold reason=missing_files_scope body=<sha> -->`. If a trusted comment already carries the marker for the current body, it relabels without commenting. Unreadable history skips dispatch without writing.
2. `claim-task-id.sh` fails before ID allocation when an interactive session requests `auto-dispatch` with a description that lacks a Files Scope after normalization. Headless generators keep the pre-claim hold.
3. `gh_create_issue` warns (it does not block) when an auto-dispatch body has no scope declaration. Routine callers often run without headless markers.
4. The large-file gate adds a `NEW:` sibling glob, so split workers do not stop on `files_scope_excluded`.
5. `scope-guard-pre-push.sh` strips the `EDIT:`/`NEW:` prefix that the validator requires, so canonical scope lines match.
6. `workflows/brief.md` documents the required section and its verification command.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/brief.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-dispatch-validator.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scope-guard-pre-push.sh`

## Acceptance

- An unchanged unscoped body receives exactly one hold comment, however often the label is cleared. A changed body receives one new comment.
- Interactive `claim-task-id.sh --labels auto-dispatch` with an unscoped description exits non-zero before allocation. Scoped, normalized `Files to Modify`, planning-only and worker-origin cases still pass.
- Canonical `` - EDIT: `path` `` scope lines pass the pre-push scope guard.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-large-file-gate-body.sh`

title: aidevops init commits a per-machine absolute symlink and omits referenced README assets
body:
## What

Make `aidevops init` commit a clean, portable scaffold in a fresh public repository:

1. Stop committing the per-machine `.agents/commands` symlink. `_init_scaffold_commands_symlinks` links it to the absolute `$HOME/.aidevops/agents/commands`, and `_init_commit_files` stages `.agents/`, so the committed symlink leaks the local home path into public repos and is dangling on every other machine. Add `.agents/commands` and `.windsurf/` to the ignores written by `_init_update_gitignore` and leave the links as local-only.
2. Commit `docs/assets/` when the managed README seeds `docs/assets/star-history.svg`. The README references that image, but `_init_commit_files` does not stage `docs/assets/`, so new repos render a broken image.
3. Include common secret patterns (`.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `credentials.json`) in the init-created `.gitignore`. The security posture check that init runs immediately afterwards warns that exactly these are missing.
4. Substitute `{{DATE}}` in the TODO.md TOON meta block (`1.1,todo-md+toon,{{DATE}}`), which init currently leaves literal.
5. Fix the log line `Creating worktree at <sibling>-chore-aidevops-init...` in `check_protected_branch`: it prints the fallback sibling path while `worktree-helper.sh` actually creates the worktree under `${AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_BASE_DIR:-~/Git/_worktrees}`.
6. Replace the `gh pr create --fill` next-step hint in `_init_print_summary` with the wrapper path (`gh_create_pr` / `--label origin:interactive`) required by `workflows/git-workflow.md`.

## Why

Observed on 2026-09-27 initializing three new public Cloudron package repositories: each init PR needed manual fixes for items 1–4 before it could merge. Item 1 leaks the maintainer's local username path into public GitHub content, contrary to `reference/pre-push-guards.md`.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-init-lib.sh` — `_init_update_gitignore` (ignores), `_init_commit_files` (stage `docs/assets/`), `_init_planning_files` (date substitution), `_init_print_summary` (wrapper hint).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh` — `check_protected_branch` log line near `print_info "Creating worktree at $worktree_dir..."`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-init-help-gitignore.sh` — extend the existing init `.gitignore` assertions for the new ignore entries.

Reference pattern: existing `_init_update_gitignore` entry list and `_init_commit_files` `init_files+=(...)` array.

### Verification

```bash

(cd "$tmp" && AIDEVOPS_PROTECTED_BRANCH_CHOICE=2 aidevops init planning)
git -C "$tmp" ls-files | grep -c '^.agents/commands$'   # expect 0

```

## Acceptance

- [ ] A fresh `aidevops init` never tracks `.agents/commands` or `.windsurf/` and never commits an absolute home path.
- [ ] When the managed README references `docs/assets/star-history.svg`, that file is committed by init.
- [ ] Init-created `.gitignore` contains the secret patterns listed above; existing `.gitignore` entries are not duplicated or removed.
- [ ] TODO.md has no literal `{{DATE}}` after init.

title: aidevops init defaults: beads/database opt-in, public scope inference, worktree-safe naming
body:
## What

Make `aidevops init` defaults and naming fit new repositories initialized through the auto-created worktree:

1. **Beads in the default `all` set conflicts with aidevops.** `bd init` appends an AGENTS.md block that says "do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown TODO lists" and mandates `bd dolt push`, contradicting aidevops' TODO.md/TodoWrite workflow. It also writes untracked `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/settings.json`. Remove `beads` from the default `all` set (keep it opt-in), and when enabled, suppress bd's agent-instruction injection if bd supports it.
2. **Beads database and issue prefix use the worktree directory name** (`<repo>-chore-aidevops-init`) instead of the repository name. Pass the canonical repo name/prefix to `bd init`.
3. **`database` in the default set scaffolds `schemas/`, `migrations/`, `seeds/`** in repos with no database. Enable it by default only when database signals exist (ORM/migration config, `*.sql`, `schema.prisma`, etc.); otherwise keep it opt-in.
4. **`_infer_init_scope` never infers `public`.** Public GitHub repos get `standard`, so SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and CHANGELOG.md are never scaffolded, and the security posture check then warns "No SECURITY.md". Infer `public` when `gh repo view --json visibility` reports `PUBLIC` (init already calls GitHub for label sync).
5. **Scope lookup in `repos.json` uses the worktree path.** `_infer_init_scope` compares `.initialized_repos[].path` with the worktree realpath, so an explicit `init_scope` on the canonical entry is ignored when init runs in its auto-created worktree. Resolve the main worktree path first (as `_init_security_and_registration` already does).
6. **`repo_name=$(basename "$project_root")`** in `scaffold_repo_courtesy_files` yields the worktree directory name inside the auto-created worktree; use the same remote-URL-first resolution as `_init_config_and_agents`.
7. **Task counter bootstrap seeds from commented format examples.** `claim-task-id.sh` BOOTSTRAP_COUNTER reads the `t001`–`t003` examples inside the TODO.md HTML comment and starts new repos at `t4`. Ignore commented lines when seeding.

## Why

Observed on 2026-09-27 initializing three new public Cloudron package repositories: the default run added conflicting beads instructions and unused database directories, named beads after the worktree, skipped public courtesy files, and started task IDs at t4.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-init-lib.sh` — `_init_parse_features` (default set), `_init_run_beads_init` (name/prefix, instruction injection), `_init_database_and_beads` (signal detection), `scaffold_repo_courtesy_files` (repo name).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh` — `_infer_init_scope` (public inference, main-worktree path lookup).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — bootstrap seeding ignores HTML-commented TODO lines.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md` — document the inferred `public` scope if behaviour changes.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-init-scope.sh` — extend existing scope-inference assertions for public visibility and worktree-path lookup.

Reference pattern: main-worktree resolution in `_init_security_and_registration` (`git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{print $2; exit}'`) and repo-name resolution in `_init_config_and_agents`.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-init-lib.sh .agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-init.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-init-scope.sh
```

Production-path check: in a scratch repo with a GitHub remote, run `aidevops init` and confirm no beads block in AGENTS.md, no `schemas/` without DB signals, scope `public` for a public remote, and courtesy files named after the repo.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Default `aidevops init` does not enable beads or database scaffolding in a repo without database signals; explicit `aidevops init beads` / `database` still work.
- [ ] A public GitHub repo infers `public` scope and receives SECURITY.md/CONTRIBUTING.md/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md/CHANGELOG.md; private repos keep `standard`.

title: New managed repos: interactive auto-dispatch tasks start blocked and planning publication never reconciles
body:
## What

Fix four lifecycle gaps hit when publishing the first tasks in brand-new managed repositories:

1. **Interactive auto-dispatch tasks start dispatch-blocked.** `issue-sync-helper.sh push tNNN` for a TODO entry tagged `#auto-dispatch #interactive` auto-assigns the maintainer and applies `status:in-review`. After planning publication reconciled and added `auto-dispatch`, the issue stayed assigned and `status:in-review`, which pulse treats as an active interactive claim. `interactive-session-helper.sh release <N> <slug> --unassign` removed the assignee but reported "already outside status:in-review" while the label was still present, so `status:in-review` had to be swapped for `status:available` by hand. Apply the GH#20946 carve-out on push: do not self-assign or set `status:in-review` for `auto-dispatch` tasks unless the session is implementing them.
2. **Planning publication never reconciles in repos without the issue-sync workflow.** New repos have no `issue-sync.yml`, so merging the planning PR left issues at `publication:pending`. Running `planning-publication-reconcile.sh reconcile --repo <slug> --sha <merge-sha>` fixed it. Run that reconcile from `full-loop-helper.sh merge` (or the merge lifecycle) when the merged PR touched `TODO.md`/`todo/tasks/`.
3. **`full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <other/repo>` proposes syncing the wrong canonical repo.** Run from the aidevops checkout for a PR in another repo, it printed `CANONICAL_SYNC_NEXT=canonical-recovery-helper.sh fast-forward-current --repo <aidevops canonical path> ... --issue 3`. Resolve the local path from the target slug via `repos.json`, not the current directory.
4. **`#ops` TODO tag produced a `bug` label** on operator checklist issues. Map `#ops` to an ops/chore type (or no type label), not `bug`.

## Why

Observed on 2026-09-27 publishing t4/t5 in three new public Cloudron package repos: every issue needed manual label, assignee and reconcile repair before workers could pick up t4.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-push.sh` — skip self-assign/`status:in-review` for `auto-dispatch` tasks (item 1).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh` — `release` should read live labels before reporting "already outside status:in-review" (item 1).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` — post-merge planning reconcile when planning files changed (item 2); resolve canonical path from the target slug (item 3).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-labels.sh` — `#ops` tag mapping (item 4).

Reference pattern: the GH#20946 carve-out in `interactive-session-helper.sh claim`, and `planning-publication-reconcile.sh reconcile --repo --sha`.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-push.sh .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-labels.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-post-merge.sh
```

Production-path check: in a scratch repo without `issue-sync.yml`, add an `#auto-dispatch #interactive` TODO task, push, merge the planning PR via `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, and confirm the issue ends unassigned with `auto-dispatch` + `status:available` and no `publication:pending`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An interactively created `#auto-dispatch` task is dispatchable after its planning PR merges, with no manual label or assignee edits.
- [ ] Non-auto-dispatch interactive tasks keep the current claim behaviour.
- [ ] `full-loop-helper.sh merge` for another repo names that repo's canonical path in any sync hint.
- [ ] `#ops` no longer yields a `bug` label.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean; existing helper tests pass.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-push.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-commands.sh` — required implementation location for `release` lifecycle transition.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-labels.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib-compose.sh` — required implementation location for `#ops` tag alias mapping.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` — required merge lifecycle location for post-merge reconcile and target canonical sync resolution.

title: OpenCode plugin: llm_requests runtime_version and adapter_version are always empty
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `llm_requests runtime_version observability OpenCode V2 event handler` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 2 commits (2c2bb8b3b GH#32469, c6b9f0ba8 t18433) / 0 merged related PRs / 0 open PRs touch target files; neither sets runtime or adapter provenance
- [x] File refs verified: 7 refs checked, all present at `main` f9ac65147
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — known wiring pattern inside a decided boundary; the worker still chooses test placement and option plumbing
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the change is small and the call sites below are exact

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-27
- **Session:** opencode:interactive (GH#32592 first-prompt context session)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** While measuring token savings for GH#32592 from `llm-requests.db`, OC1 and OC2 rows could not be told apart and never carried a runtime version.

## What

Every `llm_requests` row written by the OpenCode plugin records the real host runtime version and an adapter identifier:

- `runtime_version`: the OpenCode version that served the request (for example `1.18.32` on OC1, `2.0.3` on OC2).
- `adapter_version`: `opencode-v1@<aidevops version>` from `index.mjs`, or `opencode-v2@<aidevops version>` from `v2.mjs`.

## Why

- Both columns are empty in every `llm_requests` row from the last 7 days (45,866 rows; `runtime_name` is `opencode` in all of them). Version-regression analysis, OC1/OC2 parity checks and the OC2 observability gap (filed separately) can't use the table.
- `runtime_version` reads `process.env.OPENCODE_VERSION`, which OpenCode never sets. The plugin already computes the right value on both runtimes but never passes it to observability.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (SQL file contents shown in the comment):

```bash
# SELECT runtime_name, COALESCE(NULLIF(runtime_version,''),'<empty>'), COALESCE(NULLIF(adapter_version,''),'<empty>'), COUNT(*)
# FROM llm_requests WHERE timestamp >= strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now','-7 days') GROUP BY 1,2,3;
sqlite3 -header ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/llm-requests.db ".read provenance-check.sql"
```

**Actual output** (2026-09-27):

```text
runtime_name|runtime_version|adapter_version|rows
opencode|<empty>|<empty>|45866
```

**Expected output:**

```text
OC1 rows carry the OpenCode 1.x version and adapter_version opencode-v1@<aidevops version>;
OC2 rows carry 2.x and opencode-v2@<aidevops version>.
```

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs:261` `handleEvent` → `handleMessageUpdated` (`:361`) on each completed assistant `message.updated` event
- **Call chain**: `handleMessageUpdated` → `requestProvenance(msg, routing, pricing)` (`observability-provenance.mjs:8`) → `runtime_version: stringOrNull(process.env.OPENCODE_VERSION)` (`:21`), `adapter_version: null` (`:22`) → row insert. No other code writes these columns.
- **Integrated verification**: the SQL above over live rows written through that same path by OC1 1.18.32 sessions returns only empty values.

**Causal code:**

```bash
git blame .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability-provenance.mjs -L 21,22
```

**Call-site sweep:**

```bash
rg -n "requestProvenance|initObservability\(" .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops --glob '!tests/**'
# observability.mjs:241 (definition), index.mjs:389 and v2.mjs:275 (callers pass only aidevopsVersion)
```

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The values and call sites are known, but the worker plumbs a new option through module state and picks where a focused test belongs. No trust boundary or migration is involved.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR uses a closing keyword for this issue.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs:241-252` — `initObservability` accepts `runtimeVersion` and `adapterId`, stores them in module state beside `aidevopsVersion`, and passes them to `requestProvenance`. Find the caller with `rg -n "requestProvenance\(" .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs`.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability-provenance.mjs:8-28` — take runtime identity from an explicit argument. Keep `process.env.OPENCODE_VERSION` only as a fallback.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs:389` — pass `runtimeVersion: DETECTED_OPENCODE_RUNTIME_VERSION` (already imported at `index.mjs:108` from `oauth-pool-token-endpoint.mjs:40`) and `adapterId: "opencode-v1"`.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs:275` — pass `runtimeVersion: (typeof ctx.app?.version === "string" && ctx.app.version) || detectOpenCodeV2RuntimeVersion()` (the same expression as `v2.mjs:344`) and `adapterId: "opencode-v2"`.
- `NEW: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-observability-provenance.mjs` — focused `node --test` coverage for explicit values, env fallback and null behaviour. Model on `tests/test-observability-routing-join.mjs`.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `requestProvenance` callers in `observability.mjs`. Readers are SQL consumers of `llm_requests`; `rg -n "runtime_version|adapter_version" .agents/scripts` shows no shell reader today.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** only `observability-provenance.mjs:21-22`.
- **Existing verification/tests:** no existing test covers `requestProvenance` (`rg -l requestProvenance .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests` is empty); `tests/test-observability-routing-join.mjs` covers the adjacent row-write path.
- **Schemas/config:** the columns already exist in `llm_requests`, created by `initDatabase` in `observability.mjs`; no schema change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys the plugin to `~/.aidevops/agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/`; there is no generated copy.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the columns already exist and historical rows stay empty; there is no backfill of guessed versions.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** N/A because no persisted state is added; rollback is a revert of `observability-provenance.mjs` and its two callers.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add `runtimeVersion` and `adapterId` to the `initObservability` options and module state. Keep the existing `aidevopsVersion` normalisation.
2. Change `requestProvenance(msg, routing, pricing)` to take a fourth `runtime` argument: `{ runtimeVersion, adapterVersion }`. Use `stringOrNull(runtime?.runtimeVersion || process.env.OPENCODE_VERSION)` and `stringOrNull(runtime?.adapterVersion)`.
3. Build `adapterVersion` as `${adapterId}@${aidevopsVersion}` only when both are non-empty; otherwise use `null`.
4. Wire both call sites (`index.mjs:389`, `v2.mjs:275`) as listed above.
5. Add the focused test file, then run a real OC1 prompt and query the newest row.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** module-level values are set once at plugin init, before any event; no race.
- **Migration/rollback:** no schema change; rollback is a revert.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older plugins keep writing empty values; readers must already tolerate NULL.
- **Idempotency/retry:** pure value plumbing; replay-safe.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if version detection fails, the fields stay NULL, as today. Never throw from `initObservability`.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-observability-provenance.mjs
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-observability-routing-join.mjs
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the new test proves explicit, fallback and null values. After deploy, one real OC1 and one OC2 request each prove the runtime wiring: rerun the Reproducer SQL and check the newest rows.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required; there are no cross-package contracts.

### Scope Notes

- Hard boundaries: leave `gh-signature-helper-detect.sh` and the `llm_requests` schema as they are.
- AI brief owner: marcusquinn (interactive maintainer session).
- Recovery: preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability-provenance.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-observability-provenance.mjs`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `requestProvenance` returns the supplied runtime version and `opencode-v1@<version>` / `opencode-v2@<version>` adapter identity

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-observability-provenance.mjs"
  ```

- [ ] Provenance no longer depends solely on the unset `OPENCODE_VERSION` env var

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "runtime_version: stringOrNull\\(process\\.env\\.OPENCODE_VERSION\\)"
    path: ".agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability-provenance.mjs"
    expect: absent
  ```

- [ ] Regression guard: `initObservability` still succeeds and writes rows when version detection returns null (fields stay NULL; no exception)
- [ ] After deploy, a fresh OC1 row and a fresh OC2 row each carry non-empty `runtime_version` and `adapter_version`
- [ ] Changed-file lint is clean (`linters-local.sh --changed`)

## Context & Decisions

- `adapter_version` identifies the aidevops adapter (`opencode-v1`/`opencode-v2`) plus the aidevops version. That separates OC1 and OC2 rows, which currently share `runtime_name=opencode`.
- Non-goal: backfilling historical rows.
- Related: OC2 currently writes no `llm_requests` rows at all (separate issue). This fix is still needed so OC2 rows carry provenance once that is fixed.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-token-endpoint.mjs:40` — `DETECTED_OPENCODE_RUNTIME_VERSION` source for OC1.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs:139` — `detectOpenCodeV2RuntimeVersion`; `v2.mjs:344` shows the OC2 expression.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-observability-routing-join.mjs` — existing observability test pattern.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** reliable OC1/OC2 cost and version comparisons
- **External:** none

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 10m | the 4 call sites above |
| Implementation | 30m | option plumbing + focused test |

title: OpenCode V2 adapter writes no llm_requests rows
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `llm_requests runtime_version observability OpenCode V2 event handler` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 5 commits in 48h touch `v2.mjs`/`observability.mjs` (2c2bb8b3b GH#32469, 26ab5ae45 GH#32498, 61f09b057 GH#32444, bf587d6d5 GH#32447, 146ded09a t18481) / 0 open PRs; none changes V2 event mapping
- [x] File refs verified: 8 refs checked, all present at `main` f9ac65147
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — bounded adapter mapping; the worker must first capture the V2 event shape, but no trust or product decision remains
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the V2 event shape is not yet captured, so a seed would anchor on a guess

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-27
- **Session:** opencode:interactive (GH#32592 first-prompt context session)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** GH#32592 measured token savings from `llm-requests.db`. OC1 probes produced rows; six OC2 (OpenCode 2.0.3) probes through the same plugin produced none.

## What

Completed assistant messages on the OpenCode V2 adapter (`v2.mjs`) write `llm_requests` rows, with tokens, cost, model and session, just as on OC1. OC2 sessions then show up in cost, cache and routing analysis.

## Why

- OC2 usage is currently invisible to all `llm_requests` consumers: token and cost reporting, cache-hit verification, and routing and A/B acceptance.
- GH#32592 had to measure OC2 by character counts because the API-reported token path was missing.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (six isolated OC2 runs through the deployed V2 plugin, then a query for Haiku rows):

```bash
# Each probe ran with the config home set to a mktemp copy of ~/.aidevops/runtimes/opencode-v2/config
# (for example ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/gh32592-oc2-iso.AbC123):
#   AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_CONFIG_HOME=~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/gh32592-oc2-iso.AbC123 \
#   ~/.local/bin/opencode2 run --standalone --agent "Build+" -m anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 \
#     "Context probe: reply with exactly OK and nothing else."
# SQL: SELECT substr(timestamp,1,19), session_id, tokens_input+tokens_cache_read+tokens_cache_write
#      FROM llm_requests WHERE timestamp >= '2026-09-27T15:00:00' AND model_id LIKE '%haiku%' ORDER BY timestamp;
sqlite3 ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/llm-requests.db ".read haiku-rows.sql"
```

**Actual output** (UTC). Every row matches an OC1 capture; OC2 probes ran at 15:50, 17:58–17:59 and 18:24–18:25 UTC and wrote nothing:

```text
2026-09-27T15:48:44|ses_f1c723f9effe…|24024   <- OC1 probe (oc1-95567)
2026-09-27T17:45:55 … 17:54:56  (12 rows)     <- OC1 probes (oc1-49997 … oc1-81492)
(no rows at 15:50, 17:58-17:59 or 18:24-18:25 UTC, when the OC2 probes ran)
```

**Expected output:**

```text
One row per completed OC2 assistant message, with the claude-haiku-4-5 model and non-zero prompt tokens.
```

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation

**Causal code** (suspected):

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs:412-418` feeds every V2 event to `handleEvent` (`observability.mjs:261`).
- `handleEvent` records a request only for `event.type === "message.updated"` with `properties.info.role === "assistant"` and `properties.info.time.completed` (`observability.mjs:267`, `:361-368`).
- `v2.mjs` never references `message.updated`. OpenCode 2 likely emits a different event name or payload shape for completed assistant messages.
- `startEventLoop` (`v2.mjs:205-228`) swallows handler and subscription errors unless `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_DEBUG=1`, so a thrown error is also possible and would be invisible.

**Call-site sweep:**

```bash
rg -n "handleEvent|startEventLoop|message\.updated" .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs
```

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** A bounded adapter fix inside a decided boundary (normalise V2 events into the existing `handleMessageUpdated` contract). The worker gathers the event shape first; no trust, billing or migration decision is open.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR uses a closing keyword for this issue.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs:412-418` — normalise the V2 completed-assistant event into the `{ type: "message.updated", properties: { info } }` shape before calling `handleEvent`, or add a V2-specific branch. Keep other handlers receiving the raw event.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs:261-278` — only if the V2 shape cannot be normalised in the adapter. Keep OC1 behaviour byte-identical.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs` — add a case next to "V2 event processing continues after one handler failure" (line 78), feeding a captured V2 completion event and asserting that `handleEvent` receives a recordable assistant message.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `v2.mjs:412` event loop → `observability.mjs:261` `handleEvent` → `handleMessageUpdated` (`:361`). The row readers are the `llm_requests` SQL consumers.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the `llm_requests` insert in `observability.mjs` (reached only via `handleMessageUpdated`) plus runtime events via `recordOpenCodeRuntimeEvent` (`:309`).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs:78` (event loop resilience), `tests/test-observability-routing-join.mjs`, `tests/test-runtime-events.mjs`.
- **Schemas/config:** no schema change; the `llm_requests` columns are unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys to `~/.aidevops/agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/`; the V2 loader is `v2-plugin/` in the same tree.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because historical OC2 requests were never captured and cannot be reconstructed from local state.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** N/A because only in-memory event mapping changes; rollback is a revert of `v2.mjs`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Capture the real V2 event shape. Run one isolated OC2 prompt with `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_DEBUG=1` and a temporary local-only log of `event.type` plus the `properties` keys inside the `v2.mjs:412` handler. Identify the event that marks a completed assistant message and where its tokens, cost, model, session ID and completion time live. Do not commit the temporary logging.
2. Confirm whether the current path throws (debug stderr from `startEventLoop`) or just never matches.
3. Map that event to the existing `handleMessageUpdated` input contract in the adapter. Deduplication via `recordedMessages` (`observability.mjs:371`) must still prevent double rows.
4. Add the adapter test with the captured (redacted) event fixture.
5. Deploy locally (`setup.sh --non-interactive`), run one OC2 prompt, and confirm exactly one new `llm_requests` row per completed assistant message.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** events are processed sequentially per loop; the existing dedup set covers repeated updates.
- **Migration/rollback:** no persisted-format change; revert is safe.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** OC1 (`index.mjs`) must keep its current path unchanged; OC2 versions without the new event shape must not throw.
- **Idempotency/retry:** repeated V2 update events for one message must still yield one row (`recordedMessages`).
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a malformed V2 event must be skipped without stopping the loop (existing behaviour at `v2.mjs:216-222`).

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-observability-routing-join.mjs
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the adapter test proves the mapping; one live OC2 prompt plus the Reproducer SQL proves the production path.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required.

### Safety-Stop Recovery

- **Original objective:** OC2 completed assistant messages write `llm_requests` rows.
- **Preserved user directions:** keep OC1 behaviour unchanged; no fabricated token values.
- **Trigger and evidence:** not triggered.
- **Completed and verified:** diagnosis evidence above.
- **Remaining acceptance criteria:** all criteria below.
- **Unsafe route not to repeat:** injecting the plugin via `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` (loads both deployed and test plugins and double-records); use an isolated `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_V2_CONFIG_HOME` copy instead.
- **Next safe route:** capture events in an isolated config home.
- **Resume condition:** V2 event shape captured.
- **Owner and status:** worker; not-triggered.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A completed OC2 assistant message produces exactly one `llm_requests` row with model, session and non-zero prompt tokens

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs"
  ```

- [ ] Regression guard: OC1 recording is unchanged (`tests/test-observability-routing-join.mjs` passes and live OC1 rows still appear)

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-observability-routing-join.mjs"
  ```

- [ ] Negative guard: repeated V2 update events for the same message never create duplicate rows
- [ ] The PR body names the V2 event type used and includes a live OC2 row from the Reproducer SQL
- [ ] Changed-file lint is clean (`linters-local.sh --changed`)

## Context & Decisions

- Related: a separate issue fixes empty `runtime_version`/`adapter_version`, which is needed to tell OC1 and OC2 rows apart once OC2 rows exist.
- Other OC2 gaps seen (not in scope): no TodoWrite task-list tool, and the Code Mode catalogue exposes 16 of 55 tools plus `search`.
- Non-goal: reconstructing historical OC2 usage.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs:726` — the OC1 `handleEvent` call to mirror.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs:361-380` — the `handleMessageUpdated` input contract.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs:78` — existing V2 event-loop test pattern.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** OC2 cost, cache and routing observability
- **External:** an OpenCode 2 install at `~/.local/bin/opencode2` with an Anthropic OAuth account for the live check

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 30m | capture V2 events in isolation |
| Implementation | 1h | adapter mapping + test |
| Verification | 30m | live OC2 row |
