title: t18495: Guard merged-PR reconcile stages 1-2 against recurrent file-size debt
body:
## What

Reconcile stages 1 (`_action_ciw_single`, `status:available`) and 2 (`_action_rsd_single`, `status:done`) must not close a generated `file-size-debt` issue on historical merged-PR evidence while its cited file is again at or above the recorded threshold. Stage 3 (`_action_oimp_single`) already applies `_pir_file_size_debt_current_outcome`; stages 1-2 skip it.

## Why

Observed on #28377: PR #28395 split `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` to 1,986 lines (threshold 2000) and merged 2026-07-21. The file regrew to 2,659 lines, yet stage 1 closed the issue on 2026-09-01 and again on 2026-09-27T18:33Z with "Closing: work completed via merged PR #28395 ... Issue was open but dedup guard was blocking re-dispatch." That text is emitted only by `_action_ciw_single` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh`. The large-file gate (`_large_file_gate_reopen_debt_issue` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh`) then reopens it from remote line-count evidence, producing close/reopen churn across runners.

## How

- In `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh`, extract one shared guard around `_pir_file_size_debt_current_outcome` (rc 0 = debt current, block close; rc 2 = unmeasurable, defer; rc 1 = proceed) and reuse it from `_action_oimp_single` (reference pattern: the existing `case "$current_outcome_rc"` block there).
- `_action_ciw_single`: accept an optional issue body (6th arg); when blocked, log and return 1 before any dedup API call.
- `_action_rsd_single`: accept an optional issue body; when debt is current, reset to `status:available` (rc 2, same as the unmerged-PR path); when unmeasurable, defer (rc 1).
- Pass `$issue_body` from `reconcile_issues_single_pass` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`, and from the legacy `close_issues_with_merged_prs` / `reconcile_stale_done_issues` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-close.sh` (include `body` in the jq selection and the `gh_issue_list --json` fallback).

## Reference pattern

Model on the existing stage 3 guard in `_action_oimp_single` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh`, the `_pir_file_size_debt_current_outcome` call and its `case` on rc 0/2).

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-close.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`

## Acceptance

- A generated file-size-debt issue whose cited file is at or above threshold is not closed by stage 1 or 2; stage 2 resets it to `status:available`.
- Non-generated issues and resolved debt close exactly as before.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` passes.
- `shellcheck` clean on the three scripts; `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` passes.

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: Prospective TODO merge guard re-downloads entire repository and times out
body:
## Observed failure
In an interactive maintained-app PR merge, full-loop-helper.sh merge passed fresh head, check, and review-bot gates but failed closed before merge. The prospective TODO check creates a new isolated bare Git repository for each attempt, then unfiltered fetches of the pinned base and refs/pull/N/head. Three attempts with 480s, 900s, and 1200s budgets could not finish: the third temporary object store exceeded 577 MiB while fetching the PR head after the base. No merge occurred. A git fetch failure/timeout discarded the temp clone, so the next attempt restarted the full transfer. This is not a request to bypass the TODO guard or weaken head/remote pinning.

## Target files / approach
- scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh: _merge_create_prospective_object_context, _merge_fetch_pinned_commit_objects, _merge_guard_prospective_todo. Use an isolated, bounded, partial object fetch (or an equivalent durable validated cache) that keeps the exact pinned remote, base/head SHA, isolated Git config, and merge-tree/TODO proof. Handle servers without partial-clone support by failing closed. Bound transfer and surface meaningful progress or size.
- scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh: test a large-history private target without repeatedly transferring unrelated blobs; test head/base mismatch, cache corruption, remote mismatch, timeout and indeterminate merge-tree fail closed.

## Verification
Reproduce with a repository whose history has large unrelated blobs and a small PR; demonstrate exact-head prospective TODO validation and guarded merge finish within a bounded interval. Run shellcheck and the focused merge-helper tests. Do not log private repository identity or temporary filesystem paths in the public issue.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: OpenCode plugin: usage-driven on-demand loading for rarely used aidevops tools on OpenCode 1
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `on-demand tool loading defer_loading rare tools usage` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: GH#32592 (PR #32606, merged) added `aidevops_on_demand` for three tools; #32622 covers built-in tool description text; 0 open PRs touch `on-demand-tools.mjs`
- [x] File refs verified: 4 refs checked, all present at `main` 2a3130a4e
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — usage-driven list extension on an existing mechanism, plus a gated provider evaluation
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the usage measurement decides the tool list

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-27
- **Session:** opencode:interactive (GH#32632 context-budget session)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** After GH#32592 and GH#32632, tool definitions are the largest remaining block in the OpenCode 1 first request. The user asked for efficiency with progressive, on-demand discovery that loses no capability.

## What

Measured, usage-driven on-demand loading for aidevops-owned tools on OpenCode 1: move further rarely used tools behind the existing `aidevops_on_demand` dispatcher, chosen from recorded tool-call frequency, and report the API-token saving. Record whether provider-native deferred tool loading is usable on the Anthropic OAuth and OpenAI paths, with evidence, without adopting it in this issue.

## Why

Measured with `context-budget-helper.sh capture oc1` (OpenCode 1.18.32, Build+, claude-haiku-4-5, `main` plus GH#32632):

- Tools are 32,913 of 82,239 request-body chars (40 percent), 20 tools in total.
- aidevops-owned direct tools total about 9,800 chars: `aidevops_memory` 1,520, `ai-research` 1,391, `aidevops_on_demand` 1,363, `aidevops_bounded_operation` 1,301, `aidevops_mcp` 1,025, `session-rename` 835, `aidevops_pre_edit_check` 804, `aidevops_hook_status` 616, `aidevops` 513, `session-rename_sync_branch` 428.
- `aidevops_on_demand` currently holds only `gpt_image_generate`, `model-accounts-pool` and `aidevops_objective_receipt` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/on-demand-tools.mjs:19-23`).
- Built-in tool text (Bash, Task, TodoWrite and others) is out of scope here; #32622 covers it.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** it extends an existing, tested dispatcher; the only judgement is the usage threshold, which the brief fixes below.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR uses a closing keyword for this issue.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/on-demand-tools.mjs:19-23` — extend `ON_DEMAND_TOOL_NAMES` with the measured rare tools.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-on-demand-tools.mjs` — cover the added names if that test enumerates them.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/context-budget.md` — add the tool-usage query used for the selection.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `index.mjs:435` calls `moveToolsOnDemand(baseTools, tool)` on the OpenCode 1 entrypoint only; OpenCode 2 already defers plugin tools into Code Mode.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `moveToolsOnDemand` and `createOnDemandTool` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/on-demand-tools.mjs`.
- **Existing verification/tests:** plugin tests under `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/`; live `context-budget-helper.sh capture oc1` and `tokens`.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because the dispatcher takes no config; `ON_DEMAND_TOOL_NAMES` is a code constant.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/plugins/`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because tools are registered per session.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** remove names from `ON_DEMAND_TOOL_NAMES`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Query tool-call frequency per session from the `tool_calls` table (schema at `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability-init.mjs:129`) in the observability DB, read-only, over the last 30 days. Report sessions-with-use per tool.
2. Move an aidevops-owned tool only if it is used in under 2 percent of sessions, is not per-agent gated (as `aidevops_mcp` is), and is not named as a mandatory step in always-loaded guidance (for example `aidevops_memory` recall and `aidevops_pre_edit_check`).
3. Measure control against candidate with `context-budget-helper.sh capture oc1 --turns 2` and `tokens`; keep the change only for a real API-token saving and a turn-2 `cache_read` equal to the turn-1 prefix.
4. Record, in the PR, whether provider-native deferred tool definitions are supported on the installed OpenCode 1.18.32 Anthropic OAuth path and on the OpenAI provider path, citing installed package exports or primary docs. Do not enable them here: the Anthropic OAuth wire shape (billing header, Claude Code identity, `mcp__` prefixes, `agent__intent`) must not change without a separate decision.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A because registration is per session.
- **Migration/rollback:** stateless; remove names to roll back.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** a moved tool stays callable through `aidevops_on_demand` with the same arguments, and its one-line signature stays in the dispatcher description.
- **Idempotency/retry:** the dispatcher output is deterministic, so the prompt-cache prefix stays stable.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** invalid sub-tool args return the schema, as today.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-on-demand-tools.mjs
.agents/scripts/context-budget-helper.sh capture oc1 --turns 2 --plugin .
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** unit tests prove dispatch and schema return; live captures prove the token delta, wire shape and cache read.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/on-demand-tools.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-on-demand-tools.mjs`
- `.agents/reference/context-budget.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The PR lists per-tool session-use rates and moves only tools meeting the stated threshold
- [ ] An OC1 control/candidate comparison reports the API-token delta, an unchanged wire shape and a full turn-2 cache read
- [ ] The PR records provider-native deferred loading support for Anthropic OAuth and OpenAI with cited evidence, without enabling it
- [ ] Plugin tests and changed-file lint pass

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-on-demand-tools.mjs"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- Mandatory-step tools stay direct: hiding them behind a dispatcher would make required guidance harder to follow.
- If no tool meets the threshold, the correct outcome is a PR or comment reporting the usage data and no code change.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/on-demand-tools.mjs:1` — dispatcher design notes.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs:435` — OpenCode 1 registration.
- `.agents/reference/context-budget.md` — capture, compare and tokens workflow.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** none
- **External:** an Anthropic OAuth account for live captures

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Measurement | 30m | tool-call frequency query |
| Implementation | 30m | name list and tests |
| Verification | 45m | live captures and provider evidence |
| **Total** | **~1h45m** | |

title: OpenCode 2 parity: no TodoWrite tool and a partial Code Mode catalogue hide tools that framework guidance requires
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `opencode v2 todowrite code mode catalog partial search` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs touch `v2.mjs` for todo or catalogue handling; related open issues are #32619 (V2 `llm_requests`) and #32622 (built-in tool text)
- [x] File refs verified: 3 refs checked, all present at `main` 2a3130a4e
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — choosing between a V2 todo adapter and runtime-aware guidance affects every OpenCode 2 session
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the approach decision comes first

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-27
- **Session:** opencode:interactive (GH#32632 context-budget session)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Isolated OpenCode 2.0.3 captures made with the new `context-budget-helper.sh` (GH#32632) showed two parity gaps against OpenCode 1 that affect how well framework guidance can be followed.

## What

OpenCode 2 sessions can follow the framework's task-tracking and tool-discovery guidance:

1. A todo capability that OpenCode 2 exposes, or guidance that names the OpenCode 2 alternative when TodoWrite is absent.
2. Framework tools that the guidance relies on (for example `ai-research`) are either in the visible Code Mode catalogue or discoverable through an explicit `search` hint.

## Why

Measured with `context-budget-helper.sh capture oc2` (OpenCode 2.0.3, Build+, claude-haiku-4-5) against `main` 2a3130a4e:

- **No TodoWrite.** The request carries 12 direct tools: `subagent`, `shell`, `question`, `execute`, `Edit`, `Grep`, `Read`, `WebFetch`, `Glob`, `Write`, `Skill`, `WebSearch`. None is a todo tool, yet `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Task and completion discipline" requires "Use TodoWrite for multi-step work", and the Build+ prompt repeats it. On OpenCode 1 the same capture shows a 2,756-char `TodoWrite` tool.
- **Partial Code Mode catalogue.** The context states "The Code Mode tool catalog below is partial" and lists 16 callable paths (`aidevops`, `aidevops_bounded_operation`, `aidevops_hook_status`, `aidevops_mcp`, `aidevops_memory`, `aidevops_objective_receipt`, `aidevops_pre_edit_check`, `gpt_image_generate`, `model-accounts-pool`, five `browser` paths, `opencode.session_move`, `opencode.session_rename`). `ai-research`, `session-rename` and `osgrep`, which the guidance names, are reachable only through `search`, and nothing in the aidevops guidance says to call `search`.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** the fix is a product choice between adding a V2 tool, changing catalogue ordering, or making guidance runtime-aware, with prompt-cache and context-budget trade-offs.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR uses a closing keyword for this issue.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs:354-367` — the V2 `agent.transform`, `catalog.transform` and `tool.transform` registrations where a todo tool or catalogue priority would be added.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs` — cover the chosen registration.
- `EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md` — only if the chosen approach is runtime-aware guidance; keep the change pointer-sized under the size ratchet.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** the model reads the V2 tool list and Code Mode catalogue that `setupAidevopsV2` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs` registers, on every request.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** V2 `tool.transform` (`addV1ToolsToV2Editor`) and `catalog.transform` (`applyV2ContextBudget`) in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs`; live `context-budget-helper.sh capture oc2`.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because no schema or config change is expected.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/plugins/`; the OC2 config home loads it from the deployed path.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because tools and catalogue are built per session.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the change in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Confirm whether OpenCode 2.0.3 ships a todo tool that is disabled or renamed (inspect the installed `@opencode/plugin` 2.0.3 exports and the V2 CLI tool registry) before designing anything.
2. Choose the lowest-context fix: expose a native todo tool if one exists; otherwise add a pointer in guidance naming the V2 alternative.
3. For the catalogue, either prioritise the framework tools named in guidance in the visible catalogue, or add a one-line hint that other aidevops tools are found with `search({ namespace: "aidevops" })`.
4. Measure with `context-budget-helper.sh capture oc2` control against candidate and report the character delta (OC2 has no `llm_requests` rows until #32619).

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A because this is per-session tool registration.
- **Migration/rollback:** stateless; a revert restores current behaviour.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** OpenCode 1 behaviour must not change; keep the change behind the V2 entrypoint.
- **Idempotency/retry:** registration stays deterministic so the prompt-cache prefix is stable.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a missing V2 capability must fail open to current behaviour, never break session start.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs
.agents/scripts/context-budget-helper.sh capture oc2 --plugin .
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the adapter test proves the registration; the live capture proves the model-visible tool list and catalogue text.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An OpenCode 2 capture shows either a todo tool or guidance that names the OpenCode 2 alternative
- [ ] Framework tools named in guidance are in the visible Code Mode catalogue or covered by an explicit `search` hint
- [ ] The change does not alter OpenCode 1 captures, and the V2 adapter tests pass

  ```yaml

    method: bash
    run: "node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- The adapter test reads host `~/.config/aidevops/settings.json`; run it with `AIDEVOPS_SETTINGS_FILE` pointing to a missing file until that isolation is fixed.
- Non-goal: V2 observability rows (#32619) and built-in tool text trimming (#32622).

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs:354` — V2 transform registrations.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/on-demand-tools.mjs:13` — notes that OpenCode 2 defers plugin tools into Code Mode.
- `.agents/reference/context-budget.md` — capture and compare workflow.

| Implementation | 1h | registration or guidance pointer |

title: bug: ChatGPT OAuth model denylist matches exact IDs only, so dated snapshots of denied models pass
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `chatgpt oauth unsupported models denylist exact match` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs touch `model-availability-probe-lib.sh` or `model-routing-table.json`; the list was last set by GH#21990
- [x] File refs verified: 3 refs checked, all present at `main` 2a3130a4e
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple` — one matching rule in one function plus one existing test file
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — small change, worker can open the PR directly

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-27
- **Session:** opencode:interactive (GH#32632 context-budget session)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** While reviewing OpenAI routing during first-prompt context work, the ChatGPT OAuth denylist was found to match model IDs exactly, so a dated snapshot of a denied model is treated as available.

## What

`_chatgpt_oauth_denylist_check` also denies dated snapshot IDs of a listed model (for example `gpt-5.5-pro-2026-01-15` when `gpt-5.5-pro` is listed), while every model not derived from a listed ID stays allowed.

## Why

- `.agents/scripts/model-availability-probe-lib.sh:1015` compares `[[ "$model_id" == "$denied" ]]`, so only the four exact IDs in `.agents/configs/model-routing-table.json:73` are denied.
- OpenAI publishes dated snapshot IDs alongside aliases. A cached snapshot ID of a denied Pro model would pass the denylist and fail at inference with HTTP 400 or 404, which is exactly what GH#21990 set out to prevent.
- A broad `*-pro` rule is wrong: the comment at `.agents/configs/model-routing-table.json:72` records that `gpt-5.6-sol-pro` passed a live OAuth smoke test.
- Impact is low: current routing uses aliases, so this is a latent defect.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (from a repository checkout; presets the OAuth caches the library reads, then checks an exact ID and its dated snapshot):

```bash
source .agents/scripts/model-availability-probe-lib.sh
_OPENAI_OAUTH_AUTH_FILE_CACHE=.agents/configs/model-routing-table.json
_OPENAI_OAUTH_AUTH_TYPE_CACHE=oauth
for model in gpt-5.5-pro gpt-5.5-pro-2026-01-15; do
  if _chatgpt_oauth_denylist_check openai "$model"; then printf '%s denied\n' "$model"; else printf '%s allowed\n' "$model"; fi
done
```

**Actual output** (on `main` 2a3130a4e):

```text
gpt-5.5-pro denied
gpt-5.5-pro-2026-01-15 allowed
```

**Expected output** (after the fix):

```text
gpt-5.5-pro denied
gpt-5.5-pro-2026-01-15 denied
```

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** a single matching rule in one function with an existing focused test file; no design choice beyond the snapshot-suffix pattern.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR uses a closing keyword for this issue.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/model-availability-probe-lib.sh:1011-1019` — deny an exact match or `<denied>-YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-availability-oauth-probe.sh` — add cases for a dated snapshot (denied), an unrelated `-pro` model (allowed) and a prefix-only match such as `gpt-5.5-pro-max` (allowed).

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `check_model_available` calls `_chatgpt_oauth_denylist_check` before cache lookups (`.agents/scripts/model-availability-probe-lib.sh:998-999`).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A because the denylist in `.agents/configs/model-routing-table.json` is read-only config.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-model-availability-oauth-probe.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** no schema change; `openai_unsupported` keeps its array-of-IDs shape.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` and `.agents/configs/`; there is no generated copy.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because availability is re-evaluated on each check.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert `.agents/scripts/model-availability-probe-lib.sh` and its test.

### Implementation Steps

1. In the loop at `.agents/scripts/model-availability-probe-lib.sh:1013-1018`, keep the exact comparison and add a snapshot comparison: deny when `model_id` equals `denied` followed by `-` and an ISO date (`[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}`), using a Bash 3.2 compatible regex held in a variable.
2. Add the three test cases listed above to the existing test file.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A because the check is a pure function of its inputs.
- **Migration/rollback:** stateless; a revert restores exact matching.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** exact IDs behave as before; only dated snapshots of listed IDs change from allowed to denied.
- **Idempotency/retry:** repeated calls return the same result.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** an unreadable routing table still yields an empty denylist, as today.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-availability-oauth-probe.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/model-availability-probe-lib.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the focused test file covers denied snapshot, allowed unrelated Pro model and allowed prefix-only match.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/model-availability-probe-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-model-availability-oauth-probe.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dated snapshot of a listed model is denied under ChatGPT OAuth
- [ ] The check does not deny `gpt-5.6-sol-pro` or prefix-only matches such as `gpt-5.5-pro-max`

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-availability-oauth-probe.sh"
  ```

- [ ] ShellCheck and changed-file lint are clean

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "shellcheck .agents/scripts/model-availability-probe-lib.sh"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- Non-goal: pattern entries in `openai_unsupported`; explicit IDs plus the snapshot rule keep the list auditable.
- Non-goal: changing which models are listed.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/model-availability-probe-lib.sh:1000` — `_chatgpt_oauth_denylist_check`.
- `.agents/configs/model-routing-table.json:71` — `chatgpt_oauth_restrictions`.


**Actual output** (on `main` 2a3130a4e):

```text
✖ V2 setup registers SDK lifecycle hooks and disposes every registration
  + 'catalog:transform',
ℹ tests 16  pass 15  fail 1
```

**Expected output** (after the fix): 16 of 16 pass on any host; with `AIDEVOPS_SETTINGS_FILE` pointing to a missing file the same command passes today.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

Leaf issue: the PR uses a closing keyword for this issue.

title: planning-commit-helper complete from canonical edits TODO.md then fails publication (canonical guard blocks planning-PR fetch)
body:
## What

`planning-commit-helper.sh complete <task> --pr <N>` (and any `todo_commit_push` caller) run from the canonical checkout edits `TODO.md` in place, then fails to publish and leaves the canonical checkout dirty. When publication cannot proceed, the helper must either publish from an isolated linked worktree without mutating canonical, or refuse before editing.

## Why

Observed 2026-09-27 after merging PR #32642:

- `planning-commit-helper.sh complete t18495 --pr 32642` in the canonical aidevops checkout printed "Marked t18495 as complete" and then "Task completion publication failed; no successful direct push or planning PR was created".
- With `AIDEVOPS_LOG_FILE` set, `todo_commit_push` logged: "Default branch main requires PR publication for planning files" -> canonical guard "BLOCKED ... canonical worktree mutation via 'git fetch'" -> "Planning PR fallback failed: cannot fetch origin/main".
- `TODO.md` stayed modified in canonical and had to be preserved and converged with `canonical-recovery-helper.sh sync-mirror`. Completion was then published via `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --completion-bookkeeping` from a linked worktree (PR #32649).

The Build+ guidance says to auto-commit planning changes with this helper, so the interactive default path is broken whenever the canonical guard is active.

## How

- In `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh`, the planning-PR fallback (`_todo_create_planning_worktree`) fetches `origin/<default>` inside the caller repo. When the caller is the canonical checkout, run the fetch through the approved non-mutating path. Precedent: the isolated Git context in `claim-task-id-counter.sh` (`_claim_counter_prepare_git_context`, ~L225-287), or `canonical-recovery-helper.sh`.
- In `.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh` `complete_task` (~L250-315), classify the repo (canonical vs linked) before `_complete_task_update_todo`. For canonical, write the edit into the disposable planning worktree rather than the canonical `TODO.md`, or fail closed before editing. On any publication failure, restore the caller file so the canonical stays clean.
- Point the failure message at the working alternative (`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --completion-bookkeeping`) instead of a bare failure.

## Reference pattern

Model the canonical-safe fetch on `_claim_counter_prepare_git_context` in `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh` (classify the path via the canonical write-policy helper, then operate in a disposable context under `AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR`). Note t18494/GH#32617: that bare-context fetch can time out on this repo's size, so prefer a linked-worktree `git worktree add` from existing objects over a fresh bare fetch.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-commit-helper-protected-default-pr.sh`

## Acceptance

- Running `planning-commit-helper.sh complete <task> --pr <merged PR>` from a guarded canonical checkout either opens a planning PR or fails before modifying any canonical file; `git status --short` in canonical is empty afterwards in both cases.
- Linked-worktree behaviour is unchanged.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-commit-helper-protected-default-pr.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-todo-commit-home-fallback.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-pr-guard.sh` pass.
- Manual: from canonical, run `complete` for a task with a merged PR and confirm a clean canonical plus a planning PR.

title: feat: issue-sync refresh-body for generated auto-dispatch issue bodies, preserving signature and pulse feedback blocks
body:
## What

Add `issue-sync-helper.sh refresh-body <issue> --repo <owner/repo> --body-file <path> [--dry-run]`. It replaces an issue's authoritative body with a regenerated body file and keeps the blocks the framework added after creation: the `<!-- aidevops:origin:… -->` / `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` signature footer, and pulse-appended marker blocks such as `<!-- feedback-route:start:… -->` … `<!-- feedback-route:complete:… -->` merge-conflict feedback. It covers auto-dispatch issues without a task ID, which `sync-body` cannot.

## Why

- **Observed need (2026-09-27, one managed project):** a project-side issue factory writes one worker brief per item (`todo/<batch>/<slug>.issue.md`) and opens one auto-dispatch issue per item, with no task ID. After two contract fixes in one session, nine open issues needed their bodies refreshed from the regenerated files before workers claimed them. Two further hand-written second-pass issues needed the same rule added.
- **No framework path fits.** `issue-sync-helper.sh sync-body tNNN` (`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-body.sh`) requires a task-ID mapping and the `no-auto-dispatch` hold, and composes the body from TODO/brief. A plain `gh_issue_edit_safe --body-file` drops the signature footer and any pulse-appended conflict-feedback block that tells the next worker how to recover the previous PR.
- **What the ad-hoc script found** (about 60 lines in the session workspace; the steps are below):
  - footers of 4 lines were kept;
  - one issue carried a 46-line `feedback-route` conflict block after its footer, which had to survive;
  - one older body had no footer, and the edit path added a wrapper signature, so the body must not end up with two signatures;
  - an idempotency re-check reported a false difference, because `gh … --jq .body` adds a trailing newline.

## How

Reuse the held-body safety primitives in `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-body-common.sh`: `_body_sync_fetch_state`, `_body_sync_validate_state`, `_body_sync_state_digest`, `_body_sync_metadata_digest`, `_body_sync_has_nonself_claim`, `_body_sync_scan_file`, `_body_sync_canonical_body` and `_body_sync_hash_body`. Follow `_body_sync_apply` in `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-body.sh` as the reference pattern: re-read before writing, post-write verification and audit receipts.

1. Validate `--body-file`: a regular, non-empty file whose content passes `_body_sync_scan_file`.
2. Fetch the issue state. Refuse closed issues, a genuine non-self claim, and `status:queued`, `status:in-progress` or `status:in-review`, because a worker may be reading the body. Require admin or maintain authority, as `cmd_sync_body` does (keep the `#aidevops:trust-boundary` marker).
3. Split the current body:
   - **Preserved tail:** the signature footer, from the first `<!-- aidevops:origin:` line (or `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` when no origin marker exists) through the end of the footer's signature paragraph, plus every complete marker-delimited block the pulse appends (`feedback-route:start … feedback-route:complete`), in their original order.
   - **Replaceable head:** everything else.
4. Compose the new body: the new file content, then the preserved tail. If the new file already contains `<!-- aidevops:sig -->`, keep only the file's footer and the pulse blocks. Never emit two signature blocks.
5. Compare `_body_sync_canonical_body` hashes of the current and composed bodies. Equal means a verified no-op; trailing whitespace alone must not count as a change.
6. `--dry-run` prints the preserved-block counts, line counts and a unified diff, and exits 2 without writing.
7. Re-read the state and refuse if its digest changed. Then write with `gh_issue_edit_safe --body-file`, re-read, verify the body hash and that labels, assignees and state are unchanged, and record audit receipts with `operation=issue-body-refresh`.

### Files to modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-refresh.sh` — `cmd_refresh_body` and the split/compose helpers (a new file keeps `issue-sync-helper-body.sh` small).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` — source the new file, dispatch `refresh-body` next to `sync-body` (around line 488), and add it to `cmd_help`.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-refresh-body.sh` — stubbed `gh`, following `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-held-body.sh`.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/cross-runner-coordination.md` — document `refresh-body` beside the `sync-body` section (around line 367), and say when to use each.

## Acceptance

- Refreshing a body keeps the signature footer and every complete `feedback-route` block verbatim and in order, and appends them after the new content.
- A body file that already has a signature produces exactly one `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` block.
- A refresh whose result differs only by trailing whitespace is a verified no-op with no write.

- `--dry-run` writes nothing and exits 2.
- Audit receipts are recorded for write, no-op and block outcomes.

title: fix(release): exact-tag-deployment lane deadlocks when auto-update already deployed a descendant of the release commit
body:
## What

A release lane stuck in `exact-tag-deployment` deadlocks every later release when the local runtime was already drift-deployed to a newer `main` commit that contains the release commit. Let reconciliation finish that phase without rolling the runtime back and without weakening provenance.

## Why

Observed 2026-09-27 on a maintainer runner. v3.37.8 published to GitHub, npm (`3.37.8`) and Homebrew (`3.37.8`), and `RELEASE_REMOTE_STATE=published`. Before that, auto-update's same-version script-drift path had deployed `main` at `bffa6139`, a descendant of the release commit `45bbf61c`. `aidevops release reconcile 32639` then fails:

```text
Runtime bundle convergence failed: deployed SHA bffa61399bd2… does not match release commit 45bbf61c4184…
Post-release deployment gate could not verify the active runtime before deployment
PARTIAL RELEASE SUCCESS: GitHub release v3.37.8 remains published; post-publication gates failed
```

The lane stays `active` (`phase=exact-tag-deployment`), so `aidevops release patch <next-pr>` refuses with `ACTIVE_RELEASE_LANE source_pr=32639`. Every runner that auto-deploys `main` between tag push and reconcile hits this. Publication of already-merged fixes (here PR #32634) is blocked for the whole fleet until someone intervenes by hand.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
aidevops release reconcile <source-pr>   # after auto-update deployed a newer main
aidevops release patch <other-merged-pr> incremental
```

**Actual output**: the reconcile ends with `Runtime bundle convergence failed: deployed SHA … does not match release commit …`. The second command prints `ACTIVE_RELEASE_LANE source_pr=<source-pr> phase=exact-tag-deployment`.

**Expected**: the lane reaches a terminal receipt. Either reconcile deploys the exact tag from its detached worktree, as the release workflow describes, or it records the verified runtime that contains the release commit. Then the next release can reserve the lane.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/runtime-bundle-verifier.sh` (the check near line 219) and the post-release deployment gate caller in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh` / `version-manager` reconcile path: confirm whether the gate runs before the exact-tag deploy. If so, make reconcile perform the documented detached-tag deploy instead of pre-verifying the current runtime.
2. Alternatively, accept an active validated bundle whose manifest SHA descends from the release commit (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <release> <deployed>`), with the release sentinel files unchanged or verified. Record the actual deployed SHA in the terminal receipt.
3. Keep provenance, signature and channel verification unchanged.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/runtime-bundle-verifier.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/deploy-agents-on-merge.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-atomic-runtime-bundle-deploy.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-incremental-deploy-runtime-config.sh`

Integration scope correction: the gate is implemented in `version-manager-release.sh:853-1033`, not `full-loop-release-helper.sh` (which sources reconciliation). Its existing `test-agent-auto-sync.sh:824-1109` fixtures cover verified descendants and stale deployment stamps; changes there are required to distinguish a verified descendant from inconsistent provenance. No change to signature/channel verification is authorized.

Additional integration evidence: `deploy-agents-on-merge.sh:314-329,449-450,786-787` skips deployment on manifest ancestry alone, even if the stamp does not match the active bundle. The release gate correctly rejects this inconsistency but the deploy skip prevents repair. Require exact bundle convergence before any ancestor no-op, and exercise the existing atomic-deploy fixture; keep the exact release gate and all authentication checks fail-closed.

Existing `test-incremental-deploy-runtime-config.sh:85-92` explicitly tests the shortcut with a mock manifest/stamp; its fixture must model a validated bundle and exact stamp and assert the inconsistent-stamp repair path. This is the directly affected integration test.

## Acceptance

- With a runtime deployed from a descendant of the release commit, `aidevops release reconcile <pr>` writes a terminal receipt and deactivates the lane.
- A runtime not containing the release commit still fails closed.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-runtime-bundle-rollback.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh`

title: Pulse: auto worker cap (50% of cores) with one-time fleet reset of capacity overrides
body:
## What

Make the Pulse worker ceiling (`MAX_WORKERS_CAP`) an auto value: 50% of logical CPU cores, bounded by total RAM, clamped to [2, 64]. Ship a one-time setup migration that resets hand-tuned capacity overrides on every install so auto-update applies the new default fleet-wide without manual steps.

## Why

- Maintainer runners (other machines) report `Max Workers 2` on their supervisor dashboards. Stale per-machine overrides and a RAM-only formula leave capacity unused or starved.
- The throughput fixes in #32634 remove the old reasons for hand-tuned low or high ceilings. The maintainer decided on a one-time reset of all custom capacity settings to the new auto default.
- On macOS, `calculate_max_workers` counted only free+inactive pages. That under-reported reclaimable memory on busy Macs because it skipped speculative and purgeable file cache.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `aidevops config get orchestration.max_workers_cap` on a runner with a legacy override, then check the supervisor dashboard issue.

**Actual output:** the override value (for example `2` or `24`) is used regardless of core count, and the dashboard shows `Max Workers 2`.

**Expected:** with no override, the cap is `cores / 2` (for example 8 on a 16-core host), bounded by RAM.

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh`: auto cap from `hw.logicalcpu`/`nproc`, min'd with the RAM cap. Config value `0`/`auto`/empty selects auto. Floor lowered to 2.
- `EDIT: .agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc`, `.agents/configs/aidevops-config.schema.json`: `max_workers_cap` defaults to `0` (auto).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`: clamp `min_worker_concurrency` to `MAX_WORKERS_CAP` so the refill floor never exceeds the host ceiling.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh`: the macOS reclaimable RAM estimate adds speculative and purgeable pages.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh`: new `migrate_worker_capacity_reset`, modelled on `migrate_custom_model_routing_reasoning_defaults`.
  - Removes `orchestration.max_workers_cap`, `min_worker_concurrency` and `provider_account_slot_multiplier` from the user config.
  - Strips capacity env keys from `plist-env-overrides.json`.
  - Writes backups to `~/.aidevops/config-backups/migrations/`.
  - Uses a one-time marker in `~/.aidevops/cache/migrations/`, so later explicit settings are honoured.
- `EDIT: setup.sh`: run the migration in both the interactive and non-interactive paths.

## Acceptance

- Running setup without overrides resolves `MAX_WORKERS_CAP` to `cores/2` (bounded by RAM).
- An explicit config value still wins.
- The migration removes the legacy capacity overrides exactly once and keeps backups. A second run is a no-op.
- `shellcheck`, `linters-local.sh --changed`, `test-pulse-wrapper-worker-count.sh` and `test-model-routing-reasoning-migration.sh` pass.

body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `platform-fix regression evidence keyword false positive plugin tests` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs or issues touch `platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh`; last change `3bdcfd092` (#29421, origin #29416)
- [x] File refs verified: 6 refs checked, all present at `main` fe3cb09b5
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple` — one script, one existing test file, one doc paragraph; exact behaviour specified below
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — small change, worker can open the PR directly

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-27
- **Session:** opencode:interactive (GH#32632 full loop)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** PR #32639 failed the non-required "Platform Fix Regression Evidence" check although it changed no platform behaviour. The only platform words were in its `## Runtime Testing` narrative, and it changed a plugin test that the gate does not recognise.

## What

The Platform Fix Regression Evidence gate triggers on platform-fix claims (title and summary text), not on platform words inside testing/verification narrative. It also accepts a changed test in any repository test directory, including `.agents/plugins/*/tests/`.

## Why

- `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md:65-68` scopes the gate to PRs that "claim Linux/macOS or coreutils portability fixes". The implementation scans the whole title plus body (`.agents/scripts/platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh:153-154`) with a plain keyword regex (`:23-27`), so a passing mention anywhere triggers it.
- `_platform_changed_test` (`:29-41`) accepts only `.agents/scripts/tests/*`. The repository also has `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/` (93 files), `.agents/tests/`, `tests/` and `packages/*/tests/`.
- Recent failures (last 60 runs: 3 failures; wider failure list checked):

  | PR | Trigger words and location | Test changed | Classification |
  |----|----------------------------|--------------|----------------|
  | #32639 | "macOS", "Linux" only in `## Runtime Testing` | plugin test | false positive |
  | #32540 | "macOS"/"Linux" in summary and testing text | plugin test | author hand-wrote rationale: "not a platform shell fix" |
  | #32405 | "macOS" in summary | plugin test | author hand-wrote rationale: a shell test "would not execute this code path" |
  | #32664 | `hw.logicalcpu` (macOS) / `nproc` (Linux) in summary | none | correct trigger |
  | #32594 | macOS `/proc` fix | — | correct trigger |

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (on `main` fe3cb09b5, from the repository root):

```bash

printf '%s\n' '## Summary' 'Adds a JavaScript skill-catalogue helper.' '## Runtime Testing' 'One unrelated test fails on every macOS host; Linux CI runs the full suites.' > "$repro_dir/body.md"

```

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** one self-contained CI policy script with an existing table of cases; the section-skipping loop mirrors `_platform_has_regression_evidence` in the same file.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR uses a closing keyword for this issue.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/platform-fix-regression-evidence.sh:23-41,153-157,171` — build the trigger text from the title plus non-evidence body sections; widen the accepted test paths; update the error message.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add `_platform_trigger_text TITLE BODY_FILE`. Print the title, then every body line except:

title: Raise the minimum routed reasoning effort to medium for every model
body:
## What

Make `medium` the lowest reasoning effort the framework selects for any routed model. This covers headless workers, OpenCode child roles and the specialist advisor.

- A model whose variants cannot express `medium` uses its lowest thinking-enabled variant. Claude Haiku 4.5 has only budget variants, so it uses `high`.
- A model with no known variant keeps its provider default, and the docs say so.

## Why

- **Maintainer decision (2026-09-27):** low effort does not serve the framework's outcome goals; medium is the minimum on any model.
- **Observed runs:** a managed project's 18 standard-tier worker attempts on 2026-09-27 all ran `openai/gpt-5.6-terra` with `variant: low`, per `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`.
  - Outcomes: 13 blocked, 2 premature exits and 3 completions (2 PR handoffs, 1 draft checkpoint).
  - Several stops were on conditions worker guidance says to handle, for example dependencies installable from the lockfile.
  - Completed runs deferred required work.
  - Brief and environment defects also contributed, so this is not a controlled comparison. It is consistent with `tools/context/model-routing.md`, which already records that "Luna low and Terra low under-spec bounded work".
- **Partial custom tables fall through to low.** A local `custom/configs/model-routing-table.json` that sets reasoning for only some models falls through to the shipped table's `low` for the rest.
  - Observed: a custom standard tier set Sonnet 5 to `medium`, while Terra still resolved to `low` and ran every attempt.
  - A minimum must therefore be a framework floor, not per-model entries each user has to remember.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`. The decision is made; implementation spans shipped tables, two resolvers, plugin roles, docs and tests.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/configs/model-routing-table.json`:
  - simple: Luna `low` → `medium`, and add Haiku 4.5 `high`;
  - standard: Sol, Terra and Sonnet 5 `low` → `medium`;
  - `specialist_advisor`: Astra `low` → `medium`;
  - update the `_defaults` note ("GPT-6 Sol is standard at low and thinking at medium").
- `EDIT: .agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc:248-260`: mirror the same tier reasoning.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-model-tier.sh`:
  - `model_tier_variant` (274–314): apply a floor after table lookup, so an omitted model resolves to `medium`, not a lower shipped value.
  - `model_tier_next_variant` (320–347): escalation ladders start at `medium`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`, `resolve_headless_variant` (486–539):
  - raise env overrides below the floor (`AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_VARIANT`, `_<TIER>`, `_WORKER_`, `_PULSE_`) to it, with a warning;
  - confirm that the GPT-5.5 standard omission (`_headless_variant_should_omit_gpt55_standard`) leaves that model at or above medium by default, or remove the omission.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-effort-handlers.mjs:60`: domain roles pick `low` for simple and `domain-light`; use `medium`, still clamped to the observed parent variant.

title: Dispatch credential-dependent issues only to runners holding the named secrets
body:
## What

Let an auto-dispatch issue declare the secret names its work needs. The pulse then claims it only on a runner whose secret store holds every named secret. Runners that lack a secret skip the issue without claiming it, posting lease comments or recording a blocked attempt.

## Why

On 2026-09-27, in one managed project with three runners, credential-dependent issues repeatedly went to a runner without the credentials:

- A catalogue data-correction issue needing scoped database SSH secrets was claimed. It ended `permission_required` after about 4 minutes, and its status flipped from blocked back to available.
- A media-publication issue needing admin publication secrets was claimed. The worker built plans, then ended `permission_required`. Its private capture and plans cannot be reused by another runner, because plans are never replayed, so the next runner repeats the capture.
- An earlier media-publication issue on the same runner closed through a tooling-only PR with `Resolves`. Nothing was published, and the acceptance criteria were unmet. It needed a manual review and a follow-up issue.
- Meanwhile a runner that holds those secrets stayed available. Each misrouted attempt costs a full worker session plus lease and claim comment churn.

The issue bodies already say "without admin credentials, stop after a dry run and post for a maintainer runner". That makes the failure graceful, but not productive.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`. The design below is decided; implementation touches candidate filtering, the label convention and docs.

## How

### Design

- **Declaration:** one label per required secret name, `needs-secret:<NAME>`, carrying names only and never values. Alternatively, a body marker `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets NAME1 NAME2 -->` when label count or name exposure matters. Support both, with the label taking precedence.
- **Runner check:** before claiming, the pulse compares the declared names with the local secret store's name list (`aidevops secret list`, names only). If any is missing, it skips the candidate silently: no claim, no comment, no blocked attempt. It logs one line per cycle.
- **Starvation guard:** if no runner claims a `needs-secret:*` issue for a configurable period (default 24 h), post one comment naming the missing secret names and add `status:blocked` with a reason. Never repeat that comment.
- **Privacy:** secret names can reveal internal naming. The body-marker form must be allowed in public repos; the check reads names only.

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`: candidate filter hook; follow the existing skip-reason pattern used for other non-claimable candidates.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh`: final pre-claim check, so a race cannot claim without the secrets.
- `EDIT` or `NEW`: a small helper that returns declared names and checks them against `aidevops secret list` output.
  - It must never read values: the store's name listing only.
  - Reference: existing secret-name handling in `.agents/scripts/` (search `secret list`).
- `EDIT: .agents/workflows/brief.md` and `.agents/reference/task-lifecycle.md`: document the declaration for briefs whose verification or publication needs credentials.
- `EDIT`: tests beside the candidate filter tests (for example `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`): skip without secrets, claim with secrets, and the starvation comment posted once.

## Verification

- With a stub secret-name list lacking one declared name, the candidate is skipped and no GitHub write happens.
- With all names present, the normal claim path runs.
- After the starvation period, exactly one comment is posted and `status:blocked` is applied.
- `shellcheck` is clean on changed scripts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Issues declaring secret names are claimed only by runners that hold every named secret.
- [ ] Runners without them make no GitHub writes for the issue.
- [ ] Starvation surfaces once, with the missing names, and no values.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/brief.md`
- `.agents/reference/task-lifecycle.md`

title: feat(log-issue): accept a body file for fingerprint commands and name the matched readiness placeholder
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `log-issue-helper fingerprint body-file placeholder unfilled readiness code span` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `log-issue-helper.sh search` for "fingerprint body-file" and "placeholder unfilled readiness" found no open duplicates; closed #28442/#28446 fixed a different placeholder false positive (generated HTML wrappers)
- [x] File refs verified: 11 files checked, all present and unchanged at `main` a1f9e9336
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple` — two helpers, two existing test files, one workflow doc; exact behaviour specified below
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — small change, worker can open the PR directly

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-27
- **Session:** opencode:interactive (log-issue follow-ups after the GH#32632 full loop)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Filing #32667 hit two frictions in the log-issue flow:
  - Step 5.5/6.5 require the full issue body as a command argument. OpenCode's Bash policy blocks command substitution and multiline commands, so the steps could only be followed through a throwaway wrapper script.
  - Brief readiness reported `placeholder:unfilled` without naming the token. Finding it took a read of the helper source and a search of the brief.

## What

1. `log-issue-helper.sh check-fingerprint` and `record-fingerprint` accept `--body-file PATH` as an alternative to the positional body argument.
2. When a schema-v2 brief fails the unfilled-placeholder check, `brief-readiness-helper.sh check` also prints `PLACEHOLDER_MATCH=TOKEN`, naming the first matching token.

## Why

- The workflow tells agents to run `check-fingerprint "EXACT_TITLE" "EXACT_BODY"` and `record-fingerprint "EXACT_TITLE" "EXACT_BODY" N` (`.agents/workflows/log-issue-aidevops.md:289-293,362-366`). The helper reads the body only from argv (`.agents/scripts/log-issue-helper.sh:526-547`). The fingerprint hashes the whole normalised body (`.agents/scripts/lib/issue-fingerprint.sh:50-55`), so a shortened or paraphrased body silently misses duplicates.
- Step 6 already requires writing the body to an absolute file with the Write tool (`log-issue-aidevops.md:310-317`). Reusing that file for the fingerprint steps removes the argv requirement and guarantees the hashed body is the posted body.
- `_validate_v2_body` appends only `placeholder:unfilled;` (`.agents/scripts/brief-readiness-helper.sh:345`). The regex in `_has_unfilled_placeholder` (`:205-215`) runs on prose that already excludes inline code spans and fenced blocks (`.agents/scripts/brief-readiness-parser.awk:101-108`). So any match is real prose, but the author has to reverse-engineer which one. Observed case: an unbackticked `.agents/plugins/<name>/tests/` inside quoted error text.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** argument parsing in one CLI dispatcher, plus one extra output line from an existing validation function; both follow patterns already in the same files.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR uses a closing keyword for this issue.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/log-issue-helper.sh:526-547,560-561,571-572` — parse `--body-file` in both subcommands and update the help and examples.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/brief-readiness-helper.sh:205-215,345` — extract the first matching token and print `PLACEHOLDER_MATCH=` from `_validate_v2_body`.
- `EDIT: .agents/workflows/log-issue-aidevops.md:284-317,357-366` — write the body file before Step 5.5 and use `--body-file` in Steps 5.5 and 6.5.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-fingerprint.sh` — add CLI cases for both body forms.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-readiness.sh:862-868` — extend the T30 area with `PLACEHOLDER_MATCH` assertions.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `.agents/scripts/framework-routing-helper.sh:292,396` call `check_recent_filing`/`record_filing` directly and are unaffected. `.agents/scripts/new-task-helper.sh:534` and `.agents/scripts/task-brief-helper.sh:639` grep only `WORKER_READY=true`. `_is_worker_ready` discards validation output (`brief-readiness-helper.sh:377`).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `record_filing` (`log-issue-helper.sh:281-310`) appends to `~/.aidevops/state/log-issue-fingerprints.jsonl`; the record format does not change.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-fingerprint.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-readiness.sh` (T21 code-span case, T30/T31 placeholder cases).
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because the JSONL record and existing readiness keys stay unchanged; one optional output line is added.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `.agents/scripts/commands/log-issue-aidevops.md` is a symlink to the workflow doc (git mode 120000), so it needs no separate edit. The deployed runtime updates through `setup.sh`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the same body yields the same hash, so existing fingerprint records stay valid.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** N/A because reverting restores the argv-only form and the current output.

### Implementation Steps

1. In the `check-fingerprint` branch of `main` (`log-issue-helper.sh:526-536`):
   - if `$3` is `--body-file`, require a readable regular file at `$4` and read it into `body`;
   - otherwise keep the positional form.
2. Apply the same parsing to `record-fingerprint` (`:537-547`), taking the issue number from `$5` in the `--body-file` form.
3. For a missing or unreadable path, print a usage error to stderr and return 1, without printing `OK` or writing a record.
4. Update the help text (`:560-561`) and examples (`:571-572`) to show both forms.
5. In `brief-readiness-helper.sh`, add `_first_unfilled_placeholder`:
   - print the first `grep -oiE` match of the existing regex over `_brief_prose_text`, truncated to 80 characters;
   - reuse it from `_has_unfilled_placeholder` so the regex exists in one place.
6. At `:345`, when a match exists, print `PLACEHOLDER_MATCH=` followed by the token before the `VALIDATION_ERRORS=` line. `cmd_check` already prints the captured validation output verbatim (`:468,481`).
7. In the workflow doc:
   - move the Write-tool body-file instruction ahead of Step 5.5;
   - switch the Step 5.5 and 6.5 examples to `check-fingerprint "EXACT_TITLE" --body-file "/absolute/path/to/aidevops-issue-body.md"` and the matching `record-fingerprint` form.
8. Add tests:
   - with `HOME` set to a temp directory, a record written through `--body-file` is reported as `DUPLICATE:` by the positional form, and the reverse;
   - a missing body file exits non-zero and leaves the state file untouched;
   - T30's body prints `PLACEHOLDER_MATCH=` with the path token, while a ready brief does not print that key.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** unchanged; `record_filing` keeps its single `printf` append.
- **Migration/rollback:** revert-only; no stored state changes shape.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** the workflow doc and helper ship in the same runtime bundle. An older helper would hash the literal string `--body-file` as the body, so do not split this change across PRs.
- **Idempotency/retry:** `check-fingerprint` is read-only. `record-fingerprint` appends one line per call, as today.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** an unreadable body file fails before hashing, so an empty-body fingerprint is never recorded.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-fingerprint.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-readiness.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/log-issue-helper.sh .agents/scripts/brief-readiness-helper.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** the fingerprint tests drive `log-issue-helper.sh`, the same entry point the workflow calls. The readiness tests drive `brief-readiness-helper.sh check`, which `verify-brief-helper.sh check-readiness` wraps.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/log-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/brief-readiness-helper.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/log-issue-aidevops.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-fingerprint.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-readiness.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `check-fingerprint "T" --body-file F` detects a record written by `record-fingerprint "T" "BODY" N` when F contains BODY, and vice versa
- [ ] A missing or unreadable `--body-file` path exits non-zero and does not print `OK` or append a record
- [ ] The positional body form and the direct function calls in `framework-routing-helper.sh` keep working unchanged
- [ ] A v2 brief failing `placeholder:unfilled` prints `PLACEHOLDER_MATCH=` with the first matched token; a brief without placeholders must not print that key
- [ ] Angle-bracket tokens inside inline code spans or fenced blocks still do not trigger `placeholder:unfilled` (T21 keeps passing)
- [ ] Log-issue workflow Steps 5.5 and 6.5 show the `--body-file` form, reusing the Step 6 body file

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-fingerprint.sh"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- Non-goal: changing the placeholder regex or the fingerprint normalisation.
- Non-goal: automatic fingerprinting inside the `gh` shim; the explicit workflow steps remain the contract.
- Correction of an earlier in-session hypothesis: code spans were suspected of triggering the placeholder check, but the prose parser strips them (`brief-readiness-parser.awk:105`). Only the diagnostic gap remains.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/log-issue-helper.sh:242` — `check_recent_filing`.
- `.agents/scripts/brief-readiness-helper.sh:205` — `_has_unfilled_placeholder`.
- `.agents/workflows/log-issue-aidevops.md:284` — Step 5.5 fingerprint pre-check.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** none
- **External:** none

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Implementation | 30m | argument parsing, token extraction, doc steps |
| Verification | 20m | CLI dedup cases, readiness assertions, shellcheck |
| **Total** | **~50m** | |

title: fix(release): release status errors on not-requested receipt while same-source lane is active
body:
## Task

`aidevops release status <PR>` fails with `Cannot reconcile terminal release:not-requested evidence for PR #N` while a release for that PR is queued and actively progressing. The release is healthy, but the error looks like a terminal failure and led the release child to report an anomaly. Status should report the active lane state (queued / pending release PR checks) instead of failing.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `aidevops release status 32657` (while release PR #32673 was waiting on required checks)

**Actual output:** `Cannot reconcile terminal release:not-requested evidence for PR #32657` (non-zero exit)

**Expected output:** lane state, e.g. `RELEASE_LANE={"active":true,"source_pr":32657,"phase":"remote-publication",...}` plus a queued/pending result

Observed during the v3.37.9 release (source PR #32657, release PR #32673):

1. Merge PR #32657 with `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, then run `full-loop-helper.sh record-no-release 32657 marcusquinn/aidevops`. The receipt is now `release:not-requested`.
2. Later, with explicit release intent, run `aidevops release patch 32657 incremental`. It exits 8 (`release:queued`), creates the protected release PR #32673, and records the lane `{"active":true,"source_pr":32657,"phase":"remote-publication","tag":"v3.37.9","terminal_receipt":null}`.
3. While #32673 is still waiting on required checks, `aidevops release status 32657` prints `Cannot reconcile terminal release:not-requested evidence for PR #32657` and exits non-zero. The release child also reported that `aidevops release reconcile 32657` failed the same way at that point. This was not re-run in isolation, so treat it as unconfirmed.
4. After #32673 merged and tag v3.37.9 was pushed, `aidevops release reconcile 32657` succeeded (`RELEASE_RECEIPT=not-requested`, then `release:published tag=v3.37.9`). `status` then reported the lane as terminal (`superseded`).

Likely cause: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` around lines 1461-1485 accepts `mode=status`. When the receipt is `release:not-requested`, it only allows `mode=reconcile` (line 1478) and prints the "Cannot reconcile" error for `status`, even though an active lane owned by the same source PR exists. The docs say `release:not-requested` may move to `release:published` or `release:superseded` through a later authorized release without asking again (`.agents/scripts/commands/full-loop.md` step 4.6).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`

## How

In `full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`, `status` mode with a `release:not-requested` receipt: if an active lane is owned by the same source PR, report the lane/queue state (or `release:queued`) as read-only output instead of erroring. Keep refusing to change the receipt from `status`.

Tests: if an existing fixture in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh` or `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh` already covers `status` with a `not-requested` receipt, extend that case. Do not add new test infrastructure.

## Reference pattern

The `reconcile`-mode branch at `full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:1477-1490` (`_full_loop_release_validate_explicit_reconciliation_intent`) shows how an existing `not-requested` receipt is reconciled against an active authorized lane. Status should reuse the same lane read without the mutation.

## Acceptance criteria

- While a same-source release lane is active, `aidevops release status <PR>` exits 0 or 8 (pending) with lane/queue output, not the "Cannot reconcile terminal release:not-requested" error.
- `status` never changes the receipt. With no active lane and no tag, `not-requested` is still reported as not-requested.
- `reconcile` behaviour is unchanged. Confirm whether the pre-merge `reconcile` failure in step 3 reproduces, and fix it in the same change if it does.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`

- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — contained change with an existing 82-test suite

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-28
- **Session:** opencode:interactive (log-issue follow-ups after the GH#32632 full loop)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Filing #32679 was blocked by the OpenCode signature gate with `body-file not found (for: ENOENT … lstat '…/for')`. The issue title contained the text `--body-file for …`, and the hook took the word after that text as the body path. Rewording the title let the same command through.

See-also: #32679

## What

The OpenCode signature-footer hook finds the `--body-file` and `--body` arguments only outside quoted strings, so text inside `--title "…"` or another quoted value is never treated as a flag.

## Why

- `tryRepairSignature` runs an unanchored regex over the raw command string (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs:231-233`) and uses the first match. A quoted title that mentions the flag wins over the real argument. The repair then fails with `FILE_NOT_FOUND` and `checkSignatureFooterGate` throws (`:288-300`), blocking a valid, well-formed `gh` write before the exec-time PATH shim can run.
- `_hasUnparseableBody` (`:130-137`) locates the body with the same kind of unanchored search (`:131`). A title mentioning `--body` followed by `$(` or backticks elsewhere can misclassify the command as `UNPARSEABLE_BODY`.
- The hook's mentoring message then points at the wrong cause, "created later in this same bash call", which sends agents down a false fix path.
- The PATH shim already parses real argv (`.agents/scripts/gh:888-905`), so only the plugin hook is affected.
- Titles that mention CLI flags are common for framework issues and PRs, e.g. "accept --body-file for …".

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (from the repository root on `main` a1f9e9336):

```bash
node --input-type=module -e '
import { mkdtempSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { tryRepairSignature } from "./.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs";
const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "sig-title-"));
const body = join(dir, "body.md");
writeFileSync(body, "probe body\n");
for (const title of ["feat: accept --body-file for fingerprints", "feat: accept a body file for fingerprints"]) {
  const cmd = `gh issue create -R owner/repo --title "${title}" --body-file ${body}`;
  const out = tryRepairSignature(cmd, "./.agents/scripts", () => {}, { commandWorkdir: dir });
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ title, status: out.status, reason: out.reason ?? null }));
}
'
```

**Actual output** (same body file; only the title differs):

```text
{"title":"feat: accept --body-file for fingerprints","status":"fail","reason":"body-file not found (may be created later in this same bash call)"}
{"title":"feat: accept a body file for fingerprints","status":"ok","reason":null}
```

**Expected output**: both lines report `"status":"ok"`.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: the OpenCode `tool.execute.before` Bash hook calls `checkSignatureFooterGate` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs:251`).
- **Call chain**: `checkSignatureFooterGate` (`quality-hooks-signature.mjs:266`) → `tryRepairSignature` (`:276`) → `--body-file` regex (`:231-233`) matches inside the quoted title → `repairBodyFile` (`quality-hooks-signature-body-file.mjs`) returns `FILE_NOT_FOUND` → throw (`quality-hooks-signature.mjs:300`).
- **Integrated verification**: the reproducer calls the exported function that the hook uses, and `tests/test-signature-footer-gate.mjs` covers the same export.

## Workarounds Applied

- Reworded the #32679 title from "accept --body-file …" to "accept a body file …" and reran the same `gh issue create`; it was signed and posted normally.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** a small scanner, but it decides which file a provenance gate signs. The fix must keep every existing fail-closed path (heredoc, process substitution, command substitution, symlink and root checks).

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR uses a closing keyword for this issue.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs:130-137,150-164,230-243` — find body arguments from unquoted tokens only.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-signature-footer-gate.mjs:417-430` — add quoted-title cases next to the existing body-file repair test.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `checkSignatureFooterGate` (`quality-hooks-signature.mjs:266-302`) is the only production caller of `tryRepairSignature`, and `quality-hooks.mjs:114,123,251` wires it into the Bash hook.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `repairBodyFile` appends the footer to the resolved body file, and `_repairBodyArg` rewrites the inline `--body` value (`:180-199`). Both must receive the real argument only.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-signature-footer-gate.mjs` (82 passing at a1f9e9336).
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because no configuration or `FAIL_REASON` values change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** N/A because the plugin runs from the deployed runtime bundle, which `setup.sh` refreshes; there is no generated copy in the repository.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the hook is stateless.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** N/A because reverting restores the current regex matching.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add `_unquotedTokens(cmd)`. It returns `{ text, start }` tokens split on unquoted whitespace and shell separators (`;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`) with these quoting rules:
   - single quotes: literal content, no escapes;
   - double quotes: backslash escapes the next character;
   - backslash outside quotes: escapes the next character;
   - any other character: ordinary.

   Model the argument walk on `.agents/scripts/gh:888-905`.
2. Replace the regex at `:231-233` with the first unquoted token equal to `--body-file` (value = the next token, with quotes removed) or starting with `--body-file=`.
3. In `_hasUnparseableBody`, compute `bodyStart` from the first unquoted `--body`, `--body-file`, `--comment` or `-c` token instead of `cmd.search` (`:131`). Keep the heredoc and process-substitution test (`:134`) unchanged, so those forms stay blocked.
4. In `_matchBodyArg`, start matching at the first unquoted `--body`/`--comment`/`-c` token offset, so a quoted title containing `--body "x"` cannot be rewritten.
5. Add tests:
   - a title containing `--body-file for x` plus a real `--body-file` → `ok`, and the real file is signed;
   - the same title plus a real inline `--body "text"` → `ok`, with the signature added to the inline body only;
   - a title containing `--body-file` with no real body argument → still `BODY_ARG_NO_MATCH`;
   - an existing heredoc case still yields `UNPARSEABLE_BODY`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A because the hook runs synchronously per tool call.
- **Migration/rollback:** revert-only; no state involved.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** the exec-time PATH shim (`.agents/scripts/gh`) is unchanged and remains the backstop for body files created in the same call.
- **Idempotency/retry:** unchanged; signed bodies are detected by `SIG_MARKER` before any append.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if the scanner finds no body argument, the existing `BODY_ARG_NO_MATCH` block still fires. Unbalanced quotes must produce no body token and therefore block, never sign an arbitrary path.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-signature-footer-gate.mjs
```

- **Surface mapping:** the test file imports `tryRepairSignature` and `checkSignatureFooterGate` from the production module that the Bash hook calls. The Reproducer command should print `"status":"ok"` for both titles.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-signature-footer-gate.mjs`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `gh issue create` whose quoted title contains `--body-file` text signs and passes the real `--body-file` argument
- [ ] A quoted title containing `--body-file` text alongside a real inline `--body` repairs the inline body
- [ ] Commands with no real body argument still fail with `BODY_ARG_NO_MATCH`; quoted text must not satisfy the gate
- [ ] Heredoc, process-substitution and command-substitution bodies are still blocked as `UNPARSEABLE_BODY`, and the allowed-root and symlink checks do not change
- [ ] All 82 existing signature-gate tests keep passing

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-signature-footer-gate.mjs"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- Non-goal: a full shell parser; the scanner covers quoting and separators only, and it fails closed for anything it cannot classify.
- Non-goal: changing `isGhWriteCommand` detection (fixed separately in #20735) or the PATH shim.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs:231` — body-file regex.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature-failures.mjs:18` — `FILE_NOT_FOUND` message.
- `.agents/scripts/gh:888` — argv-based reference parsing.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** none
- **External:** none

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Implementation | 45m | scanner plus three call-site changes |
| Verification | 20m | four new cases, full suite, reproducer |
| **Total** | **~1h** | |
