title: setup: migrate_old_backups deletes all one-time migration backups on every setup run
body:
## What

`migrate_old_backups` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh`) runs first on every `setup.sh` run, including auto-update deploys. When `~/.aidevops/config-backups/` has no legacy `20*` snapshot directories, it runs `rm -rf` on the whole directory. That directory is also where one-time migrations keep their pre-change backups (`config-backups/migrations/`). As a result, every migration backup is deleted on the next setup run.

Affected backups: `t18137-model-routing-table.json`, `t31849-settings.json`, `gh32592-agents-md/`, `gh32663-config.jsonc`, `gh32663-plist-env-overrides.json`.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `ls ~/.aidevops/config-backups/migrations/` after any migration that writes a backup, followed by one more `setup.sh --non-interactive` run (for example, the next auto-update deploy).

**Actual output:** `ls: ~/.aidevops/config-backups/: No such file or directory`. On a maintainer machine the `gh32663-worker-capacity-reset` marker exists (written 22:15Z), but the `gh32663-config.jsonc` backup and the older t18137 backup are gone.

**Expected:** migration backups survive later setup runs.

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh`: in `migrate_old_backups`, remove only legacy `20*` snapshot directories, and `rmdir` the parent only when it is empty.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-routing-reasoning-migration.sh`: after a migration writes its backup, run `migrate_old_backups` and assert the backup survives.

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-routing-reasoning-migration.sh` passes. The new assertion fails on the old code.
- `shellcheck` is clean.

title: pulse: dispatch target ignores lowered MAX_WORKERS_CAP until preflight rewrites the stale cache
body:
## What

`get_max_workers_target` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh:35`) returns the cached `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-max-workers` value. Only the `preflight_capacity` stage (`calculate_max_workers`) rewrites that cache. Refill and drain dispatch (`pulse_event_refill_drain`) runs before preflight, so a lowered `MAX_WORKERS_CAP` is ignored until a full cycle completes preflight.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** after the GH#32663 reset (auto cap resolves to 8 on a 16-core host), check `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-max-workers` and the latest `Dispatch_capacity` line in `pulse.log`.

**Actual output:** `pulse-max-workers` = `24`, last written at 21:29:57Z, before the migration ran at 22:15Z. The cycles at 22:44, 22:54 and 23:03 log `Dispatch_capacity: … simultaneous_target_raw=24 … min_floor=6`: the min floor picked up the reset (10→6) but the ceiling did not.

**Expected:** the dispatch target never exceeds the live `MAX_WORKERS_CAP`.

## How

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh`: in `get_max_workers_target`, clamp the cached value to `MAX_WORKERS_CAP` when it is a positive integer.

## Acceptance

- With a stale cache of 24 and `MAX_WORKERS_CAP=8`, the function returns 8.
- With a cap of 32, it returns 24 (the RAM-derived cache still bounds it).
- With the cap unset, it returns 24 (behaviour unchanged).

title: pulse: cycle-entry refill drain runs unbounded dispatch and the process exits before preflight stages
body:
## What

On a maintainer macOS runner (v3.37.9), each Pulse cycle since about 21:30Z runs only the cycle-entry event-refill drain (`pulse_event_refill_drain "cycle-entry"`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1668`). The process then exits during that drain's `apply_dispatch_max`, never reaching `_run_preflight_stages` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1510`). The watchdog then revives it about 9–10 minutes after each start.

Consequences:

- `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` and `preflight_capacity` have not run since 21:29:57Z / 21:30:26Z (`pulse-stage-timings.log`).
- The `pulse-max-workers` cache is never recomputed (see #32686).
- The full merge and dispatch pipeline is effectively limited to one drain pass per revival.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:**

- `rg -n "preflight_capacity" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log | tail -3`
- `rg -n "pulse-event-refill\] action=" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -8`
- `tail -8 ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-watchdog.log`

**Actual output:**

- The last `preflight_capacity` is at `2026-09-27T21:30:26Z`.
- The refill log shows `action=drain_started source=cycle-entry pass=1` at 22:44:33, 22:54:20 and 23:03:49, with **no** matching `drain_completed` or `drain_failed`.
- The watchdog logs `pulse dead for 900s … reviving` at 22:44:05, `523s` at 22:53:10 and `547s` at 23:03:15.
- Stage timings for the drain cycles (PIDs 21201, 51878, 94506) contain only `dispatch_candidate_*` rows, at 33–244s each and 9–11 candidates per drain. Each cycle ends with two `pulse-health.json written` lines (exit trap) and no stage after the drain.

**Expected:** the drain completes (or is time-bounded) and the cycle continues into preflight, merge and the dispatch rounds.

## Investigation pointers (unconfirmed root cause)

- `pulse_event_refill_drain` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh:303`) calls the full `apply_dispatch_max` with no time budget. With about 10 candidates at 50–240s each, a drain takes 9–15 minutes.
- The watchdog (`.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog-tick.sh`) only revives when `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh is-running` is false, so something ends the process first. Candidates: a lifecycle or launchd runtime bound, a `run_stage_with_timeout` parent kill, or the auto-update bundle switch. On 22:05–22:14 the log shows `wake_skipped reason=inactive-bundle`.
- Check `pulse-wrapper.log` and `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` for a max-runtime or kill path, and confirm how the process exits (signal vs clean exit) before changing behaviour.

## How

Approach:

- In `pulse-event-refill.sh`, bound the cycle-entry drain, either with a candidate or time budget, or by skipping the drain on cycle entry since the full cycle dispatches anyway.
- The exact kill path is unknown. Confirm it from logs first.
- If the root cause is in `pulse-wrapper.sh` or `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` (both large files), file a follow-up rather than widening this scope. Bounding the drain alone restores preflight.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh`

## Acceptance

- After deploy, `pulse-stage-timings.log` shows `preflight_capacity` in every full cycle.
- `pulse.log` shows `drain_completed` for cycle-entry drains.
- The watchdog stops reviving a Pulse that was mid-cycle.

title: t18496: fix(dispatch): stop false missing_files_scope holds and auto-release repaired briefs
body:
## What

The pre-claim brief-scope gate (GH#32579, GH#32598) held 7 of 49 auto-dispatch issues created on 2026-09-27 as `status:blocked` (`missing_files_scope`). Those briefs were valid and followed the template. Stop the false holds and let repaired briefs resume on their own.

## Why

Evidence (open issues #32627, #32652, #32658, #32661, #32662, #32672, #32677):

1. `.agents/templates/brief-template.md:299` recommends `` `EDIT: path/to/existing.ts:45-60` ``, but `.agents/scripts/brief_scope.py` `exact()` rejects the `:45-60` line-range suffix. 4 of the 5 bodies the normalizer rejects fail on this alone.
2. The pulse gate (`_dispatch_preclaim_brief_scope` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`) checks the raw body. `claim-task-id.sh` normalizes "Files to Modify" into a Files Scope first, so the same brief passes at claim time and is held at dispatch.
3. `status:blocked` never clears itself after the author fixes the body. #32627 was re-labelled 4 times.
4. `` `EDIT: a` and `b/c` `` silently drops `b/c` from the derived scope, so the worker is later blocked by the scope guard.
5. `claim-task-id.sh` says "globs allowed as extra lines", but the validator rejects globs.
6. The hold comment tells authors to write `` - EDIT: `path` ``, but `brief_scope.py` `existing_scope()` accepts only bare `` - `path` `` lines, so following the gate's own instruction produces a body the normalizer rejects.

## Reference pattern

Model the new module on `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh` (a focused library sourced by `pulse-dispatch-core.sh`) and the unblock guard in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` `_refresh_try_unblock_issue`.

## How

- `brief_scope.py`: strip `:N` / `:N-M` line-range suffixes from declarations, and keep `and`/`,`-joined bare path continuations (paths containing `/`) instead of dropping them.
- New `pulse-dispatch-brief-scope.sh`, sourced by the dispatch core:
  - Before holding, try `brief-readiness-helper.sh scope-normalize`. If that succeeds, rewrite the trusted issue body once per body hash; otherwise hold.
  - Sweep: for `status:blocked` issues whose latest block marker is a `missing_files_scope` brief hold, and whose current body now passes (or normalizes to) a canonical scope, restore `status:available`.
- Call the sweep from `pulse-wrapper.sh` after the blocked-status refresh.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/brief_scope.py`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-brief-scope.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-dispatch-validator.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-readiness.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-budget-priority.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/brief.md`

## Acceptance

- `brief-readiness-helper.sh scope-normalize` succeeds for the #32672/#32661 style `` `EDIT: path:12-34` `` bodies.
- Normalizable held issues are unblocked by the pulse without a human removing the label.
- Existing `test-pre-dispatch-validator.sh` passes; ShellCheck clean.
- Ambiguous briefs (approval markers, exclusions, conflicting scope headings) still fail closed.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-dispatch-validator.sh`; `shellcheck` on the changed scripts; replay the 7 held bodies through `scope-normalize`.

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

title: fix(opencode-v2): restore exact V2 sessions in restored Tabby tabs
body:
## Problem

OpenCode V2 (`opencode2`) running in a Tabby tab does not restore its exact session when Tabby restores the tab. V1 profiles (`aidevops opencode --tabby-shell`) get exact restoration: the server plugin writes a private recovery marker and reports it to Tabby with `OSC 1337 CurrentDir`, and the launcher resumes `opencode --session <id>`.

V2 misses both halves of this:

- V2 server plugins run inside the tty-less `opencode serve --service` process, so the V1 marker/OSC writer (`session-recovery-marker.mjs` `createSessionRecoveryMarkerHandler`) never reaches the terminal, and the V2 shim unsets `AIDEVOPS_TABBY_SESSION_RECOVERY` anyway.
- The V2 shim (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh` `_setup_append_opencode_v2_session_guard`) only `cd`s out of a marker directory; it never resumes the session.

Also, `processStartToken()` reads `/proc`, so owner liveness is always false on macOS. That means GH#32482's split-tab guard (do not resume a session still live in another pane) cannot fire on macOS.

## Fix

1. V2 TUI plugin (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-plugin/tui.mjs`): when running inside Tabby, write a V2 recovery marker for the routed root session and emit `OSC 1337 CurrentDir=<marker>` from the TUI process, which owns the tty.
2. `session-recovery-marker.mjs`: add a V2 marker (`schema_version: 2`, `runtime: "v2"`) and validate it against the V2 data home and the `session_v2` table. Reject cross-runtime markers (fail closed). Add a portable `ps -o lstart=` liveness fallback.
3. V2 shim: on a valid, non-live V2 marker, resume with `--session <id>` from the session directory. On a live owner or a V1 marker, keep the current `cd`-only behaviour. After a normal TUI exit in Tabby, report the project directory back to Tabby.
4. Docs: `.agents/reference/tabby-profiles.md`.

### Files Scope
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-recovery-marker.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-plugin/tui.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/tabby-profiles.md`

## Verification

- `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-recovery-marker.mjs`, `node .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-tui-title.mjs`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh`
- Runtime: `opencode2` in a Tabby tab writes a marker under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/opencode-tabby-recovery/<ses>`; resolving from that directory with the V2 data dir yields the session; launching `opencode2` from that directory resumes it.

title: fix(opencode-v2): gh loses auth inside V2 sessions because shim overrides XDG_CONFIG_HOME
body:
## Problem

Inside OpenCode V2 sessions, `gh` reports `You are not logged into any GitHub hosts`. The V2 shim exports `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=~/.aidevops/runtimes/opencode-v2/config` to isolate OpenCode, and `gh` resolves its config from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gh`. So every tool call that runs `gh` loses the user's auth.

Evidence (V2 session, macOS):

- `gh auth status` → not logged in
- `GH_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.config/gh gh auth status` → logged in (keyring)

Other XDG-aware CLIs (git, glab, etc.) may be affected the same way.

## Fix direction

In the V2 shim (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`, `_setup_write_opencode_v2_shim`), capture the caller's original config home before overriding, and export `GH_CONFIG_DIR="${GH_CONFIG_DIR:-${original_xdg_config_home:-$HOME/.config}/gh}"`. Alternatively, have the V2 service/tool environment restore the original `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` for child tool processes while keeping OpenCode's own config isolated. Check the `opencode serve --service` env as well, since tool shells inherit from the service.

### Files Scope
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh`

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh`
- Inside a fresh V2 session: `gh auth status` reports logged in without manual `GH_CONFIG_DIR`.

title: Workers: treat OpenCode runtime lockfile drift in .opencode/ as runtime-owned
body:
## Problem

Headless workers stop as blocked when a managed repository tracks `.opencode/package-lock.json` (or `.opencode/bun.lock`) and the runner's OpenCode version differs from the committed one.

- OpenCode regenerates these files in every checkout where it starts, and writes its own `.opencode/.gitignore` that lists them. A tracked file bypasses that ignore rule.
- The worktree then carries a modification the worker did not make. The only change is the `@opencode-ai/plugin` and `@opencode-ai/sdk` versions and integrity hashes, for example 1.18.31 -> 1.18.32.
- Workers follow "do not revert others' changes", so they refuse to restore or stash the file. `git rebase` then fails with "You have unstaged changes", and the attempt ends with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=target_code_blocker` and no push.

Observed 2026-09-28 in a managed repo: one worker lost a 32-minute attempt (artifacts built, nothing pushed) to exactly this. The repo-side fix is to untrack the file, but every other managed repo that tracks it will hit the same stop.

## Proposed change

1. **Worker guidance.** In `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`, near the fresh-worktree dependency step (GH#32633), add one rule. Changes to `.opencode/package-lock.json` or `.opencode/bun.lock` whose diff touches only `@opencode-ai/*` versions and integrity hashes are runtime-owned: restore them with `git checkout -- <file>` before rebasing, never commit them, and do not treat them as another session's work.
2. **Worktree preparation (optional).** Where headless worktrees are prepared, if either file is tracked, run `git update-index --skip-worktree` on it after creation so runtime rewrites never show as dirty. The exact file is unknown: start from `headless-runtime-helper.sh` and `tests/test-headless-runtime-worktree-tests.sh`.
3. **Repo health (optional).** Where `aidevops init` or repo health checks inspect a repository, warn when these runtime-generated files are tracked, and suggest `git rm --cached` plus a root `.gitignore` entry.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-worktree-tests.sh`

## Verification

- A shellcheck-clean test that creates a repo with a tracked `.opencode/package-lock.json`, then simulates an `@opencode-ai/plugin` version rewrite. The worktree-prep path leaves `git status --short` clean, or the guidance-driven restore lets `git rebase origin/<base>` succeed.
- The existing `tests/test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh` private-workload checks still pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- A worker in a repo that tracks the OpenCode lockfile no longer stops on runtime lockfile drift.
- Real changes to other tracked files are still never auto-restored.

title: Merge helper admin fallback bypasses required checks that have not started
body:
## Problem

`full-loop-helper.sh merge` can admin-merge a PR whose required status checks have not run yet. Two behaviours combine:

1. **Wait passes on missing contexts.** `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh` classifies "no required checks reported" as terminal success (`PASS: verified no required checks …`, around line 323; the classification is near lines 280-305). Just after a PR is created or marked ready, its required contexts often do not exist yet. They are created only once a scope-detection job finishes, so the helper sees zero and passes.
2. **The fallback overrides status checks.** In `full-loop-helper-merge.sh` (around lines 1476-1494), when neither `--admin` nor `--auto` was passed, output matching `base branch policy prohibits|Required status checks? (is|are) expected|At least [0-9]+ approving review` triggers a retry with `--admin`. The first two patterns are exactly how GitHub reports pending required checks, so the fallback bypasses them.

The framework rule is that admin merge is allowed only when branch policy blocks self-review or review count **after gates pass**. This path admin-merges before the gates have started.

Observed 2026-09-28 in a managed repo:

1. The PR was marked ready, and `wait-checks` ran 4 s later: `CI wait started: none=0` then `PASS: verified no required checks`, with `no required checks are configured`.
2. The merge attempt returned `the base branch policy prohibits the merge`, and the log shows `Branch protection blocked plain merge; retrying with --admin` then `merged with --admin fallback`.
3. At merge time, the repo's required Format/Lint/Typecheck/Unit contexts had never started; its scope-detection job was still pending.
4. Minutes earlier, another PR in the same repo listed those 4 required contexts through `gh pr checks --required`.

The change merged was low-risk, but the same path would merge an untested code change.

## Proposed change

1. **`gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`:** before returning `no-required`, read the base branch's required contexts from branch protection (`repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{base}/protection/required_status_checks`) and from rulesets (`repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{base}`, `required_status_checks` rules).
   - If any are configured but missing from the PR's head SHA, classify as `pending` until they report, bounded by the existing timeout.
   - Only return `no-required` when the protection and rulesets queries succeed and list none.
   - If those queries fail, fall back to a minimum settle window (for example 90 s after the head commit or ready event) before accepting an empty required set.
2. **`full-loop-helper-merge.sh`:** stop treating `Required status checks … expected`, or a bare `base branch policy prohibits`, as permission for `--admin`.
   - Before any admin fallback, re-verify on the head SHA that every required context from step 1 is `SUCCESS` (or intentionally skipped).
   - Only then allow `--admin`, and only for the review-count/self-review block.
   - Otherwise return non-zero with `LIFECYCLE_STATE=CHECKS_PENDING`, so callers wait and retry.
3. **Tests:** extend `tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh` and `tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh` with the cases below.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`
- ShellCheck is clean on the changed scripts.

## Acceptance criteria

- Required contexts configured on the base branch but not yet reported are `pending`, not success.
- A `base branch policy prohibits` merge failure with required checks pending returns non-zero; no admin retry happens.
- The admin fallback still merges when all required checks pass and only the review count blocks.
- Repos with genuinely no required checks still merge without waiting for the full timeout.

title: fix(gh-wrappers): gh_create_issue fails on bash 3.2 with empty-array unbound variable
body:
## Problem

`gh_create_issue` aborts under macOS system bash 3.2 when `nounset` is active and no TODO-derived labels exist:

```
shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh: line 510: _GH_CI_TODO_LABEL_ARGS[@]: unbound variable
```

Bash 3.2 treats `"${arr[@]}"` of an empty array as unbound under `set -u`. Bash 4.4+ does not, so the same call succeeds with `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash`. This was observed while filing GH#32700/#32701 from an interactive session. `bash -c 'source shared-constants.sh; source shared-gh-wrappers.sh; gh_create_issue ...'` failed under `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 and succeeded under Homebrew bash.

Minimal repro: `/bin/bash -uc 'a=(); f(){ return 0; }; f x "${a[@]}"'` → `a[@]: unbound variable`.

## Fix

In `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`, guard every expansion of an array that can be empty using the Bash 3.2-safe form `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}`, or check the length first, as line 593 already does. Guidance: `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md`.

Known sites:

- Line 510: `_GH_CI_TODO_LABEL_ARGS` (confirmed failing)
- Audit these too, since each can be empty depending on caller args:
  - lines 368, 375, 376, 380 (`_GH_CI_TRUST_NORMALIZED_ARGS`)
  - line 514 (`_GH_CI_CONTRACT_ARGS`)
  - line 515 (`_GH_WRAPPER_SIG_MODIFIED_ARGS`)
  - line 567 (`_GH_WRAPPER_BODY_FILE_ARGS`)
  - line 588 (`_GH_CI_FILTERED_ARGS`)

Apply the same audit to the sibling wrappers sourced by `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` if they use the same pattern.

### Files Scope
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`

## Verification

- `/bin/bash -uc 'source .agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh; source .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh; type gh_create_issue'` loads cleanly.
- Run the existing `gh_create_issue` tests under `/bin/bash` 3.2 (`rg -l gh_create_issue .agents/scripts/tests`), with an issue body that has no TODO-derived labels. There must be no `unbound variable`.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh` passes clean.

title: fix(release): release helper collides on its control worktree after bash-4 re-exec
body:
## Problem

`aidevops release status|reconcile|patch ...` fails with `Cannot prepare a linked release control worktree.` whenever `bash` on `PATH` is macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2. This happens, for example, in OpenCode V2 sessions whose `PATH` has no `/opt/homebrew/bin`. Each failure also leaks one full checkout at `<worktree-base>/aidevops-release-control-<pid>`.

Evidence (macOS, 2026-09-28):

```
Preparing worktree (detached HEAD 9c5ad0568)
Preparing worktree (detached HEAD 9c5ad0568)
fatal: '<worktree-base>/aidevops-release-control-16613' already exists
Cannot prepare a linked release control worktree.
```

The failure reproduced on every run. With `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH`, the same command succeeds.

## Root cause

1. `aidevops.sh` `_dispatch_helper` runs `bash "$hp" "$@"`, so the helper starts under bash 3.2.
2. `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh:107` runs `_full_loop_release_prepare_control_worktree` at top level. That creates `aidevops-release-control-$$` and sets an EXIT trap.
3. `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh:123` then sources `full-loop-helper-state.sh`, which sources `shared-constants.sh`. `shared-constants.sh:47-76` re-execs the top-level script under bash 4+ with `exec`.
4. `exec` keeps the PID and skips the EXIT trap. The re-executed script repeats step 2 with the same `$$`, and `git worktree add` fails on the existing path. The first worktree leaks, and the GH#32548 reaper skips it for 30 minutes.

## Fix

In `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh`, get onto bash 4+ before any side effect. Do one of:

- source `shared-constants.sh` (or perform the same bash-4 re-exec guard) before `_full_loop_release_prepare_control_worktree` runs; or
- move the control-worktree preparation after all `source` lines.

Either way, the re-exec must happen before the worktree exists. Check other helpers that create PID-named state before sourcing `shared-constants.sh`: `rg -n '\$\$' .agents/scripts/*.sh`, then compare the line order against their `source` lines.

### Files Scope
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-helper.sh`

## Verification

- `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:$PATH /bin/bash .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh status <merged-pr>` prints lane status. It must not print "Preparing worktree" twice.
- After the run, `git worktree list | rg release-control` shows no leaked entries.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-helper.sh` passes.
- `shellcheck` passes clean.

title: test: test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh silently fails since a hardcoded rate-limit reset epoch expired
body:
## What

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh` has been failing silently since about 2026-09-21. Its `gh` stub (line 42) returns a hardcoded `x-ratelimit-reset: 1789999999`, and that epoch is now in the past. `_cb_rest_core_observation` treats an expired reset as an unknown observation, so the REST-core progress gate blocks `_dispatch_compute_capacity`. The first test (`test_capacity_raises_soft_cap_to_floor`) returns 1 and the script exits non-zero **with no output**, so none of its assertions run.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh && echo PASS || echo FAIL`

**Actual output**: `FAIL`, with no PASS/FAIL lines. Under `bash -x`, the trace shows `[[ 1789999999 -le 1790559731 ]]` → `return 2` → `REST-core progress unit blocked: context=dispatch_capacity mode=unknown` → `Dispatch_max skipped: REST-core launch headroom is unavailable`.

**Expected**: all capacity and floor tests run and report PASS.

## How

- Make the stub's reset epoch relative, for example `$(( $(date +%s) + 3600 ))`, instead of a fixed timestamp.
- Make an unexpected non-zero return from a test function report a named FAIL instead of exiting silently under `set -e`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh`

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh` prints PASS lines for every test and exits 0.
- A failing test prints a named FAIL line instead of exiting silently.

title: t18505: perf(dispatch): run read-only dedup layers before costly scope gates
body:
## What

Reorder the per-candidate dispatch gates in `_dispatch_dedup_check_layers` so the read-only dedup layers (`check_dispatch_dedup`: ledger, process, title, PR evidence, dispatch comment, assignment/stale recovery, terminal-blocker circuit) run **before** the costly scope gates (issue consolidation, large-file simplification, file-footprint overlap). Cheap label/state/NMR/blocked-by gates keep their current position; the external-author gate stays last.

## Why (evidence: last 24h on one runner, `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv`)

- 1,057 dedup checks, p50 44s, 856 min total; only ~157 candidates reached worker launch.
- `dedup.consolidation` p50 16.5s (331 min/day), `large_file` 48 min, `footprint` 71 min — these ran for ~1,045 candidates.
- `dedup.7_layers` then rejected ~650 of 852 candidates (active peer claims, terminal-blocker circuit), so most costly-gate time was spent on candidates the next layer rejects.
- Expected saving: roughly 5h/day of candidate-evaluation wall time per runner, shortening dispatch rounds (median gap ~15 min) so free worker slots refill sooner.
- Side benefit: consolidation/large-file gates have side effects (consolidation dispatch, simplification task creation); they no longer fire for issues another runner currently owns.

No gate is removed or weakened. `check_dispatch_dedup` is read-only apart from its existing stale-assignment recovery, and the `DISPATCH_CLAIM` lock still happens later in the launch path.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-external-author-gate.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on changed files.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-external-author-gate.sh` (extended: an active claim must not invoke consolidation).
- Existing dispatch tests: `test-dispatch-dedup-gh-call-budget.sh`, `test-pulse-dispatch-core-t3040-gate-removed.sh`, `test-pre-dispatch-validator.sh`.
- After release + update: in `dispatch-stages.tsv`, `dedup.consolidation` sample count falls toward the post-dedup candidate count and `dedup.dedup_check` p50 drops.

title: t18506: Persistent dashboard issues: accuracy, privacy and public meaningfulness
body:
## What

Make the repository persistent dashboard issues (`[Supervisor:<login>]`, `[Contributor:<login>]` health dashboards and the `Code Audit Routines` quality dashboard) accurate, privacy-minimal and meaningful for collaborators and public readers, and keep them cheap to maintain.

## Why

Audit of the live persistent issues on this repository (2026-09-28) found:

- **Broken quality dashboard title/body.** `_gather_quality_issue_stats` emits newline-delimited fields, but the bot-coverage section is multi-line. The reader shifts: `Badge status` renders empty, `Bot Review Coverage` renders only its heading, and the title becomes `Code Audit Routines — Open: 1 | Closed: 2039 | Simplified: | Metric | Count |`.
- **Dashboard treated as work.** The quality dashboard carried `auto-dispatch`, `status:available` and `tier:standard`. It received about 85 NMR decision packets, several dispatch claims and a `missing_files_scope` terminal blocker. It now has more than 200 comments, most of them superseded automation output. Health dashboards already normalize lifecycle labels; the quality dashboard does not.
- **Operator telemetry published on public repos.** Zero-worker diagnostics dump raw JSONL/TSV: session, worker, run and attempt IDs, PIDs, model and provider. They also publish provider credential posture (`OpenAI: oauth; Anthropic: missing; auth file: present`) and host fingerprinting (core count, free memory, process count). The memory row is mislabelled (`low (83785MB free)` means low pressure). The body also lists identity aliases, which can include local OS account names.
- **Identity split under local usernames.** When `gh api user` fails, the dashboard falls back to `whoami`. That fallback created `[Contributor:vladimir]`, `[Contributor:alexey]` and `[Contributor:vod]` with the wrong role. They then stayed open for weeks after their last refresh.
- **Placeholder noise.** Sections with no data still render as `_… unavailable._` or `—` rows every cycle.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep-issues.sh` — NUL-delimited stats transport; meaningful title; quality dashboard label normalization; minimize superseded automation comments.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep.sh` — call label normalization and comment hygiene from the dashboard update path.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard-data.sh` — privacy-minimal diagnostics summary, coarse resource pressure, omit empty sections, no alias list in public body.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard.sh` — refuse to publish under an unverified local fallback identity; archive stale dashboards of inactive operators (supervisor role only).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard-issue.sh` — also strip `tier:*` from dashboards; stale-dashboard archival helper.
- EDIT: existing focused tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` covering these renderers.
- NEW: `.agents/reference/persistent-dashboards.md` — contract: purpose, audience, content and privacy rules, lifecycle.

### Verification

- `shellcheck` on changed scripts.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stats-quality-sweep-issues.sh`, `test-stats-worker-zero-diagnostics.sh`, `test-health-dashboard-identity-aliases.sh`, `test-stats-functions-characterization.sh`, `test-health-dashboard-sentinel-abstain.sh`.
- Render both dashboard bodies locally and confirm there are no raw telemetry IDs, no auth posture, no alias list, and a correct quality title and badge row.

title: t18508: Quality sweep: publish partial results when a large repo exceeds the per-repo budget
body:
## What

Make the daily quality sweep finish and publish its dashboard for large repositories, starting with `marcusquinn/aidevops`, within the per-repository budget. If a heavy tool cannot finish in time, publish partial results and say which tools were skipped, instead of publishing nothing.

## Why

- On the supervisor host, `~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log` shows `Quality sweep attempt deferred/failed for marcusquinn/aidevops (rc=124); advancing cursor` on every daily attempt, including lines 86745–92576. The `Code Audit Routines` dashboard (#24670) was last updated on `2026-09-05T19:42:31Z`, so the pinned public quality snapshot is more than three weeks stale.
- `_quality_sweep_batch` in `.agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep.sh` bounds each repository with `QUALITY_SWEEP_REPO_TIMEOUT` (default 120s). `_quality_sweep_for_repo` runs every tool (`_run_sweep_tools`) before it updates the body or the comment, so one slow tool on a large repository discards all results.
- Found during the persistent-dashboard audit in #32730 / PR #32735.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep-tools.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stats-wrapper-timeout.sh`

### File Notes

- `stats-quality-sweep.sh`: `_quality_sweep_batch`, `_quality_sweep_for_repo`, `_run_sweep_tools`.
- `stats-quality-sweep-tools.sh`: per-tool bounding where a single tool dominates.
- `test-stats-wrapper-timeout.sh`: existing bounded-sweep fixtures, if behaviour changes.

### Implementation Steps

1. Profile the per-tool wall time for `marcusquinn/aidevops` (ShellCheck sample, Qlty SARIF, SonarCloud, Codacy, CodeRabbit, review scan) to find the dominant tool. Log the timings to `stats.log`.
2. Bound each tool with its own share of the repository budget, and render the tools that completed. The dashboard's `Tools run` count and the rolling comment must name the skipped tools rather than imply full coverage.
3. Keep the resumable cursor semantics (`GH#31356`) unchanged. Never mark the daily run complete when no repository published.

### Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-stats-wrapper-timeout.sh` passes.
- Run the sweep for the framework repository on a maintainer host, e.g. force it by removing `~/.aidevops/logs/quality-sweep-last-run` and running `stats-wrapper.sh`. `stats.log` should show `Quality sweep: updated dashboard on #24670 in marcusquinn/aidevops`, and #24670's `Last sweep` timestamp should advance.

title: t18510: fix(setup): V1 plugin pass must not write OpenCode V2 live config from ambient V2 env
body:
## What

An OpenCode V2 session failed mid-session with `AI.Error.Authentication: API key is invalid.` (preceded by `Agent not found: "Build+"`). Root cause: the live V2 config `~/.aidevops/runtimes/opencode-v2/config/opencode/opencode.json` was overwritten with a V1-style `plugin` entry pointing into a deleted `mktemp` sandbox (`.../aidevops-opencode-v2-setup.XXXXXX.*/home/.aidevops/agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`), plus a matching dangling `plugins/opencode-aidevops` symlink. V2 hot-reloaded the config, the aidevops plugin failed to load, so the Build+ agent and the OAuth pool `http.request` hook disappeared and requests went out with the placeholder API key.

## Why

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh` isolates only `HOME`. When it runs inside an `opencode2` session, the V2 shim's exported `OPENCODE_CONFIG`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` still point at the live V2 runtime config. The test's `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v1 setup_opencode_runtime_plugins` call then takes the V1 branch of `setup_opencode_runtime_plugins` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`), which, unlike the V2-selected branch, does not strip V2-owned ambient config. `find_opencode_config` and the V1 plugins dir resolve to the live V2 config.

The production V1 branch has the same latent leak whenever setup runs with the V1 profile under a V2 runtime environment. The V2 repair pass also never removes a V1-style `opencode-aidevops` symlink left in the V2 plugins dir.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`: run the V1 plugin pass with V2-owned ambient `OPENCODE_CONFIG` / `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` / `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` removed. Values under the V2 runtime root or any `*/.aidevops/runtimes/opencode-v2/*` path are dropped; user-chosen V1 locations are preserved. The V2 pass also removes a setup-managed `plugins/opencode-aidevops` symlink from the V2 plugins dir.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh`: unset ambient OpenCode/XDG/V2 env at start, and assert that a V1 pass under simulated V2 ambient env leaves the V2 config untouched.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh` passes when run inside an opencode2 session, and the live V2 config is unchanged afterwards.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the changed files.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh`

title: full-loop commit validators: honour project Node engine and configurable timeout
body:
## Problem

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` runs the project's pre-PR checks with a fixed 300-second time limit per script, using whatever `node` is first on PATH. In a real interactive full-loop on a large pnpm monorepo (a private project; name withheld), this caused two false failures in a row before the PR could be created:

1. **Timeout:** `[validators] TIMEOUT after 300s: pnpm run lint (apps/web)`. Full-workspace ESLint on a large Next.js app needs more than 300 seconds on a cold cache. It passed with `AIDEVOPS_VALIDATOR_TIMEOUT=1500`.
2. **Wrong Node version:** `CHECK FAILED (exit 1): pnpm run test (apps/web)`. Two jsdom tests failed with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getItem')`. The host's default Node was v26, which adds its own experimental `localStorage` global. It warns `localStorage is not available because --localstorage-file was not provided` and hides jsdom's version. The project declares `engines.node: ">=24.0.0 <25.0.0"`, and pnpm printed an `Unsupported engine` warning that the validator ignored. The same tests pass on Node 24, which was installed at `/opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin`. Remote CI (Node 24) passed.

Both cases look like code failures but are environment problems, so the session had to diagnose them manually.

## Proposed fix

File: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`

- In `_run_project_validators` (around line 282) or `_run_scoped_node_checks` (around line 225), resolve the Node version the project requires before running any checks. Read `.nvmrc`, `.node-version`, `.tool-versions` or `package.json` `engines.node` from the repo root or the check's directory.
  - If the active `node` does not satisfy it, look for a matching install (fnm, nvm, volta, mise, or Homebrew `node@<major>`) and put its `bin` first on PATH for the check subshell (the `( cd "$scope" ... )` block around line 257).
  - If there is no match, report `ENVIRONMENT FAILURE: node vX does not satisfy engines ">=24 <25"` with the fix command, not `CHECK FAILED`.
- Timeout: let each repo set its own limit. For example, read `.aidevops.json` / repo config key `validator_timeout_seconds` before falling back to `AIDEVOPS_VALIDATOR_TIMEOUT` and 300.
  - Make the `TIMEOUT` message (line 265) say to set `AIDEVOPS_VALIDATOR_TIMEOUT=<n>` and re-run. Do not suggest skipping the checks.
- Optional: on a test failure, check the saved log for known environment signatures (`--localstorage-file`, `Unsupported engine`) and report it as an environment failure.
- Update `workflows/full-loop.md` or `reference/ci-gate-policy.md` to document the timeout override and how the Node version is chosen.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh` reports no violations.
- In a test repo whose `package.json` has `engines.node: ">=24 <25"`, running with Node 26 first on PATH:
  - either the checks run under Node 24 automatically,
  - or they fail with a clear `ENVIRONMENT FAILURE` message.
- `AIDEVOPS_VALIDATOR_TIMEOUT` and the new repo config key are both honored, and the timeout message names the override.
- If a validator test harness exists under `.agents/scripts/tests/`, extend it there. Do not add a new test runner.

title: Anthropic prompt-cache stability, truthful profile cache stats, compaction re-read guidance
body:
## What

Three related token-efficiency fixes found while measuring real Anthropic OAuth usage in `llm-requests.db`:

1. **Remaining mid-session prompt-cache breaks** after GH#32444.
2. **Profile README cache statistics** ignore cache writes, so Claude models show `100.0%` hit rate and near-zero "Input".
3. **Compaction continuation guidance**: minimise post-compaction re-reads without bloating the summary or weakening continuity.

## Evidence (local read-only analysis, 2026-09-26 → 2026-09-28)

- 42 Opus Build+ primary sessions, 14,506 turns (`llm_requests`, `routing_population=top_level_profile`).
- 96.6% of follow-on turns reuse the full cached prefix, but cache *rewrites* cost ~27% of API-equivalent spend (priced with `configs/model-pricing.json`).
- Post-GH#32444 releases (v3.37.1+): 5,252 turns, 57 sub-5-minute breaks re-wrote ~$67 of cache (~15% of $456); 36 TTL expiries ~$38.
- Breaks cluster across *all* concurrent sessions within seconds of framework deploys (auto-update redeploys and releases). The plugin log shows the redistributed framework prefix `sha` changing mid-session in 30+ sessions.
- Proven volatile input: `buildSessionStartGreetingInstruction()` re-reads `VERSION` on every request, so every release deploy rewrites the greeting line inside the cached framework prefix of every open session (probe: `v3.37.11` → `v3.37.12` changes the block).
- Remaining breaks (tools-level `cache_read=0`, history-level) cannot be attributed from current logs: `provider-auth` logs only one prefix hash.
- Profile README: `claude-opus-5-5` (30d) renders 100.0% hit rate / 27K input; including 118.5M cache-write tokens gives 96.6%. `claude-opus-4-6` renders twice because a dated model ID collapses to the same display name.

## How

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/ttsr.mjs`: pin the resolved greeting block per root session so mid-session deploys do not change the cached prefix.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth-body.mjs` (+ new small helper module): per-session wire fingerprints of tools / system / redistributed prefix / thinking config / message history; log the changed segment (tool names, prefix line delta, first changed message index) when a stable segment changes. No request mutation.
- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-render-lib.sh` / `profile-readme-data-lib.sh`: hit rate = `read / (input + cache_write + read)`; add a Cache write column; merge rows whose names collapse after date-suffix cleanup.
- `.agents/scripts/session_time_db.py`: include the other aidevops-managed OpenCode V1 data homes (`opencode-desktop/*`, `opencode-server/*`) alongside `opencode-interactive/*`.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction.mjs`: concise re-read-avoidance guidance (targeted anchors/snippets for the next edits, retained analysis results, artifact pointers) and a corrected Read-before-Edit rule.
- Claude compaction target stays at its current value (explicit decision).

## Verification

- `node --test` for touched plugin tests (`test-ttsr-system-transform.mjs`, `test-provider-auth-cch.mjs`, compaction tests), plus a direct probe of greeting stability across a `VERSION` change.
- `profile-readme-helper.sh` render against the local DBs; confirm corrected hit rates and single `claude-opus-4-6` row.
- ShellCheck on changed shell files; `linters-local.sh --changed`.
- After deploy: plugin log shows `cache-stability` segment diagnostics on the next prefix/tool change.

title: Orphan-recovery PRs use Resolves and close issues when a killed worker's partial branch merges
body:
## Problem

The orphan-recovery path opens a PR from a worker's partial branch with `Resolves #N`, even when the worker was killed before finishing. When the deterministic merge pass merges that PR, the issue closes as done, labelled `status:done` and `solved:worker`, although its acceptance criteria are unmet.

Observed on 2026-09-28 in a managed project repo:

1. A `tier:standard` worker on a large multi-file implementation issue ended `watchdog_stall_killed` after 43 minutes.
2. Its pushed branch held one WIP commit (2 changed lines in one planning brief). The issue's required new source file was never created.
3. The orphan-recovery path opened `auto-recover: orphaned worker branch for #N` with `Resolves #N`.
4. The pulse deterministic merge pass merged it about 20 minutes later, which closed the issue. A maintainer found the false completion only by reviewing post-merge and had to reopen and re-label by hand.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`, `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` (deployed copy around lines 604-609):

```bash
if [[ -n "$issue_number" ]]; then
    pr_title="auto-recover: orphaned worker branch for #${issue_number}"
    closing_line="Resolves #${issue_number}"
fi
```

A recovery PR is by definition built from a worker that exited before declaring completion. Its branch is evidence of progress, not of completion, but the closing keyword turns the merge into a completion claim.

## Proposed fix

- Use `For #${issue_number}` in orphan-recovery PR bodies, for both `worker_branch_orphan` and `worker_local_branch_unpushed`, so merging preserves the work without closing the issue.
- After such a merge, the issue should return to `status:available` for redispatch, not `status:done`. Reuse the existing post-merge path for non-closing PRs; do not add a new one.
- Optional: when the release reason is `watchdog_stall_killed` or similar, have the recovery PR body say that the worker was killed mid-task and list the issue's scoped files that the branch does not touch.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`: `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` (`closing_line`) and `_build_orphan_recovery_pr_body`.
- Tests: the existing orphan-recovery tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`. Find them with `rg -l "orphan-recovery|_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr" .agents/scripts/tests`; if none cover the closing line, add a focused case.
- Docs: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` (orphan-recovery sections), if it describes the closing keyword.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-orphan-recovery-pr-base.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`

## Verification

- A unit or shell test asserts that the recovery PR body contains `For #N` and not `Resolves #N`, `Closes #N` or `Fixes #N`.
- ShellCheck is clean on the changed script.

title: t18514: feat(pulse): runner-local AI owner for terminal-blocker circuits
body:
## What

Give terminal-blocker circuits a durable AI owner on the runner that produced them. Today a repeated known blocker opens `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_CIRCUIT` and the issue stays `status:available` with no owner acting on it; the only AI intake (`integration-recovery-helper.sh pending`) sees just the rare `INTEGRATION_RECOVERY_REQUEST`, and the LLM supervisor that reads it runs roughly daily.

1. New `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` (runner-local queue, no authority):
   - `enqueue` — called by the worker release path when this runner opens a circuit.
   - `seed` — backfills open circuits this runner authored (GitHub search on the circuit marker), at most every 6h.
   - `pending` — re-verifies each entry against live GitHub (open issue, circuit still active via `terminal_blocker_circuit_active`), retires resolved entries, suppresses entries with a recent decision, and prints compact JSON with local failure-excerpt paths.
   - `record` — stores the owner's decision (`wake`, `next_action`, `evidence`) with the authenticated actor.
2. `headless-runtime-failure.sh`: enqueue on circuit open.
3. Supervisor prompt (`pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`): act as AI brief owner for pending entries per `reference/worker-discipline.md`.
4. `_should_run_llm_supervisor`: run the supervisor when recovery entries are pending and the last recovery run is older than `PULSE_LLM_RECOVERY_INTERVAL` (default 3h).
5. `reference/worker-discipline.md`: short "Terminal-blocker recovery" owner contract.

No gate is weakened: the circuit, retry directive and permission boundaries are unchanged; the owner never grants permissions and only revises briefs under existing brief-author authority.

## Why (evidence, 2026-09-28)

- 17 issues across aidevops, a private app repo and aidevops.sh were circuit-held; 8 had already closed, the rest waited with no owner.
- Root causes observed in local excerpts were mostly not brief defects: missing pinned Node runtime (Node 26 vs `engines` 24), validator timeouts, a missing push path, and the secret-read guard blocking its own fix (#32526/#32614).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`

title: consolidated: Run automated OpenCode harnesses as headless
body:
_Supersedes #32620 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

Ensure automated `opencode run` invocations in the agent-test CLI path and contest harness set `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1`. The plugin then skips interactive greeting, advisories, and subagent A/B assignment and records `llm_requests.routing_population = "headless"`.

## Why

`isHeadless()` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/proxy-lifecycle.mjs:52-58` recognizes only `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS`, `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS`, `OPENCODE_HEADLESS`, and `GITHUB_ACTIONS`; `opencode run` supplies none. Agent-test and contest automation therefore has interactive context, can contaminate comparison outputs with a greeting, and is classified as interactive by `observability-routing.mjs:12`; `subagent-ab.mjs:13` only skips headless runs. The missing marker is confirmed; its downstream effects remain unconfirmed pending a live harness capture.

## Reproducer

```bash
rg -n "AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS|opencode run" .agents/scripts/agent-test-helper.sh .agents/scripts/contest-helper.sh .agents/scripts/ai-research-helper.sh
```

At main `f9ac65147`, `ai-research-helper.sh:352,357` already prefixes its `opencode run` calls with `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1`, whereas `contest-helper.sh:90` and `agent-test-helper.sh:311` do not. This verifies the missing marker; it does not itself reproduce the downstream runtime symptom.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/agent-test-helper.sh:311` (`run_prompt_opencode_cli`), replace `local cmd=(opencode run --format json)` with the two-line automated-harness comment and `local cmd=(env AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1 opencode run --format json)`.
2. In `.agents/scripts/contest-helper.sh:90`, replace `timeout_sec 120 opencode run --format json` with `timeout_sec 120 env AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1 opencode run --format json`.
3. Do not change `run_prompt_opencode_server` at `.agents/scripts/agent-test-helper.sh:232`: its existing server environment determines headless mode.
4. Follow the existing `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1` conventions in `.agents/scripts/ai-research-helper.sh:352,357` and `.agents/scripts/opencode-pin-canary.sh:291`; `remote-dispatch-helper.sh:496` uses equivalent `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS=true`.

`env` is POSIX and retains PATH lookup, including mocks. This is per-process only: no migration, persisted state, concurrency, retry, or idempotency change. Older plugins harmlessly ignore it except for existing checks. `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/`; no generated mirror exists. Revert the two files to roll back.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both helpers invoke `env AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1 opencode run --format json`.
- [ ] No bare `cmd=(opencode run` or `timeout_sec 120 opencode run` remains in either helper.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-test-command-dispatch.sh` passes.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-test-helper-output-channel.sh` passes.
- [ ] `bash tests/test-contest-helper.sh` passes.
- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/agent-test-helper.sh .agents/scripts/contest-helper.sh` passes.

## Context & Decisions

- Per @marcusquinn, reproduce with `rg -n "AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS|opencode run" .agents/scripts/agent-test-helper.sh .agents/scripts/contest-helper.sh .agents/scripts/ai-research-helper.sh`; at main `f9ac65147` only the two target calls lack the marker.
- Per @marcusquinn, do not claim the downstream effect was live-reproduced.
- Per @alex-solovyev, retain `tier:standard`: the prior brief was normalized from simple because its execution contract was not in the expected machine-recognized shape.
- Scope is deliberately limited to the two child commands; the server path is excluded. This is a leaf issue and its PR closes it.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/agent-test-helper.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/contest-helper.sh

## Contributors

cc @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash

  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \

```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` is also mandatory. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.


## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #32582** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @vladimirdulov

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

Worker outcome readers must ignore metric rows timestamped in the future. Existing future-dated rows should also be quarantined, not counted.

## Why

The first two lines of the production `~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` are test-fixture rows with `"ts":4102444800` (2100-01-01). They have no `session_key`, `issue_number` or `repo_slug`, and `result=success`. Every rolling window (`worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 1h|24h|7d`, pulse capacity and success-rate readers) includes them, so each window reports 2 successes that never happened. Retention by age also keeps them forever. The same sentinel value is used intentionally in test fixtures, for example `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-activity-helper.sh:145` (`T_FUTURE_SENTINEL`). At some point a test run wrote to the real metrics path instead of its fixture override.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**

```bash
rg -n '"ts":4102444800' ~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl
```

**Actual output**

```text
1:{"ts":4102444800,"role":"worker","model":"openai/gpt-5.4","result":"success","activity":true,"duration_ms":45000,"exit_code":0}
2:{"ts":4102444800,"role":"worker","model":"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6","result":"success","activity":true,"duration_ms":240000,"exit_code":0}
```

## How

- Reader guard: in the window filters of `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh` and the pulse capacity/diagnose readers that consume this ledger, exclude rows where `ts > now + 300`. Report them as a count of `future_dated_ignored`.
- Producer: find which test writes to the default ledger path without the metrics-path override, and make it use a temporary path. Where it can't be found, record the search you did. Candidates are tests that emit `openai/gpt-5.4` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` success rows without a session key.
- Do not hand-edit the live ledger. The reader guard makes the existing rows harmless.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-activity-helper.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Rows with `ts` more than 5 minutes in the future do not count in any rolling window or success rate, and the summary reports how many were ignored.
- Current-time and past rows are counted exactly as before. The existing `T_FUTURE_SENTINEL` fixture behaviour stays deliberate and tested.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-activity-helper.sh`
- `worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 1h` on the live ledger no longer includes the two 2100-dated successes.

title: GH#32744 follow-up: cache-stability monitor family keys and block-level history attribution
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

Make the Anthropic cache-stability monitor from GH#32744 (PR #32747) separate request families and localize history mutations to the content block, so the plugin log shows which component rewrites earlier conversation bytes. Do not fix the mutator in this task; this task produces trustworthy attribution.

## Why

The monitor went live with v3.37.15. Its first 15 log lines in `~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-plugin.log` show two problems.

1. **False positives.** Title generation (`You are a title generator…`) and compaction summaries (`You are a context summarization agent…`) share the session ID with the main agent. Each switch between request families logs `segment=tools added=[…]`, `segment=thinking` and `segment=prefix` even though the requests are simply different kinds, not the same prefix changing. Example: `session=ses_f1834fc52ffegVt8ipl4KrnwOV` at 2026-09-28T11:34:00Z.
2. **History breaks can't be diagnosed.** `session=ses_f1a25864effenFG6THGD1DySzw` logged `segment=history index=66/69 role=user`, `79/83 role=assistant`, `87/91`, `95/97` within 90 seconds. Each earlier message changed bytes, forcing a full cache re-write (llm_requests shows warm-cache rewrites of 370K–400K tokens). The line names the message but not what changed: tool_result pruning, stripped thinking blocks, text rewrites, or injected/removed synthetic parts.

Baseline from `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/llm-requests.db` (Anthropic, since 2026-09-26): about 0.5–1.4% of requests on 3.37.x are warm breaks (previous request under 5 minutes earlier, `tokens_cache_read = 0`, `tokens_cache_write >= 10000`). v3.37.15: 62 requests, 0 warm breaks so far, which is too small a sample to judge.

## Tier

`tier:standard`: one plugin module, its focused test and one doc section. The design choices below are specified, but block-level diffing needs judgement.

## How (Approach)

### Worker Quick-Start

- Monitor: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/cache-stability.mjs`
  - `fingerprintRequest` (lines 50–62) hashes each message whole (`messages: messages.map((message) => hash(message))`).
  - `diffHistory` (lines 86–98) reports only the first changed message index.
  - `createCacheStabilityMonitor().observe` (lines 129–135) keys state by `sessionID` alone.
- Caller: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth-body.mjs:220` calls `(context.cacheMonitor ?? cacheStability).observe(parsed, context)`. Context comes from `provider-auth.mjs:302` (`{ sessionID, account: currentEmail }`) and `v2-provider-auth.mjs:45` (`{ sessionID }`).
- Tests: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-cache-stability.mjs`. Its `body()` helper builds Anthropic-shaped bodies; `observe` is created with an injected `log`.
- Docs: `.agents/reference/context-efficiency.md` lines ~72–76 describe the log line format.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/cache-stability.mjs`
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-cache-stability.mjs`
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/context-efficiency.md`

### Implementation Steps

1. **Family key.** Key monitor state by `sessionID` plus a request-family key:
   - `parsed.model`
   - whether `parsed.tools` is non-empty (`agent` vs `aux`)
   
   Auxiliary no-tool requests (title, summary) must never be compared with tool-bearing agent requests. A tool-set change *within* agent requests must still be reported. Keep the `maxSessions` LRU bound, now applied to family keys, and include `family=<agent|aux>` in each log line.
2. **Block-level history fingerprint.** Store per-message block hashes (`content` array items; wrap string content as one text block) along with block `type`s and text/JSON lengths. Keep excluding `cache_control`.
3. **Block-level history diff.** On the first changed message, report:
   - `block=<i>/<n>` and `type=<text|tool_use|tool_result|thinking|redacted_thinking|…>`
   - `change=<modified|added|removed>`
   - `chars=<before>-><after>`
   
   A `tool_result` whose new text starts with a short placeholder is a pruning candidate; log `now=` with at most 80 chars via the existing `snippet()`, and never log more than that of user content. If more than one message changed, add `messages_changed=<count>`.
4. **Tests.** Extend `test-cache-stability.mjs`:
   - alternating aux/agent requests in one session produce no lines
   - a tool added between two agent requests is still reported
   - a pruned `tool_result` in an earlier user message reports `type=tool_result change=modified` with char counts
   - a thinking block removed from an earlier assistant message reports `type=thinking change=removed`
5. **Docs.** Update the log-format lines in `context-efficiency.md`. Add the warm-break SQL under "Acceptance Criteria" below as the evaluation query.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `provider-auth-body.mjs:220` is the only caller of `observe` (verified with `rg -n "cacheMonitor|cacheStability" .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`). The returned change descriptors are read only by `tests/test-cache-stability.mjs`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the monitor only writes log lines through its injected `log` (default `console.error`, captured in `~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-plugin.log`) and its in-memory `sessions` Map. It never writes the request body.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `tests/test-cache-stability.mjs` (3 cases) and `tests/test-provider-auth-cch.mjs` (caller transform); production evidence is `rg 'cache-stability' ~/.aidevops/logs/opencode-plugin.log`.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A. There is no persisted schema; the only config is the unchanged `AIDEVOPS_CACHE_STABILITY_LOG=0` env opt-out read in `createCacheStabilityMonitor`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** the deployed copy is `~/.aidevops/agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/cache-stability.mjs` via `setup.sh`. The module has no generated output.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none required. `cache-stability.mjs` imports only `node:crypto` and persists nothing (verified: no fs/sqlite imports), so the new fingerprint shape takes effect on the first request after plugin load, with no ordering or backfill.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR; the LRU (`maxSessions`) bounds memory and there are no files to clean up.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Node runs `observe` synchronously per request on one event loop, so the Map needs no locking. Concurrent requests from one session just see each other's fingerprints in arrival order, as today.
- **Migration/rollback:** none needed. Rolling back restores the current whole-message hashing with no leftover state.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** keep the `[aidevops] cache-stability: session=… segment=…` prefix and only append fields, so existing `rg` recipes and older plugin processes' lines stay comparable.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a retried identical request produces identical fingerprints and logs nothing. Retries must not be reported as breaks (add this to a test if cheap).
- **Partial failure/recovery:** fail-open. Catch any exception inside `observe` so the request goes out unmodified, and never mutate `parsed`. Performance: hash each block once and store only hashes, types and lengths. Privacy: at most one 80-char snippet per break, and `account` stays hashed.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-cache-stability.mjs
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-provider-auth-cch.mjs
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the first command proves the family key, block diff, privacy cap and fail-open (acceptance items 1–4) in `cache-stability.mjs`. The second proves the caller in `provider-auth-body.mjs` still transforms bodies unchanged. The third covers changed-file lint and complexity for all three files, including the docs.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required. The change is one plugin module with a single caller.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

WIP-commit after step 3 with the tests passing, before running linters.

### Scope Boundaries

- Do not change request bodies, cache_control placement, OpenCode pruning, or thinking handling. Attribution only.
- Do not add persistence (DB tables or files) for fingerprints.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/cache-stability.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-cache-stability.mjs`
- `.agents/reference/context-efficiency.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Alternating title/summary (no tools) and agent (tools) requests in one session log no `cache-stability` lines (new test).
- [ ] A tool added to or removed from agent requests still logs `segment=tools` with `family=agent` (regression test).
- [ ] A modified `tool_result` or removed `thinking` block in an earlier message logs `segment=history` with `block=`, `type=`, `change=` and `chars=` (new tests).
- [ ] No log line carries more than 80 chars of message content, and `observe` never throws into the request path.
- [ ] `context-efficiency.md` documents the new fields and this evaluation query, run with `sqlite3 -readonly ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/llm-requests.db`:

```sql
with r as (
  select session_id, timestamp, aidevops_version, tokens_input, tokens_cache_read, tokens_cache_write,
         lag(timestamp) over (partition by session_id order by timestamp) as prev_ts
  from llm_requests where provider_id = 'anthropic'
)
select aidevops_version, count(*) as requests, count(distinct session_id) as sessions,
  sum(prev_ts is not null and (julianday(timestamp) - julianday(prev_ts)) * 86400 < 300
      and tokens_cache_read = 0 and tokens_cache_write >= 10000) as warm_breaks,
  round(100.0 * sum(tokens_cache_read) / nullif(sum(tokens_input + tokens_cache_write + tokens_cache_read), 0), 1) as hit_pct
from r group by aidevops_version order by min(timestamp);
```

## Context & Decisions

- Follow-up to #32744 / PR #32747, which added the monitor and pinned the session greeting.
- Fixing the mutator is left to a later issue, once block-level lines identify it. Leading hypotheses: OpenCode tool-output pruning rewriting old `tool_result` text, and thinking blocks dropped from older assistant turns. Neither is verified.

title: Populate context/keywords.md search targets
body:
## What

Create and populate `context/keywords.md` plus the `context/keywords/` registry (targets, questions, clusters, modifiers, entities) so every search-facing change in this repo uses the same target keywords, AI-answer questions and entity names.

## Why

aidevops now standardises search targets per repository (`~/.aidevops/agents/seo/keywords-standard.md`). Repositories rank on GitHub, package registries and AI answers even without a website, and agents for copy, images, video, schema, social and PR read this registry instead of guessing keywords.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `context/keywords.md` — create with `aidevops keywords scaffold .`, then fill Positioning, Priorities, Naming and metadata rules.
- `context/keywords/*.toon` — rows added with `aidevops keywords add|set` (never hand-edit row counts).
- `.gitignore` and `AGENTS.md` — updated by the scaffold (public repos keep registry data out of Git).

### Files Scope

- context/keywords.md
- context/keywords/targets.toon
- context/keywords/queries.toon
- context/keywords/clusters.toon
- context/keywords/modifiers.toon
- context/keywords/entities.toon
- .gitignore
- AGENTS.md

### Implementation Steps

1. `aidevops keywords scaffold .` — detects surfaces, migrates any `context/target-keywords.md`, and picks tracked vs ignored data.
2. Add the brand entity (`role=self`, `same_as` profiles) and 3-5 competitors to `entities`.
3. Add 10-30 targets from existing evidence first (README, docs, GSC/Bing exports, package keywords, GitHub topics); set `business_value` 1-5. Paid research must stay inside the monthly budget (`aidevops keywords budget`).
4. Add 5-15 AI-answer questions (`queries`) people ask where this project should be recommended.
5. `aidevops keywords score --apply` then `aidevops keywords validate`.
6. Public repos: run `aidevops keywords sync` to publish the registry to the team hub; commit only `.gitignore` and `AGENTS.md`. If no hub is configured, say so in the PR body.

### Verification

```bash
aidevops keywords validate
aidevops keywords brief
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `aidevops keywords validate` passes.
- [ ] At least one `role=self` entity, 10 targets and 5 questions exist with evidence notes.
- [ ] Naming and metadata rules in `context/keywords.md` contain no template placeholders.
- [ ] Public repos commit no registry data; the PR body records hub sync status.

title: fix: pre-commit root allowlist rejects legitimate Vitest configuration
body:
## Observed defect

The deployed aidevops v3.37.15 pre-commit root-file validator rejects a legitimate new `vitest.config.ts` while migrating an npm-workspaces project from Vitest 3 workspace configuration to Vitest 4 `test.projects` configuration. No commit was created and no hook was bypassed.

Sanitized failure: `Repo root file validation FAILED` followed by `vitest.config.ts` and `Commit rejected: new repo root files not in allowlist`.

## Source and proposed repair

In `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh`, `_init_root_file_allowlist` (deployed lines 779–807) allows standard ESLint config names but no Vitest config filenames. `_is_root_file_allowed` accepts only exact entries, and `validate_repo_root_files` applies this global allowlist to newly staged root files in consumer projects. No project-scoped extension is exposed in those functions.

Add legitimate Vitest configuration filenames to the existing tool-config allowlist, keeping arbitrary reports and temporary root artifacts rejected. Follow the existing exact-name ESLint config entries rather than introducing a broad wildcard or disabling validation. Modify the framework source and normal deployment path, not consumer canonical hooks directly.

## Verification

- Add a focused regression in the existing hook-test harness: stage a valid root `vitest.config.ts` and confirm root-file validation accepts it.
- Retain a negative case for an arbitrary root `TEST-REPORT.md` or `VERIFY-example.md`.
- Check supported Vitest filename variants against primary documentation before including them.
- Run ShellCheck and the existing pre-commit validator tests. The exact regression-test path is not yet known; discover the test covering `_init_root_file_allowlist` or `validate_repo_root_files`.

The consumer migration already passes 391 test files, 3,985 tests, 12 available workspace typechecks, fresh installation, and full/production dependency audits. This report does not request a general hook bypass.

title: fix(opencode): update from an opencode2 shell rewrites the V1 config in V2 shape
body:
## Problem

Running `aidevops update` (or `setup.sh`) from a shell started by `opencode2` rewrites the shared OpenCode V1 config `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` in V2 shape (`agents`, `permissions`, `plugins`, `providers`, `update`). OpenCode V1 then refuses to start:

```
Configuration is invalid at <home>/.config/opencode/opencode.json
↳ V2 permissions are not supported by OpenCode V1. Use V1 "permission" rules or run opencode2. permissions
↳ ... agents.Build+.permissions (one line per primary agent)
```

Auto-update runs inside opencode2 sessions, so this affects every user who has the V2 preview installed.

## Root cause

- The `opencode2` shim (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`, the heredoc that writes the V2 shim) exports `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v2`, together with `OPENCODE_CONFIG` pointing at the isolated V2 config.
- `update_opencode_config` → `generate-runtime-config.sh all --runtime opencode` → `agent-discovery.py opencode opencode-json`.
- `.agents/scripts/agent-discovery.py` `_load_opencode_profile()` takes the profile from `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE` (so `v2`), but `output_opencode_json()` always writes the shared V1 path `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. The result is V2 shape in the V1 file.

This is the mirror image of #32738 / t18510, which kept the V1 plugin pass out of the V2 config.

## Fix

`agent-discovery.py` ignores an env profile override when `OPENCODE_CONFIG` points at a file other than the shared V1 config, and logs that it did so. An explicit override without an isolated `OPENCODE_CONFIG` still works.

### Files Scope
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/agent-discovery.py`

## Verification

With a sandbox `HOME` that contains a V1 config, and the V2 session env (`AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v2`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG=<v2-root>/config/opencode/opencode.json`):

- before the fix, `python3 .agents/scripts/agent-discovery.py opencode opencode-json` writes the V2 top-level keys;
- after the fix, it keeps V1 keys `agent,autoupdate,permission,plugin,provider,tools`;
- `opencode debug config` with the V1 binary loads the result.

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh` passes.

## Recovery for affected users

Upgrade, then run `aidevops update` once. The generator rewrites the V1 file in V1 shape.
