title: fix: project Node resolver treats .nvmrc patch pin as exact, failing workers before launch
body:
## What

`project-node-runtime.sh` (added by GH#32815 / PR #32819) treats a numeric version-file pin such as `.nvmrc` `24.18.0` as an exact patch requirement. Headless workers on any machine without that exact patch now fail before launch with `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=project_node_environment_failure ... session_count=0`, and the pulse escalates them to `status:blocked` "dispatch infrastructure failure".

## Why

Observed on a managed consumer repo on 2026-09-28. The repo pins `.nvmrc` `24.18.0` and `engines.node: ">=24.0.0 <25.0.0"`:

- The first failure came about an hour after #32819 merged. Since then 6+ issues have had 4–13 zero-output worker failures each, all on the two maintainer runners that do not have exactly 24.18.0.
- The machine that has Homebrew `node@24` = 24.18.0 resolves correctly.

GH#32815's acceptance criterion is major compatibility ("a project requiring Node 24 ... runs under an installed matching Node 24"). A patch-exact match is stricter than that intent. Other issues in the same resolver:

- Non-numeric pins (`lts/*`, `node`, `lts/iron`) can never match, so those projects always fail.
- The Homebrew-on-Linux prefix is not searched.

## How

`.agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh`:

- Split requirements into hard and preferred:
  - `engines.node` ranges stay hard.
  - A numeric version-file pin adds its major as a hard requirement and its full value as a preference.
  - Non-numeric aliases are ignored, because resolving them needs a network lookup.
- `_project_node_bin` first looks for a candidate that satisfies hard + preferred. If none exists, it accepts a hard-only match and prints a `WARNING` naming the pin. With no hard match it still prints `ENVIRONMENT FAILURE`, as before.
- Add `${HOMEBREW_PREFIX:-/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew}/opt/node@*/bin/node` to the candidates.

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-project-node-runtime.sh`: add cases for a same-major, different-patch fallback (with the warning) and for an `lts/*` alias. The existing conflicting-major and no-match cases must still fail closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.nvmrc` `24.18.0` + engines `>=24 <25` with only Node 24.11.0 installed resolves to 24.11.0 and warns.
- [ ] An exact 24.18.0 is still preferred over another 24.x when both are installed.
- [ ] Root pin 24 with scoped pin 25 still fails closed. Only Node 26 still fails with `ENVIRONMENT FAILURE`.
- [ ] `.nvmrc` `lts/*` alone returns "no requirement" (rc 2) instead of failing.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-project-node-runtime.sh` and ShellCheck pass.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-project-node-runtime.sh

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

The canonical-Git command guard treats any Git repo whose root contains `.aidevops.json` as a managed canonical checkout. That includes throwaway test repos created with `mktemp -d`. As a result, `git add` and `git read-tree` are blocked inside hook test fixtures that write `.aidevops.json`.

## Evidence

Found while implementing #32805 (PR #32838). `test-pre-commit-split.sh` builds a temporary fixture repo (`mktemp -d` + `git init`). Once the fixture contained `.aidevops.json`, the next staging calls failed:

```text
BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git read-tree'. Use a linked worktree for edits. ...
BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git add'. ...
```

Two fixture assertions failed because the files were never staged. Root cause:

- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_management.py:57-62`: `is_managed_root()` returns true when `(root / ".aidevops.json").is_file()`, even if the root is not registered in `repos.json`.
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_repository.py:114-121`: a non-linked checkout with that marker is classified as canonical.

Current workaround in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-split.sh` (`_root_mode_run`): write `.aidevops.json` only after staging, and delete it after the hook runs. This works, but every future fixture that needs a project config has to know about it, and the failure only shows up locally. CI runners don't have the guard.

## How

Files to modify:

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/canonical_git_management.py` (`is_managed_root`): do not treat a bare `.aidevops.json` marker as managed when **both** are true: the resolved root is not in `_registered_roots()`, and the root is under the real system temp dir (`tempfile.gettempdir()` realpath, plus `$TMPDIR`) or `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`. Registered repos and marker repos outside temp locations keep today's protection. Follow the temp-dir checks already used in `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py` (`_is_isolated_routines_publisher`, and the `aidevops-prospective-todo.` probe), which compare `os.path.realpath(tempfile.gettempdir())`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`: add cases:
  1. An unregistered `mktemp -d` repo with `.aidevops.json` allows `git add`.
  2. A registered repo (via an `AIDEVOPS_REPOS_FILE` fixture) still blocks.
  3. A marker repo outside temp dirs still blocks.
- Optional follow-through: simplify `_root_mode_run` in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-split.sh` so it writes `.aidevops.json` before staging.

Trust boundary: the exemption only covers disposable temp roots that are not registered in `repos.json`, so real canonical checkouts can't opt out by adding a marker file. Mark the new check `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_management.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-split.sh`

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-git-safety-guard.sh
```

title: consolidated: handle OpenCode runtime lockfile drift in headless worktrees
body:
_Supersedes #32721 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Prevent headless workers from stopping on OpenCode-generated drift in a managed repository's tracked `.opencode/package-lock.json` or `.opencode/bun.lock`, while preserving genuine user/session changes. Add worker guidance for safely distinguishing and discarding runtime-only drift before rebase; optionally prevent such drift at worktree preparation if its provenance can be established safely.

## Why

OpenCode rewrites these files in each checkout and creates `.opencode/.gitignore` entries for them, but a tracked lockfile is not ignored. Differences limited to `@opencode-ai/plugin` and `@opencode-ai/sdk` version and integrity hashes (for example 1.18.31 → 1.18.32) leave a dirty worktree the worker did not intentionally edit. A worker following “do not revert others' changes” refuses to restore or stash the file; `git rebase` fails with “You have unstaged changes”, the attempt ends with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=target_code_blocker`, and nothing is pushed. A managed-repo worker lost a 32-minute attempt on 2026-09-28 after building artifacts. Untracking the lockfile fixes a single repo, not other managed repos that track it.

## Reproducer

In a repository with a tracked `.opencode/package-lock.json` (or `.opencode/bun.lock`), start OpenCode in a fresh headless worktree using a runner whose `@opencode-ai/plugin`/`@opencode-ai/sdk` versions differ from the committed lockfile. Inspect `git diff -- .opencode/package-lock.json` (or the Bun lockfile): the reported case changes only those package versions and integrity hashes. `git status --short` reports the tracked lockfile modified despite no worker edit; a subsequent `git rebase origin/<base>` refuses to proceed with unstaged changes. The 2026-09-28 report observed this failure and an unpushed 32-minute attempt; reproduce in a disposable fixture rather than changing a managed repository's lockfile.

## How

- **Required guidance:** In `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md:171-180`, adjacent to the fresh-worktree dependency/rebase instructions (GH#32633), explain that a tracked `.opencode/package-lock.json` or `.opencode/bun.lock` is runtime-owned **only when the entire observed diff is confined to `@opencode-ai/*` versions and integrity hashes**. Before rebasing, verify the path and diff, restore only that confirmed runtime-only lockfile to its committed version (for example `git checkout -- <verified-file>`), and never commit the runtime rewrite or classify that verified rewrite as another session's work. Do not restore uncertain, intentional, or other tracked modifications. Prefer the repository's established safe Git restore convention if it differs.
- **Optional preparation:** Start with `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:156-168`, which sources `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh` and `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh`; locate the actual headless worktree creation/preparation path before selecting an edit. If a tracked runtime lockfile can safely be identified at preparation time, consider `git update-index --skip-worktree` after worktree creation so OpenCode rewrites do not present as dirty. Assess whether this could hide a real worker edit, how the bit is cleared, and how the pre-rebase and final-diff checks still detect intentional changes; do not implement masking if those guarantees cannot be met. The required guidance path is the safe minimum.
- **Optional repository health:** Where `aidevops init` or repository health checks inspect tracked files, consider warning that tracked OpenCode runtime lockfiles should be untracked with `git rm --cached` and covered by a root `.gitignore` entry. This is a suggestion to the repository owner, not authorization to change another repository's index or remove its lockfile.
- **Reference test:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-worktree-tests.sh:1-10` is sourced by the existing headless runtime test harness. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh` covers private-workload behavior. Confirm actual functions and available runtime/tool versions before editing or running tests. If the optional preparation requires a directly necessary sourced library not in the initial scope, apply `reference/worker-discipline.md` “Integration scope recovery” first; do not edit undeclared paths without a corrected brief.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/workflows/full-loop.md
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-worktree-tests.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh (integration scope recovery: the worktree test module is sourced-only; new tests must be registered in this harness main() to run)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A worker encountering only OpenCode-owned lockfile version/integrity drift can rebase and push without a `target_code_blocker`; neither OpenCode runtime lockfile rewrite is committed.
- [ ] A genuine change to another tracked file, or an ambiguous/intentional change in an OpenCode lockfile, is never silently restored or concealed.
- [ ] If optional worktree-prep behavior is implemented, a shellcheck-clean focused test creates a repo with tracked `.opencode/package-lock.json`, simulates an `@opencode-ai/plugin` version rewrite, and shows clean `git status --short`; otherwise exercise the documented safe restore and show `git rebase origin/<base>` succeeds. Cover `.opencode/bun.lock` equivalently where the implementation handles it.
- [ ] Existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh` private-workload checks still pass; run the applicable changed-file lint/ShellCheck checks.

## Context & Decisions

- Original report by @marcusquinn: runtime rewrites of tracked OpenCode lockfiles, not a user's code change, caused an unrecoverable dirty-worktree rebase and a lost 32-minute attempt. The worktree guidance is required; index masking and repo-health warnings are optional. Repository-side untracking is a local fix, not a replacement for framework-wide guidance.
- Per @vladimirdulov: the original issue's scope declaration did not satisfy the dispatch validator; a canonical, machine-readable `### Files Scope` with exact paths is necessary. This was a brief-format hold, not a new behavioral requirement.
- Per @marcusquinn's later clarification: the parent scope was repaired and `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check <N> <body> 1` returned 0; the missing-scope hold was resolved. Agent-runtime issue creation failing closed on unscoped `auto-dispatch` briefs is separately tracked as #32880, not part of this implementation.
- No commenter rejected the original guidance or made optional worktree preparation/repo-health checks mandatory. Real tracked changes must remain protected by the original regression guarantee.

## Contributors

cc @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

title: bug(planning): held no-auto-dispatch tasks never leave publication:pending because reconcile requires worker readiness
body:
## Description

Planning publication never clears `publication:pending` for held interactive tasks (`#no-auto-dispatch`). The reconciler gates every task on the full worker-dispatch readiness check, including tasks that will never be dispatched to a worker. Briefs for held interactive tasks are intentionally lighter (the operator implements them in session), so they fail `check-readiness` and the label stays forever.

Effect: every held interactive task created through `/new-task` in a managed repo keeps `publication:pending` indefinitely after its planning PR merges. The Issue Sync workflow run on the merge commit fails (`Planning publication failed`), on every subsequent push to the default branch, for as long as any such task is open. One task in the observing repo has been stuck for over a day, and every later merge re-fails the workflow.

## Expected Behavior

For a task whose TODO.md entry is `#no-auto-dispatch` (held / interactive-only), reconciliation should validate only what publication needs: the canonical task line exists on the default branch, its `ref:GH#N` matches the issue, and the brief file exists. It should then remove `publication:pending`. Full `check-readiness` (worker-ready brief schema v2) should gate only tasks that will be auto-dispatched (`#auto-dispatch`).

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (GitHub Actions, `issue-sync.yml` on push to `main` after merging a planning PR created by `planning-commit-helper.sh`; repo slug redacted):

```
bash __aidevops/.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh reconcile \
  --repo "$PUBLICATION_REPO" --sha "$PUBLICATION_SHA"
```

**Actual output**:

```
[WARNING] t29/#89: canonical task, ref, or brief validation failed; retaining publication:pending
[WARNING] t28/#79: canonical task, ref, or brief validation failed; retaining publication:pending
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
...
##[error]Planning publication failed; bounded relationship safety repair completed or was checkpointed for retry.
```

The same happened in a second managed repo for two newly published tasks.

Running the gate directly on one of the affected briefs (a held interactive task, TODO.md tags `#interactive #no-auto-dispatch #tier:standard`):

```
$ verify-brief-helper.sh check-readiness todo/tasks/t29-brief.md
WORKER_READY=false
SCORE=4
THRESHOLD=4
SCHEMA=v2
VALIDATION_ERRORS=files-to-modify:target;implementation-steps:substantive;write-surface:Callers/readers;write-surface:Writers/mutation paths;write-surface:Schemas/config;...;hazard:Concurrency/atomicity;...;verification:surface-mapping;verification:command;acceptance:negative-regression;
```

The task line, `ref:GH#N` and brief file are all present on the default branch at the merge SHA. Only the readiness check fails.

**Expected output**: `t29/#89: planning publication reconciled`; `publication:pending` removed; workflow succeeds.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` push-to-default-branch job, step running `planning-publication-reconcile.sh reconcile --repo ... --sha ...`.
- **Call chain**: `cmd_reconcile` (`.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh:253`) lists open `publication:pending` issues, calls `_publication_reconcile_one` (`:175`), which calls `_publication_validate_mapping` (`:165`). Its line `:171` runs `verify-brief-helper.sh check-readiness "$brief_path" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1`; that returns 1 for held briefs, and `:179` prints the warning and keeps the label.
- **Integrated verification**: the CI run log above (production path), plus direct `check-readiness` on the same brief returning `WORKER_READY=false`.

**Causal code**: `.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh:171`, present on `main` (last file change c244ac65d, 2026-09-27, GH#32588).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a managed repo with `issue-sync.yml`, run `/new-task` for an interactive task and tag it `#interactive #no-auto-dispatch` with an ordinary (not worker-ready) brief.
2. `planning-commit-helper.sh "plan: ..."` creates the planning PR; merge it.
3. Observe the Issue Sync push run on the merge commit fail with the warning above; the issue keeps `publication:pending`.

## Suggested fix

In `_publication_validate_mapping` (or its caller), run `check-readiness` only when the task line carries `#auto-dispatch` (equivalently, when the desired labels include `auto-dispatch`). For held tasks, keep the task-line, ref and brief-existence checks. Add a regression case in the reconcile tests: a `#no-auto-dispatch` task with a non-worker-ready brief reconciles and loses `publication:pending`; an `#auto-dispatch` task with the same brief still stays pending.

## Workarounds Applied

None. The labels were left in place; a manual label removal would hide the defect.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.37.22 (latest 3.37.22)
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21
- **gh CLI**: 2.100.0

## Additional Context

Related, not duplicates: #32542 (template/validator label mismatch; fixed), #32608 (repos without Issue Sync; merge-time reconcile added), #32588 (closed issues).

Possible sibling, **unconfirmed**: the merge-time reconcile added for #32608 (`full-loop-helper-merge.sh:1685-1708`) runs in the canonical checkout and requires canonical `HEAD` to equal the merge SHA (`planning-publication-reconcile.sh:61-70`). Interactive sessions keep canonical checkouts read-only, so this path always printed `Refusing reconciliation: HEAD is not exact origin/main SHA ...` and `CANONICAL_SYNC_PENDING=true reason=origin_fetch_failed` in the observing session. Separately, `_merge_refresh_canonical_for_cleanup` (`full-loop-helper-merge.sh:1824,1833`) runs `git fetch` and `git rev-parse origin/<branch>` without `-C "$canonical_dir"`, so it acts on the caller's working directory rather than the target canonical repo. Not verified whether that caused the fetch failure here.

title: fix(pulse-triage): brief-hold and brief-repair comments falsely trigger issue consolidation
body:
## What

Stop brief-hold and brief-repair comments from counting as "substantive" discussion in the consolidation trigger, so a held-then-repaired brief no longer spawns a `consolidation-task` child.

## Why

Consolidation tasks jumped from ~1–5/day to 7 on 2026-09-28. Three of the four parents (#32760, #32826, #32849) have exactly two >=500-char comments, neither of them discussion:

1. `<!-- aidevops:brief-hold reason=missing_files_scope ... -->` — machine hold notice (756 chars), introduced 2026-09-27 by GH#32598.
2. `Brief repaired: added a canonical ### Files Scope ...` — operational repair note (827 chars).

`_consolidation_filter_substantive_comments` does not exclude either shape, so threshold=2 fires. The false children are #32896, #32898, #32901.

## Reproducer

`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/32849/comments` returns a brief-hold comment, a "Brief repaired" comment, and then "Issue Consolidation Dispatched" (#32901). Feeding the first two into `_consolidation_filter_substantive_comments` yields length 2, which is at or above `ISSUE_CONSOLIDATION_COMMENT_THRESHOLD=2`.

## How

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh` — add `^<!-- aidevops:brief-(hold|scope-normalized)` and `^Brief (repaired|scope normalized):` to the `$patterns` list in `_consolidation_filter_substantive_comments` (~line 925).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` — add a filter regression case modelled on `test_stale_recovery_tick_comments_are_filtered`.

### Files Scope

.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh

## Acceptance

- Hold + repair comments alone do not trigger consolidation; threshold (2) unchanged.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` passes; shellcheck clean.
- Cleanup: close #32896, #32898, #32901 as false positives and clear `needs-consolidation` on #32760, #32826, #32849.

title: bug(full-loop): _merge_refresh_canonical_for_cleanup fetches and reads origin ref in caller cwd, not canonical_dir
body:
## What

`_merge_refresh_canonical_for_cleanup` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` mixes repositories. It reads the target canonical checkout's branch and `HEAD` with `git -C "$canonical_dir"` (`:1829`, `:1831`). But it runs `git fetch --quiet origin "$default_branch"` (`:1824`) and `git rev-parse "origin/${default_branch}"` (`:1833`) with **no** `-C`, so those two commands act on the caller's working directory.

Found while reviewing #32904; the reporter flagged it as an unconfirmed sibling, and the code on `main` (936b4f2bb) confirms the missing `-C`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`

## Reproducer

**Causal status**: confirmed by code inspection; runtime impact unconfirmed. The #32904 reporter saw `CANONICAL_SYNC_PENDING=true reason=origin_fetch_failed`, but it has not been verified that this defect caused that output.

Static evidence on `main` 936b4f2bb (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`):

```
1824:	if ! git fetch --quiet origin "$default_branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
1829:	current_canonical_branch=$(git -C "$canonical_dir" branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || true)
1831:	canonical_head=$(git -C "$canonical_dir" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)
1833:	remote_head=$(git rev-parse "origin/${default_branch}" 2>/dev/null || true)
```

Runtime reproduction: source the helper, `cd "$HOME"` (not a Git repo), and call `_merge_refresh_canonical_for_cleanup <clean current canonical dir> main`. Expected: `LIFECYCLE_STATE=CANONICAL_SYNCED`. Actual (predicted from the code): `CANONICAL_SYNC_PENDING=true reason=origin_fetch_failed`.

## Impact

- If the caller's cwd is a linked worktree of the same repository, refs are shared, so the result happens to be correct.
- If the cwd is a different repository (cross-repo full-loop, or a session rooted elsewhere), the fetch updates the wrong repo. `remote_head` then comes from the wrong `origin`, so the helper reports `CANONICAL_SYNC_PENDING` or a bogus `reason=origin_fetch_failed` for the target.
- If the cwd is not a Git repo, the fetch fails outright and prints `CANONICAL_SYNC_PENDING=true reason=origin_fetch_failed`, even when the canonical repo is reachable.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` `_merge_refresh_canonical_for_cleanup`, change `:1824` to `git -C "$canonical_dir" fetch --quiet origin "$default_branch"` and `:1833` to `git -C "$canonical_dir" rev-parse "origin/${default_branch}"`. The sibling `_merge_report_canonical_sync_state` (`:1858-1861`) already uses this `-C` pattern.
2. Check whether the canonical-guard shell policy allows `git -C <canonical> fetch` from this helper path. If the guard blocks canonical fetches, route through the audited `canonical-recovery-helper.sh` refresh instead of adding an exemption.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- Run the existing full-loop merge tests: `rg -l "_merge_refresh_canonical_for_cleanup\|CANONICAL_SYNC" .agents/scripts/tests/`, then run the matching files.
- Manual: call the function with cwd set to an unrelated directory (for example `$HOME`) and a clean, current canonical dir. Expect `LIFECYCLE_STATE=CANONICAL_SYNCED`, not `origin_fetch_failed`.

## Acceptance

- Both git commands target `$canonical_dir`.
- No behaviour change when cwd is a linked worktree of the same repo.

Tier: `tier:simple` (two-line, pattern-matched change).

title: bug(cleanup): missing-worktree metadata never pruned across managed repos — /tmp wiped on reboot leaves prunable entries that trip the 200-worktree dispatch cap
body:
## Description

Missing-worktree metadata is never pruned for managed repos when the worktree directory disappears outside aidevops. The most common way that happens is an OS reboot wiping `/tmp`. Stale `prunable` entries then accumulate until the per-repo worktree cap (`AIDEVOPS_MAX_WORKTREES`, default 200, `pulse-dispatch-core.sh:322`) blocks all dispatch for that repo.

## Observed (aidevops 3.37.22, Ubuntu 24.04.5)

- `website-factory` (a managed repo): 232 registered worktrees, **216** of them `prunable gitdir file points to non-existent location`, almost all `/tmp/tmp.*`. Two other managed repos had 135 and 115 prunable entries.
- `pulse.log`: 290 × `Dispatch blocked ... worktree capacity remains unavailable after bounded guarded cleanup`, all for this repo.
- `cleanup_worktrees.log*`: **0** occurrences of `pruned missing worktree metadata` or `missing worktree metadata prune failed`. The prune path has never run for these repos.
- The same `/tmp` paths were repeatedly logged as `worktree-skipped ... cwd-visibility-degraded` (3,771 skip lines in the rotated log). The now-resolved #32871 class of issue left them in place until the reboot removed the directories.
- Ubuntu `/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/tmp.conf`: `D /tmp 1777 root root 30d` (wiped at boot). The last boot was the same day.
- A manual `git worktree prune` on the three repos dropped them from 232→17, 187→50 and 126→11, and unblocked dispatch.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
git -C <managed-repo> worktree list --porcelain | rg -c '^prunable'
```

**Actual output**: `216` (website-factory, before manual prune). The pulse log repeatedly shows `Dispatch blocked for #N in <slug>: worktree capacity remains unavailable after bounded guarded cleanup` (290 lines).

**Expected output**: `0` after a cleanup cycle; dispatch not blocked by entries whose directories no longer exist.

**Causal status**: confirmed. A manual `git worktree prune` removed exactly the stale entries (232→17) and unblocked the cap. There were 0 prune log lines for these repos across both cleanup logs.

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: the pulse dispatch gate `_dispatch_worktree_capacity_gate` (`pulse-dispatch-core.sh:204`) counts registered worktrees, including `prunable` ones. Its remediation `_dispatch_cleanup_worktree_capacity` → `cleanup_worktrees`, together with async cleanup `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` `main`, is the only automatic cleanup.
- **Call chain**: `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh:224-259` `_prune_current_repo_missing_worktree_metadata` → `prune_missing_worktree_metadata` (`audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh:1902`). It is scoped to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the helper cwd and stops after the first prunable path (`break`, L243). The other `git worktree prune` calls (`pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh:415,827,1229`) run only after aidevops itself removes a directory. No path prunes externally vanished directories in other managed repos.
- **Integrated verification**: on the live host, both `cleanup_worktrees.log` and `.log.1` contain 0 `pruned missing worktree metadata` / `prune failed` lines, while 216 prunable entries existed in one managed repo. A manual `git worktree prune` reduced the counts 232→17, 187→50 and 126→11.

**Steps**:

1. Have pulse create temp worktrees under `/tmp` for a managed repo (normal operation).
2. Reboot Ubuntu, which empties `/tmp` via systemd-tmpfiles.
3. Run pulse cleanup cycles. The `prunable` count never decreases; once it reaches 200 or more, dispatch for that repo is blocked.

## Root cause (code paths)

Metadata pruning only happens:

1. **After aidevops removes a worktree itself.** `pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh:415,827,1229` run `git -C "$rp" worktree prune`, but only after a successful `remove_worktree_path_permanently`.
2. **For the current repo only.** `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh:224-259` `_prune_current_repo_missing_worktree_metadata` resolves `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the helper's cwd. It then prunes only the **first** prunable path it finds (`break` at L243), not every managed repo.
3. **In manual `worktree-helper.sh remove` / `clean` flows** (`worktree-helper-cmds.sh:424`, `worktree-clean-lib.sh:1584`).

None of these covers "directory vanished externally in a managed repo". The dispatch cap gate (`_dispatch_worktree_capacity_gate` → `_dispatch_cleanup_worktree_capacity`) runs `cleanup_worktrees`, which only iterates existing directories. So the count never drops.

## Expected

Each cleanup cycle, for **every** repo in `repos.json`, prune metadata whose target path is absent. The existing `prune_missing_worktree_metadata` (`audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh:1902`) is already safe for this: it requires `! -e "$wt_path"` and verifies the entry is gone. Then the cap counts only live worktrees.

## Suggested fix

- In `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`, iterate over the managed repo paths, not just the cwd repo. Call `prune_missing_worktree_metadata` for each prunable, absent path (remove the single-entry `break`, or prune once per repo after confirming at least one absent entry).
- Optionally, have `_dispatch_worktree_capacity_gate` count only non-prunable entries, or prune missing metadata before counting. That way externally removed temp worktrees can never block dispatch.
- Skip locked worktrees (native `git worktree prune` already does).

## Verification

- Create a linked worktree under a temp dir in a fixture repo, `rm -rf` the directory, and run the async cleanup helper from a **different** cwd. Assert the `prunable` entry is gone.
- Existing: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-metadata-prune.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh`.

## Environment

- aidevops 3.37.22, OpenCode, Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, bash 5.2.21, gh 2.100.0

See also: #32871 (why the `/tmp` worktrees weren't removed before the reboot).

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

The canonical-Git command guard treats any Git repo whose root contains `.aidevops.json` as a managed canonical checkout. That includes throwaway test repos created with `mktemp -d`. As a result, `git add` and `git read-tree` are blocked inside hook test fixtures that write `.aidevops.json`.

## Evidence

Found while implementing #32805 (PR #32838). `test-pre-commit-split.sh` builds a temporary fixture repo (`mktemp -d` + `git init`). Once the fixture contained `.aidevops.json`, the next staging calls failed:

```text
BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git read-tree'. Use a linked worktree for edits. ...
BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git add'. ...
```

Two fixture assertions failed because the files were never staged. Root cause:

- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_management.py:57-62`: `is_managed_root()` returns true when `(root / ".aidevops.json").is_file()`, even if the root is not registered in `repos.json`.
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_repository.py:114-121`: a non-linked checkout with that marker is classified as canonical.

Current workaround in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-split.sh` (`_root_mode_run`): write `.aidevops.json` only after staging, and delete it after the hook runs. This works, but every future fixture that needs a project config has to know about it, and the failure only shows up locally. CI runners don't have the guard.

## How

Files to modify:

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/canonical_git_management.py` (`is_managed_root`): do not treat a bare `.aidevops.json` marker as managed when **both** are true: the resolved root is not in `_registered_roots()`, and the root is under the real system temp dir (`tempfile.gettempdir()` realpath, plus `$TMPDIR`) or `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`. Registered repos and marker repos outside temp locations keep today's protection. Follow the temp-dir checks already used in `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py` (`_is_isolated_routines_publisher`, and the `aidevops-prospective-todo.` probe), which compare `os.path.realpath(tempfile.gettempdir())`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`: add cases:
  1. An unregistered `mktemp -d` repo with `.aidevops.json` allows `git add`.
  2. A registered repo (via an `AIDEVOPS_REPOS_FILE` fixture) still blocks.
  3. A marker repo outside temp dirs still blocks.
- Optional follow-through: simplify `_root_mode_run` in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-split.sh` so it writes `.aidevops.json` before staging.

Trust boundary: the exemption only covers disposable temp roots that are not registered in `repos.json`, so real canonical checkouts can't opt out by adding a marker file. Mark the new check `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_management.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-split.sh`

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-git-safety-guard.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-split.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

Test 18 in `test-pre-commit-split.sh` should pass without the stage-then-write ordering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unregistered temp-dir repos that contain `.aidevops.json` allow index mutations under the guard.
- [ ] Registered repos and non-temp marker repos stay blocked (tests prove both).
- [ ] Existing guard tests pass.

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Problem

The orphan-recovery path opens a PR from a worker's partial branch with `Resolves #N`, even when the worker was killed before finishing. When the deterministic merge pass merges that PR, the issue closes as done, labelled `status:done` and `solved:worker`, although its acceptance criteria are unmet.

Observed on 2026-09-28 in a managed project repo:

1. A `tier:standard` worker on a large multi-file implementation issue ended `watchdog_stall_killed` after 43 minutes.
2. Its pushed branch held one WIP commit (2 changed lines in one planning brief). The issue's required new source file was never created.
3. The orphan-recovery path opened `auto-recover: orphaned worker branch for #N` with `Resolves #N`.
4. The pulse deterministic merge pass merged it about 20 minutes later, which closed the issue. A maintainer found the false completion only by reviewing post-merge and had to reopen and re-label by hand.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`, `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` (deployed copy around lines 604-609):

```bash
if [[ -n "$issue_number" ]]; then
    pr_title="auto-recover: orphaned worker branch for #${issue_number}"
    closing_line="Resolves #${issue_number}"
fi
```

A recovery PR is by definition built from a worker that exited before declaring completion. Its branch is evidence of progress, not of completion, but the closing keyword turns the merge into a completion claim.

## Proposed fix

- Use `For #${issue_number}` in orphan-recovery PR bodies, for both `worker_branch_orphan` and `worker_local_branch_unpushed`, so merging preserves the work without closing the issue.
- After such a merge, the issue should return to `status:available` for redispatch, not `status:done`. Reuse the existing post-merge path for non-closing PRs; do not add a new one.
- Optional: when the release reason is `watchdog_stall_killed` or similar, have the recovery PR body say that the worker was killed mid-task and list the issue's scoped files that the branch does not touch.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`: `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` (`closing_line`) and `_build_orphan_recovery_pr_body`.
- Tests: the existing orphan-recovery tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`. Find them with `rg -l "orphan-recovery|_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr" .agents/scripts/tests`; if none cover the closing line, add a focused case.
- Docs: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` (orphan-recovery sections), if it describes the closing keyword.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-orphan-recovery-pr-base.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`

## Verification

- A unit or shell test asserts that the recovery PR body contains `For #N` and not `Resolves #N`, `Closes #N` or `Fixes #N`.
- ShellCheck is clean on the changed script.

body:
## What

Replace the hand-maintained list of operational-comment regexes in `_consolidation_filter_substantive_comments` with one shared, machine-readable marker (for example `<!-- aidevops:ops kind=<name> -->`). Every automated or lifecycle comment emits the marker, and the filter excludes it structurally. Keep the existing regexes as a legacy fallback for comments already posted.

## Why

Each new automated comment type silently becomes "substantive" discussion until someone adds it to the regex list. The most recent case: the `missing_files_scope` brief-hold comment (GH#32598, 2026-09-27) produced 4 false `consolidation-task` children within a day (#32893, #32896, #32898, #32901), fixed reactively by #32905 / PR #32909. ## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --state all --label consolidation-task --search "created:2026-09-28"`

**Actual output:** 7 consolidation-task children in one day, including #32893, #32896, #32898 and #32901. Their parents' only comments of 500+ characters were the machine brief-hold notice and the repair note. Before PR #32909, `_consolidation_substantive_comments` counted those parents as 3/2/2/2 substantive (threshold 2).

**Expected:** automated lifecycle comments never count, without needing a per-shape regex. Any new operational comment of 500+ characters posted twice reproduces the problem today.

title: OAuth pool: expired auth-error cooldown leaves valid account unavailable, pulse capacity stuck at 0
body:
## What

An OAuth pool account marked `auth-error` stays unavailable to pulse dispatch after its cooldown expires, even when its token is valid. Pulse capacity drops to zero with no alert until the token nears expiry (up to ~a week) or an operator runs `oauth-pool-helper.sh reset-cooldowns <provider>`.

## Observed

- Single-account `openai` pool. `oauth-pool.json` showed `status: "auth-error"`, `cooldownUntil: 0`.
- `oauth-pool-helper.sh check openai`: `Token: expires in 169h`, `Refresh token: present`, `Token endpoint: OK`.
- Supervisor LLM on the same provider ran successfully during the outage, so credentials worked.
- Every pulse cycle for ~3 days logged:
  `Dispatch_capacity: ... provider_accounts_total=1 provider_accounts_available=0 account_cap=0 auth_error_accounts=1 ... simultaneous_target_final=0`
  `Dispatch_max skipped: no available worker slots (max=0, active=0, available=0)`
- `oauth-pool-helper.sh reset-cooldowns openai` restored capacity on the next cycle (`simultaneous_target_final=3`, `provider_accounts_available=1`) and queued issues dispatched.

## Root cause (three interacting paths)

1. `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh` (`available_account`, ~L95-98) treats any `auth-error` account as unavailable, **ignoring `cooldownUntil`**. `rate-limited` correctly honours the cooldown.
2. `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_auto_clear.py` (`_clear_expired_cooldown`, ~L30-41) zeroes an expired cooldown but deliberately keeps `auth-error` status, so the account never returns to `idle`.
3. `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_refresh.py` (`_should_refresh_account`, ~L71-73) skips refresh while the token is far from expiry, so the success path that sets `status=active` (`_apply_refresh_response`) never runs.

Result: `auth-error` + expired cooldown + unexpired token = permanently unavailable until expiry-driven refresh or manual reset. Platform-independent (Python + jq logic).

## Suggested fix

Once an `auth-error` cooldown has expired, re-validate instead of staying blocked. Options (pick one or combine):

- In `_should_refresh_account`, treat `status == "auth-error"` with an expired (or zero) cooldown as refresh-eligible regardless of token expiry; a successful refresh already sets `active`, a failure re-applies exponential backoff via `_mark_refresh_failure`.
- Alternatively, have `pulse-capacity.sh` treat `auth-error` with `cooldownUntil <= now` as a probe candidate (e.g. allow one canary dispatch) rather than hard-unavailable.
- Emit a pulse health/dashboard signal when capacity is zero solely because of `auth-error` accounts for more than N cycles, with the `reset-cooldowns` remedy in the message.

Do not simply flip `auth-error` to `idle` in auto-clear without a probe, or genuinely revoked credentials would thrash.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_refresh.py`
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-lib/pool_ops_auto_clear.py`

title: fix(pulse): infrastructure hold counts its own notices and never resets
body:
## What

The dispatch-infrastructure hold (`_dlw_hold_repeated_zero_output`) counts its own notices as evidence, and it never forgets failures from before a fix. Once an issue reaches the threshold, it stays held forever, and each dispatch cycle posts another notice.

## Why (evidence)

- A private managed-repo issue: every OWNER/MEMBER comment that matches the zero-output evidence pattern is a `<!-- dispatch-infrastructure-failure -->` hold notice (7 of 7). The notice text says "zero-output or zero-attempt worker failures", which matches `zero[- ]output` in `_DLW_ZERO_OUTPUT_EVIDENCE_PATTERN` (`pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:56`). Each hold adds one to the next count (12 → 13).
- The remaining evidence is unmatched `DISPATCH_CLAIM` comments from the Node runtime failure (`project_node_environment_failure`, fixed by GH#32897 / v3.37.24). No reset boundary exists, so that history counts forever.
- The label timeline shows pulses on different runners flipping `status:blocked` ↔ `status:available` about every 10–50 minutes. Each flip leads to a new lease comment and a new hold comment, which is a comment storm.

## Reproducer

1. On an issue that already has at least 4 unmatched `DISPATCH_CLAIM` comments from a fixed runtime failure, let the pulse dispatch it.
2. `_dlw_hold_repeated_zero_output` posts a `<!-- dispatch-infrastructure-failure -->` comment ("…accumulated N zero-output…") and sets `status:blocked`.
3. Another pulse flips the issue back to available. The next dispatch counts N+1, because the previous hold comment matches `zero[- ]output`, and holds again.
4. Check: `gh api --paginate repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<N>/comments --jq '.[] | select(.body | test("zero[- ]output";"i")) | (.body | test("dispatch-infrastructure-failure"))'` prints only `true`.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh`:
  - `_dlw_comment_bloat_metrics_from_json`: exclude comments that carry breaker markers (`dispatch-infrastructure-failure`) from the explicit zero-output and zero-attempt counts. Count only evidence and claims created after the latest authoritative reset boundary: an OWNER/MEMBER comment containing `aidevops-signed-approval` or `<!-- dispatch-infrastructure-reset -->`.
  - `_dlw_zero_output_comment_count`: apply the same exclusion and boundary.
- EDIT the hold comment: tell maintainers that a `<!-- dispatch-infrastructure-reset -->` comment clears the count after a fix.
- Tests: extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh` (or the nearest existing test of these helpers).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Hold notices never count as zero-output or zero-attempt evidence.
- [ ] Evidence and unmatched claims before the latest authoritative reset or approval comment are ignored.
- [ ] Existing tests pass; new cases cover self-counting and reset; ShellCheck is clean.

title: consolidated: keep orphan-recovery merges from closing incomplete issues
body:
_Supersedes #32745 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Prevent orphan-recovery PRs for incomplete headless workers from closing their implementation issue on merge. Preserve partial work for review and redispatch instead of claiming completion.

## Why

On 2026-09-28, a `tier:standard` worker on a large multi-file issue was killed by `watchdog_stall_killed` after 43 minutes. Its branch contained one WIP commit changing two lines in a planning brief; the required new source file did not exist. Recovery opened `auto-recover: orphaned worker branch for #N` with a closing `Resolves #N` clause. The deterministic merge pass merged that partial branch about 20 minutes later, closing the issue and applying `status:done` and `solved:worker` even though its acceptance criteria were unmet. A maintainer had to reopen and relabel it. Per @marcusquinn, this happened a third time in the same managed repository: a successor to the second falsely closed issue was itself marked done when an orphan PR containing only a partial builder script and brief notes merged. The maintainer again corrected labels and filed another successor. This is systematic, not a one-off.

## Reproducer

In a managed project repo, start a multi-file worker issue whose acceptance requires a new source file. Kill the worker after it pushes only a WIP brief change, before it finishes or opens its own PR. `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` creates a PR for the orphan branch and, at `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:608`, embeds `Resolves #N` in its body. Merging that partial PR closes the implementation issue and applies completion labels despite the missing required source file. The reported `watchdog_stall_killed` run and the third repeat described above supply observed instances.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:426-446,603-615` — `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` currently assigns `closing_line="Resolves #${issue_number}"` at line 608 and passes it to `_build_orphan_recovery_pr_body`. Emit `For #${issue_number}` instead for both `worker_branch_orphan` and `worker_local_branch_unpushed` (the body builder selects mode at lines 432-439). Keep the PR title/identity and normal review/merge pipeline intact.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-orphan-recovery-pr-base.sh:130-160` — extend existing recovery PR tests to assert the generated body has `For #N` and no closing keywords for both remote and published-local branches; include the draft checkpoint path as applicable. Existing test stubs exercise `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` without a live GitHub write.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md:899` — only if its orphan-recovery guidance implies that recovered partial work closes the task; otherwise leave unchanged.

### Implementation Steps

1. Replace the closing keyword at `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:608` with a non-closing `For #${issue_number}` reference. The recovery PR means a worker exited without declaring completion; a branch is progress evidence, not proof of acceptance.
2. Verify both pushed-branch (`worker_branch_orphan`) and locally committed/unpushed-branch (`worker_local_branch_unpushed`) body paths. A draft dirty-worktree checkpoint must not assert completion either.
3. On merge the implementation issue must remain open and return to `status:available` for redispatch rather than `status:done`/`solved:worker`. Reuse the existing post-merge path for non-closing PRs; do not introduce another post-merge flow. If existing behavior cannot satisfy that, inspect the relevant caller and apply integration scope recovery before editing an adjacent file.
4. Optional, not required for completion: when release reason is `watchdog_stall_killed` or similar, identify the worker as killed mid-task in the recovery PR body and list the issue-scoped files absent from its branch, provided the evidence is available and the change stays within authorized scope.

### Verification Before Dispatch

Run `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-orphan-recovery-pr-base.sh` and `shellcheck .agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`. Inspect the captured PR body for `For #N` and absence of `Resolves #N`, `Closes #N`, and `Fixes #N` in each recovery mode. Validate the existing non-closing post-merge redispatch path rather than inventing a new one. Use `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` if required by the current repository gate.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-orphan-recovery-pr-base.sh
- EDIT: .agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh — integration scope recovery: `test_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr_uses_authoritative_worker_issue` (line ~1093) asserts the old `Resolves #N` recovery body and must assert `For #N`; verify with `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Orphan recovery PRs in both `worker_branch_orphan` and `worker_local_branch_unpushed` modes cite the linked issue as `For #N`, including draft checkpoint variants when generated.
- [ ] Their bodies do not contain `Resolves #N`, `Closes #N`, or `Fixes #N` for the incomplete issue; a merged recovery PR does not close or mark that issue `status:done`/`solved:worker`.
- [ ] After the partial PR merges, the issue remains open and is available for redispatch through the existing non-closing post-merge path, without a new post-merge flow.
- [ ] The focused orphan-recovery shell test and ShellCheck pass on the changed script.

## Context & Decisions

- Original report: three stages of the first false closure (stalled worker, two-line WIP branch, auto-recovery PR using a closing clause, merge-induced false completion) establish the root cause at `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:608`.
- Per @marcusquinn: a third repeat on a successor issue establishes systemic impact; non-closing `For #N` is the selected fix over trying to infer completed acceptance criteria from partial branches.
- Per @alex-solovyev: automated pre-dispatch tier checks first normalized `tier:simple` to `tier:standard` because the original body lacked an exact transform; the self-hosting dispatch-path override then selected `tier:thinking` because this task edits `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`. Carry `tier:thinking` into dispatch. These automated comments do not change the feature requirements.
- Preserve the parent's three-file scope; update diagnostics only if inaccurate. The optional killed-worker context is not a prerequisite. Do not confuse merge of a recovery checkpoint with a completed implementation.

## Contributors

cc @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

title: t18532: fix(compaction): cap compaction effort and route to first fitting simple-tier candidate
body:
## What

Cap OpenCode compaction reasoning effort independently of the session effort, and make the GH#32494 simple-tier compaction route choose the first simple-tier candidate that fits the managed compaction input instead of giving up when the first candidate is too small.

## Why

Interactive compaction stalled twice on 2026-09-28 (`~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/llm-requests.db`, `agent='compaction'`): Opus 5.5 `max` ran 196s and 165s with 0 output tokens, ended `MessageAbortedError`, then succeeded at `high` in 39s and 53s. Since 2026-09-01, Opus compaction averages 56s at medium, 78s at high, 146s at xhigh; Astra max averages 619s (max 1159s).

Root causes, verified:

1. OpenCode passes the session variant to compaction (`anomalyco/opencode` `packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts` uses `userMessage.model.variant`; `session/llm/request.ts` merges variant options last), so `agent.compaction.variant` cannot lower effort. The plugin `chat.params` hook receives `agent: "compaction"` and the merged options, so it can clamp effort there.
2. `applyCompactionRouting` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-routing.mjs`) only checks `routingProfile(routing, "simple").model`. A custom routing table listing `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` first (168K usable input < 240K target) disables the route even though `openai/gpt-6-luna` (260K) fits. No Luna compactions have been recorded since 2026-09-15.

## How

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-routing.mjs`: iterate `routingCandidates(routing, "simple")` and route to the first candidate whose input limit fits; keep user pins; add `capCompactionEffort(input, output, routing)` that clamps `effort`, `reasoningEffort`, `reasoning_effort` and `reasoning.effort` down (never up) to the routed variant for the routed model, otherwise to a `high` ceiling (`AIDEVOPS_COMPACTION_MAX_EFFORT` override).
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`: call the cap last in the `chat.params` hook.
- `.agents/tools/context/model-routing.md`: document the compaction route and ceiling.

### Files Scope

- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-routing.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs
- .agents/tools/context/model-routing.md
- TODO.md

## Acceptance

- With the routing table `simple: [haiku, luna]`, the config hook routes compaction to Luna; with no fitting candidate it leaves the parent model.
- A compaction `chat.params` call with Opus `effort: "max"` is clamped to `high`; non-compaction agents are untouched; lower efforts are never raised.
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs` passes.
- After deploy and an OpenCode restart, new `llm_requests` compaction rows show no `max`/`xhigh` duration spikes.

## Verification

`node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs`; post-deploy query: `select model_id, variant, duration_ms, error_type from llm_requests where agent='compaction' order by timestamp desc limit 10`.

title: t18534: fix(pulse): restore retry context lost to torn objective-evidence lines; add sanitised failure signals
body:
## What

Restore and enrich worker retry context:

1. Make objective-evidence ledger readers tolerant of malformed lines, and lock the unlocked failed-worker append that produces them.
2. Add bounded, sanitised failure signals from the newest local worker failure excerpt to the retry prompt.
3. Fix the cascade-escalation comment that tells the next worker to read prior comments, which contradicts the clean-room retry prompt.

## Why

- `~/.aidevops/state/objective-evidence.jsonl` contains 2 torn lines (the first from 2026-09-01: two concurrent CI-repair `worker.failed` records for a managed private repo interleaved mid-string). `objective-reconciliation-helper.sh` slurps the tail with `jq -s`, so one bad line fails the whole parse, `evidence_json` falls back to `[]`, and `disposition` returns `source:"none"` for every issue (`jq: parse error: Invalid numeric literal at line 1174`). Retry prompts have therefore carried no validated prior-attempt state since about 2026-09-01, and the `suppress_fast_fail`/`suppress_retry`/`suppress_enrichment` flags have been lost.
- The writer at `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh:242` appends records over 1KB with `printf >>` and no lock; `objective-reconciliation-helper.sh` already uses `_objective_acquire_append_lock`.
- `worker-activity-helper.sh:215` and `worker-failure-feedback-helper.sh:87` have the same `jq -s` failure mode.
- Retry prompts (`pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh` `_dlw_prior_attempt_context`) carry only classification tokens; the excerpt's `[WORKER_EXIT_DIAGNOSTICS]` line and tool error strings (for example `BLOCKED by shared command policy (...): shell redirection is unsupported`) would let the next attempt avoid repeating the same failure.
- `worker-lifecycle-common.sh:1706` says "review prior attempt comments", while the retry prompt excludes comments and prior model prose.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/objective-reconciliation-helper.sh` (both `tail | jq -s` readers, via one `_objective_read_evidence` helper), `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh` and `.agents/scripts/worker-failure-feedback-helper.sh`: parse line-by-line with `fromjson?`, dropping malformed lines.
- `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh`: take the shared `<ledger>.lockdir` mkdir lock (same directory as `_objective_acquire_append_lock`) around the append; fix the comment wording.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh`: add `_dlw_prior_failure_signals`. Repo scoping comes from the newest `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` row matching `repo_slug` + `session_key=issue-<N>`; its `output_file` must be a regular, non-symlink `issue-<N>-<UTC>-<pid>.log` directly inside `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-failure-excerpts` and at most 7 days old (a newer success row carries no excerpt, so recovered issues get nothing). Extract only `WORKER_EXIT_DIAGNOSTICS` key tokens and the last 3 distinct JSON `"error"` field strings (charset-restricted, 160 chars each), labelled as evidence, never instructions. A success disposition suppresses all retry context. Default retry-context budget raised to 1536 chars.

- .agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/worker-failure-feedback-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh

- .agents/scripts/tests/test-objective-reconciliation.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-worker-launch-comment-metrics.sh

title: t18535: fix(command-policy): resolve default git remote for bare push/fetch/pull; classify pushurl and --multiple remotes
body:
## What

Make the worker command policy resolve the destination of `git fetch`, `git pull`, `git push` and `git ls-remote` when no remote is named. Use the same remote git would choose, instead of failing closed as an unclassified destination. Close two related classification gaps in the same function.

## Why

- Workers are hard-blocked on a plain `git push`: `BLOCKED by shared command policy (forbid, network.worker-policy): [NET-TIER] BLOCKED: unclassified worker network destination (git-push-destination-missing)`. This appears in 7 retained September failure excerpts (for example `issue-1-20260928T005515Z-50825.log`, `issue-32682-20260927T234504Z-64283.log`). Each one costs a worker turn and pushes it towards retries or a stalled PR.
- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_git.py:41-43` records `git-<sub>-destination-missing` whenever no positional remote is present. Git itself resolves the remote from `branch.<current>.pushRemote` → `remote.pushDefault` → `branch.<current>.remote` → `origin` for push, and from `branch.<current>.remote` → `origin` for fetch, pull and ls-remote.
- Security gap 1: `_resolve_git_remote` (`.agents/scripts/command_policy_network.py:73`) returns fetch URLs only, so a push to a remote with a different `remote.<name>.pushurl` is classified by its fetch host.
- Security gap 2: `git fetch --multiple origin other` classifies only the first positional remote.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_network.py`:
  - factor the fixed-argv `git -C <cwd>` subprocess call into one bounded helper;
  - let `_resolve_git_remote` optionally include `--push` URLs.
- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_git.py`:
  - when no remote is named, resolve the default remote from git config with at most two extra bounded git calls, then classify its URLs exactly like an explicitly named remote;
  - for `push`, classify both fetch and push URLs;
  - `clone` without a repository stays unclassified;
  - `fetch`/`pull` with `--all` stay unclassified (all remotes);
  - `--multiple` classifies every positional remote;
  - fail closed on options that change which repository or remote URL git uses, because the policy resolves remotes from the working directory's config:
    - `-c`/`--config` keys under `remote.`, `branch.` and `url.`, and `core.sshCommand` (in addition to today's proxy/insteadOf check);
    - `--config-env=` (today only the separate-argument form is caught);
    - `--git-dir`.
    These already allowed explicitly named remotes to be misclassified; default resolution would otherwise widen them.
- Resolution failure keeps today's fail-closed `git-<sub>-destination-missing`.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/command_policy_git.py
- .agents/scripts/command_policy_network.py
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh
- TODO.md

## Acceptance

- In a worker linked worktree whose `origin` is `https://github.com/...`, `command-policy-helper.py check-command --worker --argv-json '["git","push"]'` (and `fetch`, `pull`) exits 0.
- The same command exits 20 with `network.worker-policy` when:
  - the resolved default remote is a Tier 5 host; or
  - `origin` has a Tier 5 `pushurl` (push only); or
  - `--multiple` names a Tier 5 remote as its second remote; or
  - `fetch --all` is used.
- `git clone` with no repository remains blocked.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh` passes with the new cases.
- `shellcheck` on the test script is clean.
- `python3 -m py_compile` passes on the changed modules.

title: review-issue-pr: posting the review after an existing signature stales the approval
body:
## Observed

During an interactive `/review-issue-pr` of #32913, the maintainer had already signed the issue (`approval-helper.sh verify` → `VERIFIED`, `proven-locked-continuity`). The workflow then required posting the structured review comment. That comment changed the content-bound snapshot, verify returned `STALE_APPROVAL` (`stale-or-unproven-continuity`), `full-loop-helper.sh start` refused to start, and the maintainer had to re-run `sudo aidevops approve issue 32913 marcusquinn/aidevops`.

`workflows/review-issue-pr.md` "Approval sequencing (MANDATORY)" assumes the review is posted before any signing. It does not cover the case where a valid signature already exists before the review is posted.

## Fix

title: consolidated: canonical-git-guard should not treat unregistered temp-dir repos with .aidevops.json as managed
body:
_Supersedes #32849 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Stop the canonical-Git command guard from treating disposable, unregistered temp-dir repos as managed canonical checkouts just because their root contains `.aidevops.json`. Today `git add` and `git read-tree` are blocked inside hook test fixtures created with `mktemp -d` that write `.aidevops.json`.

## Why

Found while implementing #32805 (PR #32838). `test-pre-commit-split.sh` builds a fixture repo (`mktemp -d` + `git init`). Once the fixture contained `.aidevops.json`, staging failed:

```text
BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git read-tree'. Use a linked worktree for edits. ...
BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git add'. ...
```

Two fixture assertions failed because files were never staged. Root cause:

- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_management.py:57-62`: `is_managed_root()` returns true when `(root / ".aidevops.json").is_file()`, even if the root is not registered in `repos.json`.
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_repository.py:114-121`: a non-linked checkout with that marker is classified as canonical (read-only reference).

Current workaround in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-split.sh` (`_root_mode_run`): write `.aidevops.json` only after staging and delete it after the hook runs. Every future fixture needing a project config must know this, and the failure only shows locally (CI runners lack the guard).

## How

- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_management.py` (`is_managed_root`): do not treat a bare `.aidevops.json` marker as managed when BOTH are true: the resolved root is not in `_registered_roots()`, and the root is under the real system temp dir (`os.path.realpath(tempfile.gettempdir())`, plus `$TMPDIR`) or `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`. Registered repos and marker repos outside temp locations keep today's protection. Follow the temp-dir checks in `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py` (`_is_isolated_routines_publisher`, and the `aidevops-prospective-todo.` probe), which compare `os.path.realpath(tempfile.gettempdir())` (read-only reference).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`: add cases:
  1. An unregistered `mktemp -d` repo with `.aidevops.json` allows `git add`.
  2. A registered repo (via an `AIDEVOPS_REPOS_FILE` fixture) still blocks.
  3. A marker repo outside temp dirs still blocks.
- Optional follow-through: simplify `_root_mode_run` in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-split.sh` so it writes `.aidevops.json` before staging.

Trust boundary: the exemption covers only disposable temp roots not registered in `repos.json`, so real canonical checkouts cannot opt out by adding a marker file. Mark the new check `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_management.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-split.sh`

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-git-safety-guard.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-commit-split.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

Test 18 in `test-pre-commit-split.sh` should pass without the stage-then-write ordering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unregistered temp-dir repos that contain `.aidevops.json` allow index mutations under the guard.
- [ ] Registered repos and non-temp marker repos stay blocked (tests prove both).
- [ ] Existing guard tests pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Original report and approach: @marcusquinn (interactive session, #32849).
- @vladimirdulov (automated scan): flagged the brief hold for missing `### Files Scope`.
- @marcusquinn: repaired the brief with a canonical `### Files Scope` so the pre-claim scope gate passes (rc=0 via `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`); systemic follow-up for fail-closed unscoped `auto-dispatch` briefs is #32880.

title: t18536: fix(worktree): log dependency provisioning reason codes; skip package dirs without a supported lockfile
body:
## What

Make worker dependency snapshot provisioning observable, and stop spending restore slots on package directories it can never provision.

1. `worktree-dependency-provision.py` logs a fixed, path-free reason code instead of the bare `dependency-provision-rejected`.
2. Both restore loops only attempt package directories whose worktree copy contains a supported lockfile (`package-lock.json` or `pnpm-lock.yaml`), the only formats the validator accepts.

## Why

- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` has 24 `dependency-provision-rejected` → `Dependency provisioning unavailable; no external permission granted` pairs in the current window, with no reason. `main()` (`.agents/scripts/worktree-dependency-provision.py:91-99`) discards the specific `Rejected(...)` code, and unexpected errors (for example `FileNotFoundError`) are indistinguishable from policy rejections.
- Local diagnosis with the validator modules shows the attempts cannot succeed:
  - **aidevops:** root `.` fails reading `package-lock.json` because the canonical checkout has a gitignored, stale root `package-lock.json` while the tracked lockfile is `bun.lock`. `packages/gui-web` → `missing-or-ambiguous-supported-lock`.
  - **A managed private pnpm workspace:** every workspace package → `missing-or-ambiguous-supported-lock`, because the lock exists only at the root. The root `node_modules` is about 4.1 GB, against a 64 MB copy budget.
- Each doomed attempt costs about 0.7 s of git and Python work, taken under the global restore lock that concurrent dispatches wait on for up to 2 s. Each one also consumes one of the `WORKTREE_NODE_MODULES_RESTORE_MAX_DIRS` (default 2) slots, which can starve a provisionable directory.
- Out of scope (no failure evidence): pinning the worker Node version. Only pnpm `WARN Unsupported engine` lines appear; there are no `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE`, `NODE_MODULE_VERSION` or `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` failures. Workers are already told to install from the committed lockfile (`.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` step 5).

## How

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-dependency-provision.py`:
  - print `dependency-provision-rejected reason=<code>`;
  - `<code>` is the `Rejected` code when it matches `^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$`, `git-query-failed` for subprocess errors, `os-error-<ERRNO>` for `OSError`, and `invalid-metadata` otherwise;
  - never print paths or exception text.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` (`_dlw_restore_worktree_deps`) and `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh` (`_restore_worktree_node_modules`): require `package-lock.json` or `pnpm-lock.yaml` in the worktree package directory before counting an attempt.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/worktree-dependency-provision.py
- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh
- .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-worker-launch-lock.sh
- TODO.md

## Acceptance

- A malformed lock still yields no raw content: stderr is exactly `dependency-provision-rejected reason=invalid-object-metadata`.
- Package directories without a supported lockfile are not attempted and do not consume the directory budget.
- Directories with a supported lockfile keep today's budget semantics for rejected, mixed and successful provisioning.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-worker-launch-lock.sh`
- `shellcheck` on the changed shell files.

title: fix(pulse): unblock merges wedged by never-reported required checks and private-plan ruleset 403
body:
Target repository: marcusquinn/aidevops

## What

Two merge-pass throughput defects observed in live pulse logs.

### A. Never-reported required checks loop native auto-merge

PR #32756 (head `78f16868`): required contexts `Complexity Analysis`, `ShellCheck (macos-latest)`, `Qlty Regression Gate` and `Framework Validation` never produced runs; GitHub dropped the `opened`-event runs for `code-quality.yml` and `qlty-regression.yml`. `_check_required_checks_passing` (`pulse-merge-process.sh`) counts them as `NOT_FOUND`, and `_set_native_auto_merge_or_skip` treats that as pending. Every cycle therefore re-arms native auto-merge (14 cycles logged), and another runner disarms it about every 30 minutes (12 `AutoMergeDisabledEvent` entries). The existing GH#26899 update-branch remedy in `_pmp_stage_admin_merge` is never reached.

Fix: when required contexts are absent from the exact-head rollup, no check is in flight, and the head commit is older than a threshold, classify them as missing rather than pending. Request one expected-head update-branch to retrigger CI instead of arming native auto-merge, and defer without re-arming.

### B. Private-plan ruleset 403 fails the review-policy gate closed

`_ruleset_required_review_policy_for_default_branch` (`pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`) discards stderr and fails closed on the plan-unsupported 403 (`Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature.`). Rulesets cannot exist on those repos. PR #73 in a private repo was blocked for 18 cycles. The contexts path already treats this 403 as empty (GH#29484); apply the same classification and return 0 approvals required.

## Reproducer

- A: `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/78f16868bd341d2020910b7df479f76996649f32/check-runs` has no `Framework Validation`/`Complexity Analysis`/`ShellCheck (macos-latest)`/`Qlty Regression Gate` runs, while `_required_contexts_for_default_branch marcusquinn/aidevops` lists them. The pulse log shows `4 required context(s) not passing for PR #32756` followed by `native auto-merge set` on every cycle, and the PR timeline shows repeated `AutoMergeDisabledEvent`s.
- B: The pulse log shows `rulesets list failed for <private repo> — caller will fail closed (GH#24577)` 18 times, while the same cycle's contexts path logs `rulesets unavailable ... on the private plan (HTTP 403)`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on edited scripts
- Existing pulse-merge tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/` covering required checks, rulesets and native auto-merge
- Live probe: `_ruleset_required_review_policy_for_default_branch` against a private free-plan repo returns `0<TAB>0`

title: t18537: fix(plugin): retry policy helper once on ETIMEDOUT under host load; label second timeout as transient
body:
## What

Stop blocking worker commands when the OpenCode command-policy hook times out under host load. Retry the policy evaluation once with a larger budget. If that also times out, fail closed with a message that names the block as a transient infrastructure timeout, not a policy decision, and tells the worker to retry the same command.

## Why

- 10 retained September worker failure excerpts contain `BLOCKED: command policy failed closed: spawnSync python3 ETIMEDOUT` (17 occurrences; 8 excerpts on 2026-09-27). Examples: `issue-32682-20260927T234504Z-64283.log` (×4), `issue-10901-20260927T205513Z-14438.log` (×2), `issue-31608-20260908T174728Z-83091.log` (×2).
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-git-safety.mjs:176-204` (`executeCommandPolicy`) and `:141-156` (`checkCanonicalWriteSafetyGate`) run `python3` helpers with a fixed `timeout: 10000`.
- A normal worker network check (`command-policy-helper.py check-command --worker ... --command 'git push origin HEAD'`) takes 2.75 s wall time (0.7 s user, 1.0 s sys) at load average ~23 on 16 cores, because it spawns `network-tier-helper.sh`, `jq` and a second Python process. Peak-load spikes exceed 10 s.
- The current message reads like a policy block. Workers then waste turns on workarounds or abandon the step, even though re-running the same command would be evaluated normally.

## How

`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-git-safety.mjs`:

- One shared `python3` policy-helper runner for both hooks:
  - base timeout from `AIDEVOPS_POLICY_HELPER_TIMEOUT_MS` (positive integer, default 10000), read at call time;
  - on `ETIMEDOUT` only, retry once at 3× the base.
- A second timeout still throws (fail closed) with a distinct message: `BLOCKED: command policy timed out under host load (transient infrastructure timeout, not a policy decision); retry the same command`, plus the canonical-write equivalent.
- Non-timeout failures, nonzero exits with allow payloads and malformed output keep today's fail-closed behaviour and messages.

### Files Scope

- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-git-safety.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs
- TODO.md

## Acceptance

- A policy helper that times out once and then answers `allow` lets the command run.
- A helper that always times out still blocks, with the transient-timeout message.
- The existing fail-closed tests (missing helper, malformed policy, nonzero exit with an allow payload) still pass unchanged.

## Verification

`node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`

title: pulse: prune expired GitHub read caches (21k stale files, unbounded growth)
body:
## What

The persistent GitHub read caches under `~/.aidevops/cache/` grow without bound. On one pulse host (2026-09-29), 20,970 of 23,843 cache files were older than 7 days: `pulse-pr-view-cache` 9,448, `gh-pr-list-snapshots` 4,917, `gh-pr-check-status` 4,123 (99 MB total). No code prunes these directories. Every entry older than its maximum TTL is dead weight: PR view/list default TTL is 3600s, and check-status terminal TTL is at most 7 days (`_gh_pr_check_status_cache_ttl`). `gh_pr_list_cache_invalidate_repo` also globs the whole snapshot directory on every merge/close, so its cost grows with the backlog.

## How

- Add a bounded prune, reusing the pulse's existing scheduled cleanup stage (model on `cleanup_stale_opencode` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`, which calls `system-cleanup.sh` with a time budget). Delete regular files (not symlinks) older than 8 days, safely beyond the 7-day maximum TTL, in exactly these directories: `pulse-pr-view-cache`, `gh-pr-list-snapshots`, `gh-pr-check-status`, `gh-pr-view-snapshots`. Respect their env overrides (`AIDEVOPS_GH_PR_VIEW_CACHE_DIR` / `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_PR_VIEW_CACHE_DIR`, `AIDEVOPS_GH_PR_LIST_CACHE_DIR`, `AIDEVOPS_GH_CHECK_STATUS_CACHE_DIR`).
- These are private disposable caches, so direct `find -type f -mtime +8 -delete` is appropriate (no trash). Keep a time budget and log one summary line: dirs, deleted count, elapsed.
- Never touch `auto-dispatch-locks`, `bundle`, or any lock/lease files.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] A pulse cycle removes cache files older than 8 days from the four named cache dirs only, within a bounded time budget.
- [ ] Fresh entries (younger than 8 days) and non-cache dirs are untouched.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`
- Manual: create an old file with `touch -t` in a temp `AIDEVOPS_GH_CHECK_STATUS_CACHE_DIR`, run the stage function, and confirm only the old file is removed.
